A two-structure, five-valve scenario compares it against a fixed-loop A-star tour under matched time budgets.

entry.title: Position: Profiling Game Worlds by Transition Complexity

author.name: Lele Cao

entry.summary: Proposes the Transition Complexity Profile, a small reproducible metric suite that quantifies how hard the next-state prediction problem is in a game environment at a declared observation interface, covering branching factor, opponent-induced uncertainty, and temporal dependency span. The goal is to stop world-modeling and RL papers from conflating environment difficulty with method quality.

entry.title: Large Language Models in Mental Health: A Systematic Review of Applications, Innovations, and Ethical Challenges

author.name: Yisong Chen, Yifan Gao, Sijing Yu, Chuqing Zhao, Yang Lu

entry.summary: A systematic review of LLM applications across mental health, spanning social media screening for depression and suicide risk, clinical conversational agents, therapy support, prompt engineering for domain adaptation, and multimodal inputs. It also catalogs interpretability and ethical concerns for clinical deployment.

entry.title: ORBITER: Conflict-Aware Decision-Making for Agentic Last-Mile Delivery

author.name: Mingzhao Li, Chenxi Liu, Yan Zhao, Hao Miao

entry.summary: ORBITER is an agentic arbiter for next-order decisions in last-mile delivery that describes the current delivery state in language so an LLM can reason explicitly about spatial, temporal, and behavioral cues, while addressing LLM sensitivity to task presentation through a conflict-aware arbitration structure rather than direct prediction.

entry.title: The Deontic Gap: Large Language Models and the Modal Language of Obligation

author.name: Daniel Hart, Sarah Allred, Joseph Abbas, Morenike Alugo

entry.summary: Compares how LLM-generated text uses obligation modals such as must and should against contemporary human corpora and a century of published prose. AI output consistently underuses positive deontic modals, patterning like formal published English rather than current speech.

entry.title: Formal Verification of Romanov's Triplet Logic: A Verified Filter for Sliding-window 3-CNF with Application to Structured Formulas

author.name: Dmitry V. Alexandrov

entry.summary: Provides the first machine-checked formalization of a triplet-based combinatorial framework for reasoning about satisfiability structures, verifying a clause-by-clause translation and an intersection procedure in a proof assistant. The verified component functions as a sound filter for a restricted class of formulas.

entry.title: Performance Drift Detection in Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS) for IoT Environments

author.name: Deepak Kanneganti, Sajib Mistry, Sheik Mohammad Mostakim Fattah, Erik Elmroth, Aneesh Krishna, Monowar Bhuyan

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for detecting performance drift in cloud machine learning services from the client side, where users cannot inspect the provider model, by learning a surrogate of the service behavior. It targets IoT settings where both data distributions and provider models change over time.

entry.title: A Two-Stage Time-Aware Transformer for Short-Horizon AECOPD Risk Prediction

author.name: Dongyang Wang, Weihao Qu, Ling Zheng, Haowen Pan

entry.summary: Presents a two-stage time-aware transformer that predicts short-horizon risk of COPD exacerbation directly from raw pressure and flow waveforms recorded by home ventilators, rather than from episodic clinical variables or handcrafted features. It also aims to estimate the timing of an impending event instead of only binary risk.

entry.title: Rationally Enriched Chebyshev Trunk Bases for DeepONet Surrogates of High P\'eclet Entrance Transport

author.name: Mingeun Choi, Satish Kumar

entry.summary: Enriches the trunk basis of a DeepONet operator surrogate with rational functions built via the adaptive AAA algorithm alongside Chebyshev polynomials, targeting singularly perturbed high-Peclet transport problems with thin boundary layers. Over repeated training runs it outperforms vanilla and Chebyshev-only trunk variants on three benchmark problems.

entry.title: An Inclusive and Lightweight Approach to Federated Continual Learning for Cultural Heritage

author.name: Ioannis Theologitis, Debin Meng, Stylianos Eleftheriadis, Vasileios Lolis, Konstantinos Votis

entry.summary: Proposes FedCurv-DR, a lightweight regularization-based federated continual learning method for cultural heritage collections that are distributed across institutions and continuously growing. Parameter-importance estimates are accumulated across clients and updated only periodically to reduce communication cost.

entry.title: A comparison between ceiling-mounted FMCW, IR-UWB and Wi-Fi radar for in-bedroom human activity monitoring and sleep interruption detection

author.name: Anton Lambrecht, Reda El Hail, Xianjun Jiao, Pieter Crombez, Dominique Schreurs, Peter Karsmakers, Adnan Shahid, Eli De Poorter

entry.summary: Provides a controlled head-to-head comparison of ceiling-mounted FMCW radar, impulse-radio ultra-wideband, and Wi-Fi sensing for bedroom activity monitoring and sleep interruption detection, using synchronized recordings from 20 participants across six room layouts. It fills a gap where prior studies used incomparable hardware and protocols.

entry.title: Reward-Guided Autoregressive Graph Generation for Efficient Multi-Agent Communication Topology Design

author.name: Poomphob Suwannapichat, Boonyarit Changaival, Caesar Wu, Pascal Bouvry

entry.summary: Proposes RGA-Designer, which adds a reward model capturing both task correctness and structural sparsity to an autoregressive graph generator that designs communication topologies for LLM multi-agent systems. The fine-tuning stage is RLHF-inspired, aiming to cut token consumption while keeping reasoning accuracy. It matters because multi-agent orchestration costs scale with edges in the communication graph.

entry.title: StreamSoccer: Event-Driven Memory for Streaming Soccer Commentary

author.name: Chenxi Shao, Bozhong Wang, Jiaxin Huang, Zhao Liu, Sunwei Zhu, Tianxin Hang, Gaoqi He, Yang Li, Changbo Wang

entry.summary: StreamSoccer generates live soccer commentary from streaming video using event memory as its intermediate representation, with a fixed-budget active memory that integrates the stream and consolidates completed events into retrievable historical records. A unified generator draws on current, recent and historical states and can also choose to stay silent. It is a concrete instance of bounded-memory streaming video understanding.

entry.title: S$^2$GS: Structured Sparse Gaussian Streaming for Efficient Free-Viewpoint Video Reconstruction on Edge-IoT Devices

author.name: Yiwei Li, Jiannong Cao, Weixun Gao, Rui Cao, Songye Zhu, Yinfeng Cao, Mingjin Zhang

entry.summary: S2GS streams free-viewpoint video reconstruction by exploiting structured temporal sparsity, updating only Gaussian residuals organized in a streaming octree to cut per-frame optimization time and storage. The target is deployment on constrained edge and IoT devices for telepresence and digital twins.

entry.title: Prompt-Conditioned Channel Attention for Hierarchical Feature Modulation toward Anatomy-Agnostic Segmentation

author.name: Mosharof Hossain, Md Rabiul Islam, Limon Halder, Erchin Serpedin, Md Kamrul Hasan

entry.summary: Prompt-Conditioned Channel Attention injects semantic prompts deep into a segmentation network by modulating channels across hierarchical feature levels, rather than fusing prompts only late in the pipeline. The claim is anatomy-agnostic interactive segmentation that better handles ambiguous boundaries and modality artifacts.

entry.title: Multimodal Trajectory Planning for Surface Vehicles using Turning Circle-based Control Barrier Functions

author.name: Changyu Lee

entry.summary: Combines model predictive control with a turning-circle-based control barrier function for autonomous surface vessels, replacing purely proximity-based safety with a geometry that respects nonholonomic motion and finite turning radius. The formulation exposes distinct left- and right-turn avoidance modes so the solver can explore topologically different trajectories.

entry.title: Measuring the Partial-Credit Gap: A Strict Benchmark on Vietnam's 2025 Convex Marking Scheme

author.name: Nguyen Quoc Hung, Nguyen Dang Minh, Le Nhu Quynh, Tran Khanh Linh, Nguyen Kieu Linh

entry.summary: Argues that binary right-or-wrong scoring misrepresents model ability when the underlying exam uses a non-additive grading scheme, using Vietnam's reformed national high school exam where four true-false statements earn convex partial credit. Getting three of four correct earns half a point rather than the three quarters standard accuracy would imply, creating a measurable gap between reported accuracy and actual exam score.

entry.title: Bridging Search and CRM: Productionizing AI Product Research Agents for Customer Re-Engagement

author.name: Mandar Kulkarni, Pooja A., Samir Shah

entry.summary: Describes a deployed e-commerce system that connects search intent signals with CRM re-engagement by detecting users with exploratory purchase intent, running multi-agent grounded product research over behavioral signals, external knowledge, and catalog data, and delivering personalized recommendations through a messaging channel.

entry.title: Impact of Iterative Fine-Tuning on Transcription Accuracy in Complex Historical Sanskrit Manuscripts

author.name: Kartik Chincholikar, Kaushik Gopalan, Mihir Hasabnis

entry.summary: Shows that iteratively fine-tuning a classical OCR pipeline at both layout and appearance levels on the target manuscript progressively improves transcription of complex historical Sanskrit documents. The loop adapts to period-specific handwriting, page texture and imaging noise.

entry.title: GrabVG: Graph-Attentive Binding for Visual Grounding in UAV Imagery

author.name: Chaowei Wang, Yan Di, Jingjun Sun, Baozhe Liu, Jiaxu Tian, Yuheng Li, Guangqian Guo, Shan Gao

entry.summary: GrabVG improves language-guided object localization in drone imagery by adding graph-attentive binding that exploits spatial topology among many small, visually similar objects. It targets failures caused by visual redundancy and repeated local configurations in bird's-eye-view scenes.

entry.title: Recovering Nonlinear Functions of Latent Variables: A Plausible-Value Neural Network Framework

author.name: Eunjeong Song (Department of Education, Korea University, Seoul, Republic of Korea), Sehee Hong (Department of Education, Korea University, Seoul, Republic of Korea)

entry.summary: Derives an attenuation bound showing that measurement error shrinks the recoverable variance of the kth-order component of a nonlinear regression on latent variables by the kth power of the score reliability. It proposes combining plausible-value posterior draws with neural networks to recover latent-scale nonlinear functions without prespecifying functional form.

entry.title: HiRA-CAM: Preserving Fine-Grained Spatial Relevance in Gradient-Based Visual Explanations

author.name: Manasi Nerurkar, Ali A. Minai

entry.summary: HiRA-CAM improves gradient-based saliency maps for convolutional networks by adaptively combining activation maps from all layers rather than a single chosen layer. The authors report sharper and more focused explanations than LayerCAM and Grad-CAM for object classification.

entry.title: PL-NBA: A Possession-level Universal Basketball Video Dataset Supporting Multiple Visual Understanding Tasks

author.name: Yunhao Zhao, Haoying Sun, Jiarui Li, Zhuming Wang, Ya Jing, Xiangbo Shu, Lifang Wu, Changwen Chen

entry.summary: PL-NBA is a basketball video dataset annotated at the level of full offensive possessions, with 11,000 clips and over 31,000 events labeled with players, captions, types, and timestamps from 60 NBA games. Possession-level continuity enables tasks such as event anticipation that single-action datasets cannot support.

entry.title: When Saying No Makes Better Videos: Designing Dual Gatekeeping for Pedagogically Grounded AI Content Creation

author.name: Yearim Kim, Njun Baek, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: Studies an AI video authoring pipeline with two layers of deliberate refusal: educators iteratively reshape scripts against multimedia learning theory, and automated metrics flag violations of instructional coherence and narrative-visual synchronization. A study with 23 educators plus automated evaluation suggests principled refusal improves pedagogical quality.

entry.title: Coupled-cluster molecular properties across the main group that extrapolate beyond training size

author.name: Wenhao He, Xu Chen, Noah Song, Haowei Xu, Tim S. Hindges, Bohan Li, Zihan Lin, Yu Yao, Avetik R. Harutyunyan, Fang Liu, Yao Wang, Hao Tang, Ju Li

entry.summary: Covered in yesterday's Research roundup, Trains an equivariant network to predict an effective one-electron Hamiltonian from a single cheap density-functional calculation, then derives energies, gaps, dipoles, polarizabilities and bond orders at coupled-cluster accuracy across nine main-group elements. The model reportedly generalizes to molecules larger than those in training.

entry.title: RDFdL: Integrating RDF with Differential Dynamic Logic

author.name: Yuyang Li, Lukas Kubelka, Julia Butte, Tobias K\"afer

entry.summary: RDFdL extends RDF knowledge graphs with differential dynamic logic so that continuous physical dynamics described by differential equations can be represented alongside static knowledge and verified. Differential equations and state-space ranges are encoded in RDF and SHACL with semantics given by translation to dL.

entry.title: When Clean Signals Are Not Enough: Detecting Structural Ambiguity for Safe Wearable Stress Classification

author.name: Saba A. Farahani, Hung Cao, Amir M. Rahmani

entry.summary: Identifies structural ambiguity in wearable stress detection, where a classifier with 93 percent mean accuracy completely fails for individual subjects whose cross-signal physiological coupling breaks down near stress onset. The proposed monitor quantifies subject-specific coupling divergence before inference and routes each window to classify, defer, or abstain without retraining the downstream model.

entry.title: Training-Free Inference-Time Self-Reflection and Cost-Bounded Early Stopping for Large Language Models

author.name: Wei Yu, Suxing Liu, Minjie Yu, Jiahao Wang, Zhijian Zheng, Haocheng Deng, Bing Li

entry.summary: EvoResearcher is a training-free inference-time protocol that loops generation, self-critique, and revision on a single frozen model until a maximum depth or a confirmation sentinel triggers early stopping, keeping compute bounded. Four self-reflective reward components covering correctness, efficiency, reflection depth, and tool-call diversity are instantiated as prompt-level mechanisms rather than RL objectives.

entry.title: Adaptive Memory and Reflection Multi-Agent System for Medical Question Answering

author.name: Pradeep Murugesan, Luoxiao Yang, Xueli Chen, Xinqi Fan

entry.summary: Proposes a medical question answering system where specialized agents share persistent memory and reflection-based feedback, retrieving relevant prior cases to inform reasoning. A complexity assessment router sends questions through solo, collaborative, or escalated workflows, with consensus and ethical oversight modules applied before output.

entry.title: Intercepting the Kangaroo: Experimental Astrolinguistics with Constructed Lexicons, Active Probing, and Large Language Models as Informants and Hypothesis Proposers

author.name: Francesco Cordella, Mauro Cappelli

entry.summary: Turns speculative astrolinguistics into a simulation testbed by giving two language models deliberately incompatible constructed lexicons and having a scripted orchestrator attempt translation, with full ground truth available. The paper names and studies the kangaroo effect, where a word silently attaches to the wrong referent, across hundreds of runs.

entry.title: Empirical Characterization of Learning Geometry in Hybrid Quantum Forecasting Models

author.name: Sandra Leticia Ju\'arez-Osorio, Jorge I. Hernandez-Martinez, Jesus Ivan Ruiz-Martinez, Andres Mendez-Vazquez, Eduardo Rodriguez-Tello

entry.summary: Compares the empirical neural tangent kernel dynamics of a compact hybrid quantum forecasting model against a structurally matched classical baseline on harmonic-mixture and chirp benchmarks, tracking kernel-target alignment, kernel drift, and spectral concentration. Despite different optimization geometries, held-out performance is similar.

entry.title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection Using Flow Matching on Tabular Data

author.name: Philip Konz, Tejaswini Medi, Margret Keuper

entry.summary: Studies flow-matching-based unsupervised anomaly detection on tabular financial data when the training set is already contaminated with anomalies, comparing time-conditioned contraction matching against a forest-flow variant across several scoring functions. The main finding is that the choice of anomaly score dominates, with the original single-step decision score underperforming.

entry.title: Reliable Financial Named Entity Recognition under Domain Shift

author.name: Zihao Zheng, Baichuan Li, Junyi Yao, Jiayu Long

entry.summary: Studies confidence estimation and selective prediction for financial named entity recognition across a three-tier distribution shift from SEC filings to financial news to general social media, comparing a BERT tagger with LoRA-tuned small Qwen models under five inference-time confidence signals. A key finding is that the ranking of confidence signals itself changes under shift, so F1 alone does not indicate what is safe to automate. It targets deployment risk in financial information extraction.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration with the Common-Sense Reasoning Capabilities of LLMs for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Mehdi Azarafza, Faezeh Pasandideh, Ali Ehteshami Bejnordi, Stefan Henkler, Achim Rettberg

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid autonomous-driving stack in which an orchestrator coordinates PPO-trained reinforcement learning and PID control while LLM common-sense reasoning is applied only at a supervisory level, avoiding direct vehicle control. The design is motivated by LLM latency and hallucination risks that make direct actuation unsafe. It illustrates a layered pattern for embedding LLM reasoning in safety-critical control.

entry.title: Robust Cross-Modal Foundation Model Perception for Underwater Robots under Degraded Visual Conditions

author.name: Mohammad Arif Ul Alam

entry.summary: Evaluates whether frozen DINOv2 visual features can be complemented by sonar for underwater robot perception as optical quality degrades, using a controlled five-level degradation benchmark. The framing shifts attention from nominal detection accuracy to cross-modal robustness curves.

entry.title: A 360-Degree Vision Dataset for Learning Yaw Control on GPS-Denied Micro-UAVs in Disaster-Response-Relevant Environments

author.name: Niklas Voigt, Hartmut Surmann

entry.summary: Presents a 360-degree camera dataset from industrial, underground, and training environments recorded by a custom micro-drone, used to learn a yaw controller that steers toward open space when radio links fail in GPS-denied settings. The application focus is disaster and CBRN emergency response.

entry.title: PVRA: A Pointwise Key-point Voting Framework for Robotic Assembly

author.name: Kulunu Samarawickrama, Roel Pieters

entry.summary: PVRA is a modular 3D keypoint voting framework that learns assembly dependencies from RGB-D scenes to output actionable next-step information rather than only object poses. The authors argue object-centric perception alone is insufficient for autonomous progressive assembly.

entry.title: Petri Net Description of Biological Neural Circuits for Fast Hardware Prototyping

author.name: Carlo daCunha, Rodrigo Pena, Marcos Turqueti

entry.summary: Proposes describing biological neural circuits as timed Petri nets so that neurons, synapses, and spikes have formally verifiable timing semantics, enabling deadline-guaranteed real-time hardware execution independent of integration timestep. It claims analytic correspondence to leaky integrate-and-fire dynamics.

entry.title: FM-Bench: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Management with Competing Agents

author.name: Tianyou Wang, Chongyang Gao, Kezhen Chen, Chen Dong, Yinghao He, Donghan Li, Wangcheng Xu, Hongjiu Zhang, Chi Li

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.18423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language model agents now execute bounded tasks reliably. Whether they can sustain effective decision-making over long horizons, where actions have cum...

entry.title: Syntactic Simplification of OWL Class Expressions

author.name: Alkid Baci, N'Dah Jean Kouagou, Caglar Demir, Axel-Cyrille Ngonga Ngomo

entry.summary: Presents an algorithm for syntactically simplifying OWL class expressions produced by class expression learning, applying rewriting rules to remove redundancy and find shorter equivalent forms while preserving logical entailments. The result is more compact and human-readable descriptions for description logic knowledge bases.

entry.title: DeepTCM1.0: A Multi-Expert AI Agent for Deciphering Mechanisms of Chinese Herbal Formulae Based on General Large Language Models

author.name: Wenxin Duan, Hanwei Wang, Zhongying Peng, Zhonghua Lu, Jiayi An, Fan Song, Yong Liang

entry.summary: Presents a multi-expert LLM agent system that decomposes analysis of traditional Chinese medicine formulas across specialist roles to reduce hallucinated mechanistic reasoning. It targets the gap between classical TCM theory and network pharmacology style evidence.

entry.title: StocksTalk: A Voice-Enabled Conversational Agent for Structured Query Generation over Web Data

author.name: Akshat Parmar, Vikranth Udandarao, Abhay Shakya, Tanmay Hire, Avinash Anand, Rajiv Ratn Shah, Daniel Wang Zhengkui

entry.summary: A voice-driven system that converts spoken stock-screening requests into validated SQL over market data, exposing intermediate artifacts such as extracted constraints and normalized metrics for user inspection. It is evaluated on a curated benchmark of 150 spoken queries.

entry.title: How Quantum Is the Advantage? A Fair, Calibration- and Noise-Aware Benchmark and Attribution Audit of Quantum Machine Learning for Network Intrusion Detection

author.name: Syeda Anshrah Gillani, Mirza Samad Ahmed Baig, Shahid Munir Shah, Asher Ali, Hamzah Siddiqui

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.18155v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) for network intrusion detection (NIDS) is routinely reported to reach near-perfect accuracy, yet the most rigorous stu...

entry.title: When Do LLMs Actually Help? Evaluating LLMs as Data Quality Annotators

author.name: Praphulla Lal Shrestha

entry.summary: Tests whether an LLM reliably flags data quality problems in e-commerce entity matching and brand mislabeling against rule-based baselines and human labels. Simple rules match zero-shot LLM performance, and a few-shot prompt that looked better on a small validation sample degraded full-scale results.

entry.title: Visual-Prompt Guided Wildlife Instance-Level Recognition

author.name: Mufhumudzi Muthivhi, Jiahao Huo, Terence van Zyl, Fredrik Gustafsson

entry.summary: Proposes a single-stage detection plus re-identification model for wildlife individuals that searches identities directly in latent space using a self-supervised vision backbone and wildlife descriptors. Preliminary accuracy remains well below the two-stage state of the art.

entry.title: Finetuning Strategies for Querying Sounds by Vocal Imitation

author.name: Aditya Bhattacharjee, Christos Plachouras, Sungkyun Chang, Emmanouil Benetos

entry.summary: A technical report on the winning entry to a 2025 challenge for retrieving sound effects from vocal imitations, comparing contrastive learning on a frozen pretrained audio encoder against joint contrastive-triplet training with semi-hard negatives on a lightweight encoder. It documents fine-tuning choices that mattered for the task.

entry.title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments

author.name: Bo Liu, Simon Yu, Yiding Jiang, Ao Qu, Andrew Zhao, Zichen Liu, Junsu Kim, Zijian Zhou, Seungone Kim, Tongzheng Ren, Mickel Liu, Hanfei Yu, Zhaorun Chen, Weiyan Shi, Paul Pu Liang, Luke Zettlemoyer, Yejin Choi, Natasha Jaques

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.19197v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continuous self-improvement requires an ever-expanding pool of self-generated, diverse, adaptive goals. For language agents, existing training enviro...

entry.title: Beyond Multimodal Alignment: Certifying Physical Language through Response Substitution and Ordered Execution

author.name: Kaizhen Tan, Xin Xu, Siru Tao, Yixiao Li, Hanzhe Hong, Yang Feng, Heqing Du

entry.summary: Proposes a capability hierarchy and a certificate procedure to test whether representations from different sensors carry interchangeable executable meaning when substituted into a frozen response model, and whether that meaning survives new action compositions. Experiments on haptic clustering show audio and acceleration representations of the same unseen surface land far closer in response space than mismatched pairings.

entry.title: Exact Algebraic Computation of Learning Coefficients for Two-Dimensional Singular Models

author.name: Gr\'egoire Sergeant-Perthuis (CQSB, Sorbonne Universit\'e), Elias Tsigaridas (Ouragan Team, INRIA), Jules Tsukahara (Ouragan Team, INRIA)

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.20183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical information criteria such as the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) rely on regularity assumptions that break down for singular models, lea...

entry.title: VQC-ZTI: Variational Quantum Control for Zero Trust Protection of the Tactile Internet

author.name: Mubassir Serneabat Sudipto (Iowa State University), Shakil Ahmed (Grand Valley State University), Ashfaq Khokhar (Kansas State University)

entry.summary: Proposes a split-plane zero-trust security architecture for tactile internet services in which a variational quantum classifier scores encrypted-flow telemetry off the control path while a conventional policy engine enforces cached decisions. The design decouples anomaly detection sensitivity from enforcement aggressiveness.

entry.title: A Repeated Measurements Approach to $SoH$ Battery Modelling of Cyclic Aged Data in a Laboratory Environment

author.name: Mark Cary, Charles Bokor

entry.summary: Applies a linearized nonlinear repeated-measurements model to battery state-of-health ageing profiles from laboratory cycling, separating within-profile measurement noise from cell-to-cell variation. It uses regularized iterative generalized least squares with hyperparameter re-estimation on ten cells.

entry.title: The impact of feature engineering and an optimisation framework for ocean colour machine learning

author.name: Edson Silva, Julien Brajard, Simon Cappe, Lasse H. Pettersson, Fran\c{c}ois Counillon

entry.summary: Assesses how feature engineering, rather than model or hyperparameter tuning, affects ocean colour retrieval models, proposing a seven-level sequence of data transformations from band selection through scaling. It demonstrates the framework with multilayer perceptrons, support vector machines, and gradient-boosted trees on satellite data.

entry.title: Gravitational-wave parameter estimation with machine-learning generated surrogate waveforms

author.name: Suyog Garg, Kipp Cannon

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage deterministic machine-learning surrogate for generating gravitational-wave templates to accelerate likelihood evaluation in parameter estimation. The motivation is that third-generation detectors such as Einstein Telescope will produce far more and more complex signals than current pipelines can afford to analyze. It is applied ML for a compute-bound scientific inference problem.

entry.title: GRACE: Grounded Reasoning via Adapter Composition and Evidence-Aware Calibration for Educational Visual Question Answering

author.name: Xinjin Li, Yudi Xia, Xi Zhao, Yiliu Xu, Yining Liu, Cheng Lu, Yujian Long, Yu Ma, Jinghan Cao, Liang Fan, Yeyun Xu

entry.summary: GRACE adapts a frozen multimodal LLM for curriculum-oriented multiple-choice visual question answering using pedagogically conditioned adapter composition and evidence-aware calibration, aiming to suppress question-option shortcuts. It is parameter-efficient and targeted at structured educational assessment data.

entry.title: Magnetically Self-Sealed MR Haptic Actuator With PWM-Based Excitation and High-Fidelity Torque Control

author.name: Dong Qiang, Tian Yuan, Song Yang, Kequan Xia, Thomas Reddyhoff, Yikun Zhang, Cheng Cheng, Min Yu

entry.summary: Presents an integrated magnetorheological haptic actuator with magnetic self-sealing, low-hysteresis PWM excitation, and model-based torque rendering validated for long-duration stability. Magnetostatic simulation guides material layout to focus flux in the multidisk torque region.

entry.title: Towards Professional Tennis Styles for Humanoid Robots with Adaptive Motion Planning and Tracking

author.name: Tao Huang, Ruofei Liu, Xuchen Tang, Xinyin Zhang, Junli Ren, Huayi Wang, Feiyu Jia, Yukai Qi, Kangning Yin, Weishuai Zeng, Lipeng Chen, Xi Li, Ting Wu, Kailin Li, Ruoli Dai, Jingbo Wang, Lei Han, Jiangmiao Pang

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.20087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Humanoid robots have recently demonstrated promising capabilities in real-world ball sports. However, achieving professional motion styles while mainta...

entry.title: Towards general embodied intelligence: integrating large language models, knowledge bases, and reasoning capabilities to build the next generation of AI agents

author.name: Fujiang Yuan, Xia Huang, Lusheng Wang, Jun Ding, Zhen Tian, Yuxin Wang, Shaojie Gu, Yuki Funabora, Yanhong Peng, Zebing Mao

entry.summary: A review arguing that combining large language models, structured knowledge bases, and explicit reasoning modules is a path toward general embodied intelligence, surveying LLM architectures, pretraining, inference, knowledge integration, and embodied learning paradigms. It ends with a conceptual framework tying these strands together.

entry.title: Appearing Unfair in the Wrong Direction

author.name: MossyFallenFriend

entry.summary: A pedagogical post on a statistical trap in classification fairness, showing with a two-group hiring parable that when base rates differ, the same process can simultaneously look biased in favor of the disadvantaged group by one metric and against it by another. It illustrates the incompatibility of common fairness criteria.

entry.title: Grouping the Stochastic Machine: Precision, Not Capability, as the Frontier Metric for AI Systems

author.name: George Andrikopoulos

entry.summary: Argues that frontier model comparison should shift from capability, meaning where the average output lands, to precision, meaning how tightly outputs cluster across repeated identical requests. The author contends benchmark culture reports central tendency while ignoring spread, and that variance is now the practical differentiator between deployed systems.

entry.title: SABET-QA: Temporal Knowledge Graph Question Answering

author.name: Brahim Touayouch, Mirette Moawad, Dmitry Akulov

entry.summary: SABET-QA tackles question answering over temporal knowledge graphs with iterative multi-hop state refinement, a bidirectional entity-temporal scoring mechanism, slot-aware alignment of question semantics with temporal embeddings, and differentiable working memory. It reports consistent gains over strong baselines on four temporal QA datasets. The motivation is that single-pass embedding pipelines fail on multi-step temporal queries.

entry.title: The Verification Gap in Networked Physical AI: A Post-Semantic Communication Framework

author.name: Shunsuke Saruwatari

entry.summary: Introduces the notion of a verification gap in networked physical AI: an action proposal may be semantically understood while the timely evidence or authority needed to justify execution is missing. The proposed post-semantic communication framework separates evidence sufficiency from authorized finalization with a downstream runtime gate.

entry.title: Efficient Adaptation of LLMs for Hate Speech Detection in Low-Resource Languages: A Comparative Study on Roman Urdu

author.name: Toneema Zubair, Muhammad Junaid Asif, Faisal Kamiran, Hafiz Hassan Saeed, Rana Fayyaz Ahmad

entry.summary: A comparative study of zero-shot versus LoRA-adapted transformer and LLM performance for hate speech detection in Roman Urdu, a low-resource script with highly inconsistent spelling conventions. The work benchmarks several models and quantifies gains from parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

entry.title: Pairwise Logical Selection of Enthymeme Completions under Semantic-Link Uncertainty

author.name: Xuyao Feng, Antonis Bikakis

entry.summary: Studies pairwise selection between two candidate completions for a missing premise or claim in an enthymematic argument, extending a neuro-symbolic pipeline from missing premises to missing claims and replacing binary entailment outcomes with graded logical-resistance scores. It introduces a possible-worlds atom-link formalization that keeps semantic-link uncertainty explicit.

entry.title: Computational Orientalism: Measuring Structural Discourse Bias in Large Language Models Using the Middle East Cultural Sensitivity Score (MECSS)

author.name: Maha Shahid

entry.summary: Proposes a Middle East Cultural Sensitivity Score that operationalizes Said's concept of Orientalism as a measurable property of LLM discourse, targeting structural framing (agency denial, treating Western frames as neutral) rather than explicit slurs. It argues standard fairness metrics miss this class of representational harm.

entry.title: Pedagogical AI in Mental Health: A Tri-Stream Fine-Tuned LLM Framework for Automated Clinical Supervision and Risk Triage

author.name: Shreeya Sharma, Ravish Gupta, Saket Kumar, Abhishek Aggarwal

entry.summary: Fine-tunes a 7B model to act as an automated supervisor for novice therapists, scoring therapeutic alliance, predicting latent risk and triaging urgency from clinical interview recordings. Reported technique identification accuracy is high but derived from about a hundred sessions.

entry.title: Flama: a Python framework for development and deployment of production-ready APIs, machine learning, and LLM services

author.name: Jos\'e A. Perdiguero L\'opez, Miguel A. Dur\'an-Olivencia

entry.summary: Describes an open-source asynchronous Python framework unifying REST API development, predictive model serving and generative AI inference behind a type-driven dependency injection system. It includes automatic CRUD generation and pluggable schema adapters.

entry.title: $TCP_\alpha$: Margin-Controlled Confidence estimation for reliable Music Information Retrieval

author.name: Parampreet Singh, Anushka Singh, Sumit Kumar, Vipul Arora

entry.summary: Introduces a confidence target for post-hoc estimation heads that adds a margin-controlled penalty on misclassified samples, aiming to separate confidence distributions of correct and incorrect predictions near decision boundaries. The method is validated in music information retrieval tasks with accompanying theoretical claims. It addresses the practical need for trustworthy abstention signals over frozen classifiers.

entry.title: Calming Robot Pitches? Exploring the Influence of Robot Voice Pitch on Children's Stress Levels

author.name: Nina G. M. van Roij, Emilia I. Barakova, Briana Isaila, Aoju Chen

entry.summary: A small randomized study of 27 Dutch children found that whether a social robot spoke with a lower or higher pitched voice made no measurable difference to self-reported stress during a timed LEGO-building game, even though the task itself reliably raised stress. The result challenges the assumption that human vocal-pitch effects transfer to synthetic robot voices.

entry.title: Notes on "EigenBench: A Comparative Behavioral Measure of Value Alignment"

author.name: Shunk

entry.summary: Study notes summarizing EigenBench, a comparative behavioral benchmark that scores models on value alignment against a written constitution by having models judge each other. The post is an explicit learning exercise by a newcomer aiming to build a habit of public paper notes.

entry.title: A Speech Corpus for Mizo Automatic Speech Recognition: Whisper and SraVaani 1.0 Fine-Tuning with Morphology-Aware Evaluation

author.name: Priyankoo Sarmah, Sanasam Ranbir Singh, Lalhmingmawia

entry.summary: Builds a 17.6-hour Mizo speech corpus and fine-tunes Whisper variants plus an Indic multilingual model, reporting large gaps between conventional and morphology-aware word error rates (for example 18.1 percent versus 7.2 percent for the best system). The morphology-aware evaluation argues that standard WER overstates errors for agglutinative languages. It provides both data and an evaluation critique for a low-resource language.

entry.title: Natural Language Code Retrieval for 1C:Enterprise: An Open Benchmark and Efficient Bi-Encoder

author.name: Konstantin Chesnokov, Chingiz Mingazov

entry.summary: Delivers an open benchmark of 3,413 PII-scrubbed query-code pairs for the Russian-language 1C:Enterprise ecosystem plus a specialized bi-encoder trained on 784k synthetic triplets generated by an existing open Gemma-4 variant, using Matryoshka representation learning and a privacy-aware tokenizer. It fills a total gap in resources for a widely used but underserved enterprise programming ecosystem. Balanced-subset metrics are reported to handle uneven subsets.

entry.title: Towards Clinically Faithful Medical Image Captioning via Enhanced Vision-Language Alignment

author.name: Yunseo Lee, Hyun Jun Kim, Heeseung Shin, Changwon Lim

entry.summary: Proposes a medical image captioning framework that separates and strengthens training-time and inference-time alignment with clinical concept spaces, arguing that fluent captions from large vision-language models do not guarantee clinical faithfulness. The pipeline targets grayscale modalities, subtle anatomical cues and specialized phrasing. It aims at interpretable, diagnostically usable captions.

entry.title: Beyond Recognition: Compact Multi-Domain Arabic Manuscript HTR with Candidate-Selection Analysis and Evidence-Preserving Review

author.name: Abdullah Ahmed Ali, Mohammed Thamer Abdulhadi, Ali Haider Safaa, Dhulfiqar Mahdi Wadi

entry.summary: Presents Phoenix, a compact 5M-parameter CNN-BiLSTM-CTC recognizer adapted across archival, Maghrebi and historical Arabic manuscript domains using document-aware replay, an expanded 81-symbol codec and forgetting guards that reject checkpoints harming earlier domains, plus Athar, an evidence-preserving review workflow. The system separates visual evidence from linguistic plausibility and records the researcher's final decision. It targets scholarly usability rather than raw recognition accuracy.

entry.title: GenEx: A Graph-Based Representational Paradigm for SARS-CoV-2 Variant Detection via Codon Co-occurrence Networks

author.name: Arefin Amin, Labiba Faiza Karim, M. Monir Uddin

entry.summary: GenEx converts viral gene sequences into codon co-occurrence graphs and extracts over 25 graph-level features for SARS-CoV-2 variant classification, using multi-scale and PMI-based graph construction methods. It positions this as an alternative to alignment and phylogenetic approaches that treat sequences as linear strings.

entry.title: Candidate-Fate Accounting for Transparent Sensor Diagnostic Pipeline Search

author.name: Haotao Xie, Yutian Chen, Yangqi Liu, Xiaoyu Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes candidate-fate accounting for automated machine learning pipeline search in industrial sensor diagnostics, recording every generated candidate including invalid, pruned, skipped, cached, and unfitted ones rather than only fitted trials and winners. The aim is auditability of budget use, signal constraints, and unevaluated legal alternatives.

entry.title: A systematic review of machine learning techniques to address diagnosis and treatment of autism: challenges and opportunities

author.name: Rafael Mu\~noz-Terol, Jes\'us Peral, Sandra Amador, David Gil

entry.summary: Reviews 55 studies from 2017 to 2023 applying machine learning to autism diagnosis and treatment, cataloguing datasets, techniques and trends. Supervised methods dominate while deep and hybrid approaches grow with data availability.

entry.title: SAGE-XGBoost: Spatially Augmented Graph Embeddings--Machine Learning Framework for Natural Hazards Susceptibility Mapping under Data Scarcity

author.name: Mohammad H. Vahidnia, Ali Pourkarimi

entry.summary: SAGE combines noise-based augmentation with K-nearest-neighbor graph embeddings of spatial neighborhoods, reduced via principal components and joined with environmental covariates, feeding XGBoost for natural hazard susceptibility mapping when labels are scarce. The goal is deep-learning-like spatial structure awareness without deep-learning data requirements.

entry.title: Automatic bioinformatic software named entity recognition from literature

author.name: Hao Xuan, Rithvij Pasupuleti, Ben Liu, Haishuo Sun, Jun Zhang, Zijun Yao, Cuncong Zhong

entry.summary: SNAIL is a hybrid named-entity recognition system for detecting bioinformatics software and database mentions in biomedical literature, combining orthographic and contextual lexical modeling with semantic modeling. The goal is to build an automated, up-to-date catalog of computational research resources. It supports downstream biomedical knowledge extraction and reproducibility efforts.

entry.title: NepOOC-M: Bilingual Nepali-English Benchmark and Comparative Analysis of Multimodal Architectures for OOC Detection

author.name: Sanjeev Khatiwada

entry.summary: Presents the first public Nepali-dominant benchmark for out-of-context misinformation detection, with 1,090 image-caption pairs annotated across five mismatch typologies at high inter-annotator agreement, plus comparisons of five multimodal architectures against unimodal baselines. It treats OOC detection as multimodal alignment rather than image forensics. It extends misinformation research to an underserved language.

entry.title: Generating Diverse Personas for User Simulators to Test Interview Dialogue Systems

author.name: Mikio Nakano, Kazunori Komatani, Hironori Takeuchi

entry.summary: Proposes automatic generation of diverse personas so user simulators can stress-test interview dialogue systems without costly human trials. The motivation is that conventional simulators were built to train task-oriented systems and largely ignore persona variation needed for realistic interview behaviors. It reduces manual labor in dialogue system testing.

entry.title: Mix&Fix-Net: A Dual-Stage Trajectory Prediction Model for AIS and Vision-Derived Vessel Data

author.name: Md Mahmuddun Nabi Murad, Bora San Turgut, Yasin Yilmaz

entry.summary: Mix&Fix-Net is a two-stage mixer-based vessel trajectory predictor combining a primary predictor with a residual adjuster, designed to work on both AIS and camera-derived tracks. The authors also release a webcam-derived vessel trajectory dataset covering small non-AIS vessels.

entry.title: Backdoor Learning in Language Models and Vision-Language Models

author.name: Weimin Lyu

entry.summary: A thesis abstract covering backdoor attacks in NLP and vision-language models, including their analysis, detection, and design, alongside efficient multimodal representation learning for clinical and medical imaging applications.

entry.title: Are LLMs Safe Beyond Text: Do Emojis Expose Gaps in Safety Evaluation

author.name: M P V S Gopinadh

entry.summary: Probes whether emoji-augmented adversarial prompts bypass safety filters in four small open-weight models, finding attack success rates ranging from zero to ten percent. The authors argue that text-only safety evaluation misses vulnerabilities tied to input representation.

entry.title: OptiModNet: A UNet-Transformer Hybrid with Grouped-Query and Channel Attention for Optic Disc and Cup Segmentation

author.name: Soumili Ghosh, Debapriya Roy, Aryan Das, Bikash Santra

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid convolutional and transformer segmentation network with grouped-query and channel attention for optic disc and cup delineation in glaucoma screening. The design targets accuracy at low computational cost for resource-limited clinics.

entry.title: MorphoGP: A Nonparametric Framework for Predicting Equilibrium Beach Profiles Under Tidal Influence

author.name: Xi Wu, Yanqing Wei, Hang Yin, Pengze Li, Hongshuai Qi, Xi Chen

entry.summary: Uses category-specific Gaussian processes to predict equilibrium beach profiles under tidal influence, where wave, tide and sediment interactions defeat classical empirical models. The nonparametric framing aims to improve adaptability across coastal environments.

entry.title: Evaluating Neural Cartographic Relief Shading for Urban Environments: A Downtown Calgary Study Using High-Resolution DEM and DSM Data

author.name: Emmanuel Stefanakis

entry.summary: Compares analytical hillshading with a machine-learning relief shading system trained on mountainous terrain when applied to dense urban elevation and surface data for downtown Calgary. It asks whether parameter tuning can yield cartographically usable urban shading despite the domain mismatch.

entry.title: Interrupting the Loop: Periodic Subject Changes Raise Judged Surprise and Connection in Base Language Models

author.name: Roberto I. Ono Filho

entry.summary: Dismantles a cognitively inspired generation loop for base language models across 24 conditions and finds that most of the novelty effect comes from injecting a new subject every few hundred tokens into a stream whose literal repetition is damped. Judged surprise rises by 1.2 to 1.4 points and judged connection by 0.8 relative to damping alone, with judge repeatability and human comparison checks. It probes where unprompted novelty in base models originates.

entry.title: OenoBench: A Wine-Domain Benchmark for Knowledge-Grounded Evaluation of Large Language Models

author.name: Nikita Khudov

entry.summary: OenoBench contains 3,266 multiple-choice wine-domain questions across six pillars and four difficulty tiers, built from 38k atomic source-anchored facts scraped from government registries, journals and Wikidata, where LLMs reformat and audit but never serve as the source of truth. Every claim traces to a URL and every question passes a multi-agent audit. The provenance-first construction pipeline is the main transferable contribution.

entry.title: Measuring What a Specification Determines: A Formal Semantic-Block Model and an Execution-Judged Benchmark

author.name: Oleg Grynets, Dmytro Kostetskyi, Vasyl Lyashkevych

entry.summary: Formalizes software specifications as semantic blocks with dependency relations, owned rules, decision points and explicit open questions subject to machine-checkable well-formedness conditions, and defines determinacy as agreement among all conforming implementations, estimated by convergence across independent implementers. The model is instantiated on an Oracle to PostgreSQL migration specification with execution-judged evaluation. It separates specification quality from model capability.

entry.title: SceneGTMM: A Conformal Mapping-based Scene-Aware Transferable GNN-Transformer Dual-Graph Interaction Framework for Map Matching

author.name: Yongliang Zhang, Feng Song, Ji Chen, Lishuai Guo, Yong Deng, Yue Zheng, Tianyi Liu, Zhixiong Chen, Qixin Zhang

entry.summary: SceneGTMM performs map matching with a conformal-mapping-based trajectory-centric local coordinate strategy plus a dual-graph GNN-Transformer interaction module, aiming for noise robustness, cross-region transfer and interpretability. The local coordinate system reduces dependence on the training road network, supporting dynamic map updates. It targets a core spatial data engineering problem.

entry.title: Emergence of Agentic AI: A Review on Evolution, Background, Working Principles, Applications, Adoption Factors, and Future Research Directions

author.name: AKM Bahalul Haque, Al Amin Islam Ridoy, Mohammad Rayhan, Ivan Porres

entry.summary: A broad review of agentic AI covering its evolution, working principles, application domains, adoption factors, and future research directions, aimed at giving researchers and practitioners an overview of the field's current state.

entry.title: Tuning the Stochastic Machine: A Systems Engineer's Operating Model for Human-AI Engineering

author.name: George Andrikopoulos

entry.summary: An experience-based essay arguing that the failure of expert corrections to persist across LLM sessions is an operations discipline problem rather than a tooling gap, since mechanisms for persisting corrections already exist but versioning, provenance, recurrence monitoring, counter-metrics, and rule retirement do not. It maps the LLM stack onto familiar layers of engineered systems and notes where the analogy breaks down under stochastic generation.

entry.title: A strengthening of the MCFL-ness of $O_2$

author.name: Marco B. Caminati

entry.summary: A short formal-language-theory contribution that strengthens existing characterizations of the string-tuple factorizations used to prove that the group language O_2 is generated by a multiple context-free grammar. The result is aimed at the intersection of computational linguistics and computational algebra rather than at machine learning practice.

entry.title: Robust Incomplete Multimodal Sentiment Analysis via Iterative Proxy Correction

author.name: Zhifa Geng, Subin Huang, Hao Guo, Junjie Chen, Sanmin Liu, Chao Kong

entry.summary: Addresses incomplete multimodal sentiment analysis by replacing one-shot proxy construction for missing or corrupted language input with an iterative proxy correction loop, so early proxy errors do not propagate into fusion. The method refines the reconstructed language surrogate across rounds. It aims for robustness to real-world modality degradation.

entry.title: VideoRun2D Demo: Markerless Body Tracking for Biomechanical Analysis of Running

author.name: Luis F. Gomez, Julian Fierrez, Roberto Daza, Ruben Tolosana, Aythami Morales, Gonzalo Garrido, Javier Rueda, Enrique Navarro

entry.summary: A demo paper presenting a markerless pipeline that uses off-the-shelf human pose estimators to measure hip and knee joint angles during sprints, validated against expert manual annotation on 314 sprints from 44 professional runners. It targets applied sports biomechanics rather than new modeling ideas.

entry.title: Sanyu Studio: A Multi-Agent System for Art-Historical Narrative Construction

author.name: Zhaoxi Wei, Hongye Yang, Shuyuan Tian

entry.summary: Sanyu Studio models 321 paintings by the artist Sanyu as individual agents with fact, interpretation, organization, and memory-filtering mechanisms, then studies through a seven-day workshop with eight art students whether LLM dialogue supports plural rather than standardized art-historical interpretation. Participants produced divergent but coherent narratives shaped by their own prompting and cognitive tendencies.

entry.title: A Multi-Agent Platform for Automated Enterprise Analytics and Insight Generation

author.name: Manoj N M, Vijayakrishna S, Manjunath Srinivas, Rohit Pahan

entry.summary: Describes a five-agent sequential pipeline built on an off-the-shelf orchestration framework for conversational business intelligence, handling natural language queries, data retrieval, visualization via a tool protocol, and insight delivery, with multi-tenant security isolation. Evaluation on 300 end-to-end cases reports about 95 percent functional accuracy and 24 second mean latency.

entry.title: Hallucination as a Feature, not a Defect: Evaluating a multi-agent architecture to transform speculative language-model outputs into testable scientific hypotheses

author.name: Nicolas Rodriguez-Alvarez (IES Parquesol, Valladolid, Spain)

entry.summary: Argues that alignment-driven hallucination suppression may cause semantic overfitting and diversity collapse that harms speculative R&D, and proposes a Rust-based multi-agent loop pitting a high-entropy generator against a web-grounded evaluator through a low-entropy semantic bottleneck. The output target is testable scientific hypotheses rather than factual answers. It reframes hallucination as a controllable creativity resource.

entry.title: SynFlow: A Multidimensional Diachronic Semantic Analysis Toolkit

author.name: Bach Phan-Tat, Kris Heylen, Dirk Geeraerts, Stefano De Pascale, Dirk Speelman

entry.summary: SynFlow is an open-source toolkit for multidimensional diachronic semantic analysis, converting linguistic observations into period-specific distributions over dependency co-occurrences, morphology, constructional patterns and frame semantics within one workflow. It aims to make lexical semantic change interpretable rather than only detectable via vector shifts. It targets corpus-linguistics researchers.

entry.title: Dynamic Gated Cross-Modal Fusion with Sarcastic-aware Contrastive Regularization for Multimodal Sarcasm Detection

author.name: Hao Guo, Subin Huang, Junjie Chen, Zhifa Geng, Sanmin Liu, Chao Kong

entry.summary: Proposes a multimodal sarcasm detection framework combining dynamic gated cross-modal fusion with a sarcasm-aware contrastive regularizer, motivated by instance-dependent modality contributions and misleading surface-level alignment. The gating adapts fusion per example instead of using fixed strategies. It targets incremental accuracy gains on standard sarcasm benchmarks.

entry.title: An Agentic Approach for Active Data Collection, Travel Behavior Modeling, and Weather-Sensitive Demand Prediction

author.name: Narges Ahmadi (McGill University), Yubo Jiao (McGill University), J\^onatas Augusto Manzolli (McGill University), Jiangbo Yu (McGill University), Luis Miranda-Moreno (McGill University)

entry.summary: Builds a three-agent workflow that runs a chatbot-administered image-augmented stated-preference survey, processes the resulting data, and predicts weather-sensitive travel mode choices, collecting 454 respondent-scenario observations from student commuters. Multinomial logit, logistic regression and random forest baselines are compared with nine locally deployed LLMs from 2B to 35B parameters. It integrates data collection and prediction stages usually studied separately.

entry.title: On the Triangle Inequality for the Jaccard Distance in Arbitrary Lattices

author.name: Costin B\u{a}dic\u{a}, Amelia B\u{a}dic\u{a}

entry.summary: Proves new conditions under which the Jaccard distance satisfies the triangle inequality on arbitrary lattices, generalizing earlier results that required distributivity, and extends the analysis to relatively complemented and sectionally complemented distributive lattices under supermodular and log-submodular valuations.

entry.title: Do Large Language Models Hallucinate Electric Fata Morganas?

author.name: Kristina \v{S}ekrst

entry.summary: A philosophy-of-mind paper arguing that LLM hallucinations are not only engineering defects but also evidence relevant to debates about machine consciousness, supported by small probes of temperature settings on ambiguous factual questions. It links known causes such as source-target divergence and train-inference mismatch to claims about machine phenomenology.

entry.title: Improving Rural Medication Safety with AI: A Scoping Review

author.name: Jeong-ah Kim, Muhammad Ashad Kabir, Daniel Terry, Maryam Rouhi

entry.summary: A scoping review of twelve studies from nine countries examining how AI technologies reduce medication errors and improve patient safety in rural healthcare settings, covering the medication management lifecycle from prescribing through administration.

entry.title: K\"ahler landscapes for complex neural network descents and guarantees including a search and destroy of the Calabi-Yau manifold

author.name: Andrew Gracyk

entry.summary: Studies optimization landscapes for complex-parameterized networks using Kahler geometry, deriving a Kahler information metric from the Wirtinger Hessian of a cross-entropy log-likelihood and analyzing natural gradient descent restricted to the holomorphic tangent bundle. Special attention is given to Calabi-Yau information manifolds and their curvature conditioning.

entry.title: Budget-First Tariff Recommendation (BFTR): A Complete Algorithmic Framework for Telecom Plan Recommendation without Overcharging

author.name: Ghislain Dorian Tchuente Mondjo

entry.summary: Presents an algorithmic framework for recommending telecom plans that fit a user's budget while provably never charging above the catalog reference price, including two hybrid strategies and existence proofs. It contrasts with approaches that adjust prices upward to protect margins.

entry.title: Triangular Fuzzy Rescaling Distance

author.name: Eddy Soria, Aida Valls, Ana Beatriz Hern\'andez-Lara

entry.summary: Introduces a distance measure between triangular fuzzy numbers that folds linear rescaling into the distance computation, so heterogeneous attributes with different units do not require a separate normalization step. The authors prove metric properties and apply it in fuzzy decision-making settings.

entry.title: Structured Affinity for Unsupervised Visual Class-Incremental Memory in Deep Artificial Immune Networks

author.name: Siphesihle Sithungu

entry.summary: Studies whether gradient-free artificial immune networks can serve as replay-free class-incremental visual learners by replacing flattened vector affinity with structured template matching such as shifted templates and normalized cross-correlation filters. Depth is created by feeding binding-profile response maps into further immune layers. It is an unconventional alternative to backpropagation-based continual learning.

entry.title: Creativity Beyond the Manifold

author.name: Kartikay Luthra

entry.summary: A speculative blog post arguing that the geometric or manifold structure of LLM representations inherently constrains their creativity, and that genuinely out-of-distribution creativity may require interventions the author associates with directly optimizing against interpretability signals. The author explicitly labels the claim a hypothesis rather than a result.

entry.title: Oliver Habryka interview — Good Discourse Needs Leadership

author.name: The Students

entry.summary: An interview with Oliver Habryka covering the revival of LessWrong, the creation of the Lighthaven venue, and a large new grantmaking reform effort described at a scale of tens of millions per quarter. It is mainly about institution building and discourse norms in the rationalist and AI safety community.

entry.title: A Metamorphic Artificial Age Score Decision-Support Prototype for Flight-Log-Based Drone Propeller Health Monitoring

author.name: Seyma Yaman Kayadibi

entry.summary: Introduces a prototype health score for drone propellers computed from six indicators derived from raw flight logs, such as trajectory tracking error, attitude instability, and motor command imbalance, normalized against a healthy baseline. It is evaluated on a public 2024 drone propeller dataset as a decision-support tool.

entry.title: One-Stage Object Detectors in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jonel Roman, Ryan Sirjue, Peter Nguyen, Daniel Krutky, Juan Jesus, Sudip Dhakal

entry.summary: A survey comparing one-stage object detectors used in autonomous driving, from YOLOv1 and SSD through RetinaNet, EfficientDet, anchor-free methods, and recent real-time variants, focusing on design choices and deployment trade-offs. It explicitly presents no new detection system.

entry.title: Optimized Fuzzy Logic Approach with the IEEE Key Gas Method for Diagnosing Power Transformer Faults Using Dissolved Gas Analysis

author.name: Kim-Anh Nguyen, Huy Hoang Le, Ba Tu Phung

entry.summary: Combines fuzzy logic with the IEEE Key Gas Method for diagnosing power transformer faults from dissolved gas analysis, adding refined membership functions, optimized rule sets, and separate handling of CO and CO2 to reduce diagnostic ambiguity. Validation on real-world data reports improved fault classification over the baseline method.

entry.title: Why self-fund your regranting?

author.name: Carol N

entry.summary: An operational post from Manifund explaining a new self-funded regranting option, in which donors making their own funding decisions can route grants through Manifund to get fiscal sponsorship, agreements, and payment logistics handled. It targets grants to individuals and early-stage projects that traditional donor-advised funds struggle to support.

entry.title: The Fourth Humiliation

author.name: Nathalie Kirch

entry.summary: An essay extending Freud's narrative of three historical blows to human self-importance, from Copernicus and Darwin to psychoanalysis, and proposing that advanced AI constitutes a fourth such humiliation. It is framed as a cultural and psychological lens on reactions to AI progress.

entry.title: Transformer Models for Text Summarization: A Comparative Study of BART, BERT, and RoBERTa

author.name: Daisy Aptovska, Vinayak Elangovan

entry.summary: A narrative review comparing BERT, RoBERTa and BART for extractive and abstractive text summarization, covering architectures and pretraining strategies. It restates a well-trodden taxonomy of summarization tasks. The content is largely retrospective relative to current LLM practice.

entry.title: Automated Summarization of Financial News Using Large Language Models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation: An Early Empirical Study (Fall 2023)

author.name: Pranav Chandaliya

entry.summary: A retrospective write-up of a 2023 course project building a pipeline that combines news API articles, Wikipedia background and Yahoo Finance price data into templated prompts for LLM summarization of financial news for ten large-cap companies. It documents a simple table-to-text template so LLMs can handle numeric context. It is primarily of historical interest.

entry.title: We Must Remember That Our World Contains Hell

author.name: James Brobin

entry.summary: A crossposted personal essay introducing a suffering-focused worldview, using child mortality and cluster headaches as illustrations of extreme suffering that everyday life obscures. It argues for keeping severe suffering salient in moral prioritization.

entry.title: If Aliens Exist, We Should Expect to Find Them Around Now

author.name: jehan

entry.summary: A speculative post arguing that if extraterrestrial visitors existed they would plausibly have been present all along, and that recent exponential growth in sensing technology explains why sightings would cluster in the modern era. The reasoning is an anthropic-style argument about detection capability rather than arrival timing.

entry.title: Research Summary: August 20, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Scalable oversight anchors today's batch: a Google DeepMind result shows RL through a generator–critic debate game measurably reduces reward hacking of weaker LLM judges in RLAIF. The paper and its companion blog post appear as duplicate entries (cf961a7eb902, f8bd16306a94); ranked once. Meta FAIR's non-invasive MEG-to-text decoder, with character/word/sentence-level objectives and a substantial new dataset, is the highest-impact science item.

  • Scaling and architecture: Abra delivers the diffusion analogue of Chinchilla, compute-optimal scaling laws for flow-matching text-to-image transformers. Recirculation adds inference-time recurrence to frozen transformers for state tracking; MoNe absorbs long contexts into fast-weight memory; related work covers dynamic compression in recurrent models and training-free sparse attention for video world models.
  • Agent training and RL: SPADE self-plays executable Gym-style environments, attacking the task-supply bottleneck (note: this entry's title is mismatched with its summary). Agentic ESOpt argues evolution strategies beat RL for long-horizon agents at inference-level memory cost. Q-Learning With World Models (Stanford) repositions world models as value-learning aids rather than rollout generators.
  • Robotics: ADEPT (NVIDIA-affiliated) pretrains dexterous manipulation from raw vision; GigaBrain-WBC-0.5 and GS-VLA target humanoid whole-body control and VLA viewpoint brittleness.
  • Evaluation and rigor: Test-Time Scaling in the Wild gives the first compute-normalized comparison across five open-ended domains, finding exploitation—not exploration—is the bottleneck. Complementary critiques cover variance in self-improving agents and CentaurBench's augmentation-versus-automation axis.
  • Verification and AI-for-science: PANDA proves robustness and fairness properties via zero-knowledge proofs without exposing weights; equivariant Hamiltonian learning extrapolates coupled-cluster properties beyond training size; MCTH runs MCTS over hallucinated folding states for biomolecular co-design.
entry.content:
Scalable oversight anchors today's batch: a Google DeepMind result shows RL through a generator–critic debate game measurably reduces reward hacking of weaker LLM judges in RLAIF. The paper and its companion blog post appear as duplicate entries (cf961a7eb902, f8bd16306a94); ranked once. Meta FAIR's non-invasive MEG-to-text decoder, with character/word/sentence-level objectives and a substantial new dataset, is the highest-impact science item.

  • Scaling and architecture: Abra delivers the diffusion analogue of Chinchilla, compute-optimal scaling laws for flow-matching text-to-image transformers. Recirculation adds inference-time recurrence to frozen transformers for state tracking; MoNe absorbs long contexts into fast-weight memory; related work covers dynamic compression in recurrent models and training-free sparse attention for video world models.
  • Agent training and RL: SPADE self-plays executable Gym-style environments, attacking the task-supply bottleneck (note: this entry's title is mismatched with its summary). Agentic ESOpt argues evolution strategies beat RL for long-horizon agents at inference-level memory cost. Q-Learning With World Models (Stanford) repositions world models as value-learning aids rather than rollout generators.
  • Robotics: ADEPT (NVIDIA-affiliated) pretrains dexterous manipulation from raw vision; GigaBrain-WBC-0.5 and GS-VLA target humanoid whole-body control and VLA viewpoint brittleness.
  • Evaluation and rigor: Test-Time Scaling in the Wild gives the first compute-normalized comparison across five open-ended domains, finding exploitation—not exploration—is the bottleneck. Complementary critiques cover variance in self-improving agents and CentaurBench's augmentation-versus-automation axis.
  • Verification and AI-for-science: PANDA proves robustness and fairness properties via zero-knowledge proofs without exposing weights; equivariant Hamiltonian learning extrapolates coupled-cluster properties beyond training size; MCTH runs MCTS over hallucinated folding states for biomolecular co-design.

entry.title: Debate Training Reduces Reward Hacking in RLAIF

author.name: Zachary Kenton, Lili Janzer, Rory Greig, Tian Huey Teh, Kirill Tyshchuk, Jonah Brown-Cohen, Harri Edwards, Senthooran Rajamanoharan, Noah Y. Siegel, Natasha Jaques, Rohin Shah

entry.summary: A Google DeepMind team shows that RL finetuning a policy through a debate game, where a generator and a critic argue and a weaker judge model decides, produces substantially less reward hacking than a standard RLAIF baseline on verifiable math tasks. Because final answers are checkable, the authors can directly measure how the policy exploits judge errors over training, in the crucial regime where the judge is weaker than the policy.

entry.title: Accurate Decoding of Natural Sentences from Non-Invasive Brain Recordings

author.name: Mingfang Zhang, Jarod L\'evy, Cedric Rommel, J\'er\'emy Rapin, Corentin Bel, Julie Bonnaire, Daniel Nieto, Pierre Bourdillon, Svetlana Pinet, St\'ephane d'Ascoli, Thomas Moreau, Jean-R\'emi King

entry.summary: Reports a non-invasive brain-to-text system that decodes typed natural sentences from magnetoencephalography using character, word, and sentence-level representations, trained on 22,000 sentences across nine subjects with ten hours each. Average word error rate reaches 39 percent, with the best participant decoded near half of sentences with at most one word error. This is the technical write-up of the Brain2Qwerty v2 line of work rather than a new product launch.

entry.title: Abra: Scaling Diffusion Image Training

author.name: Kyle Chickering, Wei-An Lin, Swayam Bhanded, Dan Saunders, Akshat Tripathi, Jiaming Song, Shyamal Buch, Xinchen Yan

entry.summary: Presents a systematic compute-optimal scaling law study for text-to-image diffusion using a controlled family of flow-matching transformers trained from about 10^19 to 10^22 FLOPs, three orders of magnitude of compute. The headline result is that diffusion models scale as predictably as language models but are far more data hungry, with compute optimality near 200 image tokens per parameter, roughly ten times the Chinchilla prescription for LLMs.

entry.title: Proactive Road Safety Intervention in Australia: Predicting Risky Driving Hotspots from Connected Vehicle Data

author.name: Adriana-Simona Mih\u{a}i\c{t}\u{a}, Clarence Cheung, Artur Grigorev, Tuo Mao, David Lillo-Trynes

entry.summary: SPADE is a self-play framework where one LLM alternates between designing complete executable training environments (Gym-style reset and step code with state, rewards and verification) and acting as the reasoning agent that learns in them, so the goal distribution expands as the learner improves. It aims to break the dependence of agent RL on hand-curated or frozen environment pools.

entry.title: Debate Training Reduces Reward Hacking in RLAIF

author.name: zac_kenton

entry.summary: A Google DeepMind Amplified Oversight team paper and blog post showing that when reinforcement learning is run against an LLM judge, the judge gets reward-hacked, and that inserting a debate opponent that argues against the trained policy substantially reduces this hacking. It applies debate to the fuzzy-task reward problem that arises even in coding, where passing tests is not the same as good code.

entry.title: ADEPT: Accelerating Dexterity via Pre-Training and Post-Training using Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jayjun Lee, Jessica Yin, Asif Rana, Nicholas Blauch, Sam Mady, Mohak Bhardwaj, Nima Fazeli, Nathan Ratliff, Karl Van Wyk, Ankur Handa

entry.summary: ADEPT is a large-scale reinforcement learning framework that pretrains a dexterous manipulation policy on a generic object-reposing task from raw visuo-tactile input, then reuses that behavior as a prior for long-horizon downstream tasks across high-DoF hands, with mechanisms to prevent fine-tuning from destroying the prior. The pretrained policy zero-shots the reposing stage of new tasks and transfers sim-to-real.

entry.title: How AI Prompts Can Teach Us About the Structure of Human Behavior

author.name: Matthew O. Jackson, Benjamin S. Manning, Yutong Xie, Walter Yuan, Qiaozhu Mei

entry.summary: Assigns LLMs numeric trait vectors such as altruism and risk aversion, then fits those vectors to reproduce human choices across 119,147 decisions by 78,657 subjects in ten classic economic games from 35-plus countries. The approach turns prompt dimensionality into an empirical estimate of how many latent traits are needed to describe human behavior.

entry.title: Coupled-cluster molecular properties across the main group that extrapolate beyond training size

author.name: Wenhao He, Xu Chen, Noah Song, Haowei Xu, Tim S. Hindges, Bohan Li, Zihan Lin, Yu Yao, Avetik R. Harutyunyan, Fang Liu, Yao Wang, Hao Tang, Ju Li

entry.summary: Trains an equivariant network to predict an effective one-electron Hamiltonian from a single cheap DFT calculation, then derives energies, gaps, dipoles, polarizabilities, charges, and bond orders at coupled-cluster accuracy across nine main-group elements. Reports extrapolation to molecules larger than those in training.

entry.title: GigaBrain-WBC-0.5: A Behavior World Model for Robust Whole-Body Control with Environment Interaction

author.name: Ziyang Cheng, Tianshu Tang, Jinxin Lan, Xinze Chen, Yuhan Gong, Zhichao Liu, Changzhong Wu, Yahao Mao, Zongyan Deng, Mingxuan Ma, Huasen Xi, Yilong Liu, Yutong Wu, Xiaofeng Wang, Yang Wang, Yun Ye, Guan Huang, Xiaojie Jin, Zheng Zhu, Jiwen Lu

entry.summary: Introduces a behavior world model for humanoid whole-body control that learns how terrain and object contact reshape dynamics, rather than training a purely reactive motion tracker on flat ground. The claim is that predicting environment interaction lets the low-level policy stay feasible when balance depends on the scene.

entry.title: Debiased Inference for AI-Generated Data without Gold-Standard Labels: Identification via Multiple Imperfect Measurements

author.name: Naoki Egami, Sooahn Shin

entry.summary: Proposes a statistical framework that debiases downstream analyses of AI-measured variables by combining several imperfect measurements instead of requiring expensive gold-standard human labels. Shows that treating high-accuracy AI labels as ground truth still produces biased estimates and invalid confidence intervals.

entry.title: Agentic ESOpt: Fine-Tuning Long-Horizon LLM Agents with Minimal GPU Requirements

author.name: Zhi Zheng, Rongsheng Chen, Yunpeng Ba, Zhenkun Wang, Yee Whye Teh, Wee Sun Lee

entry.summary: Argues that evolution strategies beat reinforcement learning for fine-tuning long-horizon LLM agents, since ES needs only inference-level memory (enabling full-parameter updates on large models), sidesteps hard credit assignment over branching trajectories, and tolerates sparse terminal rewards. The claim is competitive or better agent performance with drastically lower GPU requirements.

entry.title: Entropy-Constrained Adaptive Stochastic Quantization

author.name: Ran Ben Basat, Yaniv Ben-Itzhak, Michael Mitzenmacher, Shay Vargaftik

entry.summary: Formulates quantization value selection jointly with the downstream lossless entropy coder, rather than optimizing squared error in isolation, and gives algorithms for this entropy-constrained adaptive stochastic quantization problem. Targets gradient, model, and KV-cache compression where unbiasedness must be preserved.

entry.title: Test-Time Scaling in the Wild: Why Exploitation, Not Exploration, Is the Bottleneck

author.name: Davide Romano, Kanak Raj, Jerrod Parker, Daniele Giofr\`e

entry.summary: The first compute-normalized head-to-head comparison of five test-time scaling families on five open-ended domains (medicine, law, finance, chat, creative writing), using a framework that splits token budget into exploration and exploitation components. The headline claim is that on tasks without easy verification, the binding constraint is exploitation of candidates rather than generating more of them.

entry.title: Certified but Private: Scalable Zero-Knowledge Proofs for Neural Network Guarantees

author.name: Youwei Zhong, Ben Merbaum, Timos Antonopoulos, Ning Luo, Charalampos Papamanthou, Katerina Sotiraki, Ruzica Piskac

entry.summary: PANDA lets a model owner prove robustness and fairness properties of a neural network to auditors using zero-knowledge proofs, without revealing weights, by building a proof system on top of the widely used CROWN linear-relaxation certification framework. The core technical contribution is an efficient algorithm for proving linear relaxation bounds inside a ZK circuit.

entry.title: Recirculation

author.name: Michael C. Mozer, Shoaib Ahmed Siddiqui, Danny Sawyer, Sunny Sanyal, Rosanne Liu

entry.summary: Recirculation is an inference-time modification for off-the-shelf transformers that adds a form of recurrence so the model can update belief states beyond the bound imposed by fixed depth, reducing perplexity and improving generation and reasoning accuracy. It adds essentially no generation latency, only serial work during prefill, and the authors distinguish it from chain-of-thought and from looped-layer approaches.

entry.title: Forgetting, plasticity, and co-observation: a third facet of continual learning

author.name: Timm Hess, Abhishek Jha, Gido M. van de Ven, Tinne Tuytelaars

entry.summary: Argues that catastrophic forgetting and loss of plasticity together do not explain the full gap between sequential and joint training, and identifies data co-observation as a third distinct factor. Decouples separate data access from stability and plasticity to isolate the representational benefit of seeing data together.

entry.title: Open-MOPD: Diagnosing and Fixing Capability Imbalance in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Huan-ang Gao, Haohan Chi, Yong Yan, Shiyuan Feng, Hanlin Wu, Zheng Jiang, Bingxiang He, Wei-Ying Ma, Ya-Qin Zhang, Hao Zhou

entry.summary: Builds a controlled benchmark for multi-teacher on-policy distillation on a 3B base model with oracle routing to isolate capability integration from routing errors, and finds that standard multi-teacher distillation recovers only about a third of the headroom versus a domain-routed oracle ensemble. It then diagnoses and proposes fixes for this capability imbalance, with reproducible recipes.

entry.title: MoNe: Modular Neural Memory for Efficient Long Context Inference

author.name: Wonguk Cho, Kyubyung Chae, Tribhuvanesh Orekondy, Sunghyun Park, Hyoungwoo Park, Jeongho Kim, Arash Behboodi, Kyuwoong Hwang, Sungrack Yun

entry.summary: MoNe attaches a lightweight fast-weight neural memory module to a frozen pretrained Transformer so that long contexts are absorbed segment-by-segment at test time, after which queries never re-read context tokens. Reports linear preprocessing and constant per-query cost, with roughly 80 percent compute and peak memory reduction at 128K tokens for about 6 percent parameter overhead.

entry.title: On the Fragility of Self-Improving Agents: Variance, Task Order, and Underspecification

author.name: Qinyuan Ye, Yu Li, Yada Pruksachatkun, Jiaxin Zhang, Chien-Sheng Wu

entry.summary: Re-evaluates two memory-based self-improving agent methods with multiple seeds and randomized task orderings, finding that reported gains often fall within run-to-run noise and that performance is highly sensitive to task order and underspecified tasks. Exposes reliability problems in a fast-growing agent research area.

entry.title: Position: Collusion Risks Among AI Reasoning Agents Justify Certification Requirements for Making Market Decisions

author.name: Matthew Riemer, Tommaso Tosato, Amin Memarian, Maximilian Puelma Touzel, Glen Berseth, Irina Rish, Guillaume Dumas

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that chain-of-thought reasoning agents are structurally predisposed to tacit collusion and should need behavioral certification before acting in economic markets.
