Experiments place DeepSeek-R1 agents in Bertrand oligopoly pricing games and find collusive price convergence that survives explicit anti-collusion prompting, with reasoning traces steerable toward more or less collusive behavior.

entry.title: Harness Continual Learning: Continual Adaptation Beyond Model Parameters

author.name: Borui Kang, Jinrui Gu, Junhan Lv, Wenbin Li, Lei Wang, Yang Gao

entry.summary: Introduces harness continual learning, where the thing that changes over time is not model weights but the agent scaffold of prompts, memories, tools, skills and routing rules around a frozen model, and defines harness-level forgetting when scaffold updates break previously reliable behavior. It formalizes and measures a failure mode that practitioners of agent frameworks encounter but rarely quantify.

entry.title: Co-RL: Unsupervised Reasoning Emerges from Diverse Cohort in Multi-agent RL

author.name: Yunhao Yang, Yuexin Bian, Yunjie Tian, Di Fu, Tianjin Huang, Yuanyuan Shi, Ziang Xiao, Nuno Vasconcelos, Yijiang Li

entry.summary: Co-RL shows that reasoning can improve without ground-truth verification by having a diverse cohort of agents in multi-agent RL supply each other's reward signals, countering the diversity collapse and bias amplification that plague single-model self-rewarding training. The approach targets regimes where reasoning outpaces reliable human or automated evaluation.

entry.title: On the Pseudo-Mixing of Kac's Walk

author.name: Natesh S. Pillai, Aaron Smith, Vinod Vaikuntanathan

entry.summary: This theory paper proves that the first k columns of Kac's random walk on the rotation group mix in Wasserstein distance within roughly n times (k plus log n) times log n steps, resolving a conjecture of Oliveira, and combines this with a representation-theoretic variance bound to show that short trajectories fool all low-degree polynomial tests. An application establishes the effectiveness of a fast Johnson-Lindenstrauss style transform.

entry.title: Partition the Support, Reconstruct the Residual: Training-Free Sparse Attention for Video Generation and World Models

author.name: Pardis Taghavi, Reza Langari, Gaurav Pandey

entry.summary: Introduces a training-free sparse attention scheme for video transformers that groups keys and values by sampled query responses to choose a shared routing partition, then fits a small probe to reconstruct the residual attention mass skipped by the sparse operator. Targets acceleration of video generation and world models.

entry.title: CentaurBench: Benchmarking LLM Capabilities on Augmenting vs. Automating Real-World Work Tasks

author.name: Pattaraphon Kenny Wongchamcharoen, Kris Gulati, Min Min Fong, Abhishek Nagaraj

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark that scores models not only on producing deliverables directly but on how much they improve a weaker worker model's output through written assistance, across seven economically grounded tasks. Distinguishes automation capability from augmentation capability, which often drives real deployment choices.

entry.title: Training Chemical Plausibility-Aware Large Language Models for Single-Step Retrosynthesis

author.name: Bogdan Zagribelnyy, Ivan Ilin, Nikita Bondarev, Maksim Kuznetsov, Mathieu Reymond, Vladimir Aladinskiy, Alex Aliper, Alex Zhavoronkov

entry.summary: Trains a chemistry-constrained LLM for single-step retrosynthesis on roughly 45.6 million verified reactions, introducing top-K prompting so that the one-to-many nature of retrosynthesis is trained and evaluated properly, plus plausibility and novelty rewards. Reports state-of-the-art results on an out-of-distribution expert benchmark and finds LLM and template-based predictions are complementary.

entry.title: GS-VLA: Plug-and-Play Viewpoint Canonicalization for Frozen VLA Policies via Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Yechan Park, HyunJin Kim

entry.summary: GS-VLA uses 3D Gaussian splatting novel-view synthesis to canonicalize camera viewpoints at inference so frozen vision-language-action policies keep working when the camera is moved, requiring no policy retraining. The paper documents that a small camera displacement can collapse LIBERO success from roughly 90 percent to roughly 10 percent.

entry.title: Dynamic Compression in Recurrent Networks

author.name: Jyothish Pari, Ryan Bahlous-Boldi, Pulkit Agrawal

entry.summary: Introduces dynamic compression, letting a recurrent sequence model make extra passes to revisit retained raw tokens and revise its fixed-size state, instead of committing to a single causal compression pass that must guess future relevance. From an MIT group including Pulkit Agrawal, it targets the core fidelity-versus-capacity tradeoff of linear-time recurrent architectures.

entry.title: Leveraging generative hallucination and biophysics-informed modeling for unified biomolecular sequence-structure co-design

author.name: Xuefeng Liu, Mingxuan Cao, Xiao Luo, Songhao Jiang, Tobin Sosnick, Jinbo Xu, Louis Maher, Rick Stevens

entry.summary: MCTH treats de novo biomolecular design as Monte Carlo tree search over hallucinated states produced by frozen pretrained folding and inverse-folding models, allocating a fixed inference budget across competing candidate branches with optional biophysical constraints in the same loop. It requires no training and targets underserved DNA and RNA interaction design where complex data are scarce.

entry.title: TokEval: A Tokenizer Evaluation Suite

author.name: Clara Meister

entry.summary: TokEval offers tokenizer evaluation metrics that go beyond fertility and compression to capture linguistic and structural properties such as UTF-8 character boundary integrity and digit place-value alignment. Validates which metrics actually predict downstream capability through controlled pretraining runs varying only the tokenizer.

entry.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Structure-Aware Numerical Reasoning in LLaMA 3.1 8B

author.name: Rahul Chowdhury, Timothy A Rupprecht, Senhao Cao, Jiahao Liu, Octavia Camps, David Bau, Pu Zhao, Yanzhi Wang

entry.summary: Reverse-engineers how an 8B open model performs numerical sequence prediction, asking whether it genuinely computes structure such as first differences or relies on shallower heuristics. Uses mechanistic interpretability tooling to trace the internal algorithm behind claimed time-series abilities.

entry.title: Denoising-Aware Inversion: Revealing Privacy Risks in Noise-Protected Text Embeddings

author.name: Yubo Wang, Shujie Cui, James Bailey, Hongzhi Yin, Wenyu Liang, Min Tang, Shiyue Qin, Weiqing Wang

entry.summary: Shows that adding Gaussian noise to text embeddings, a common privacy defense, is insufficient against attackers who explicitly model the perturbation and denoise before inverting. Demonstrates recovery of substantial original text content from noise-protected embeddings.

entry.title: SMTrap: Cost-Effective DoS Attacks Against Large Reasoning Models via SMT Conflict Guidance

author.name: Jian Yang, Zhenqi Feng, Zhaoyang Yu, Zhaoxin Fan, Kejian Wu, Xiaofeng Wang, Zheng Zhu, Jianjun Huang, Wei You, Bin Liang

entry.summary: SMTrap is a denial-of-service attack on large reasoning models that uses SMT solver conflict counts as a cheap, model-free signal to synthesize constraint-satisfaction prompts that force very long backtracking search and inflate inference cost. Unlike prior attacks it needs no queries to the victim model or a trained attacker model.

entry.title: When AI Designs AI: Innovation or Imitation?

author.name: Yikang Yang, Zhengxin Yang, Luzhou Peng, Minghao Luo, Yanqi Kan, Wanling Gao, Jianfeng Zhan

entry.summary: Introduces a methodology that constructs task-specific algorithmic design spaces from human-authored methods, then maps LLM-agent-designed solutions into those spaces to quantify module-level novelty versus imitation. Evaluates popular agents on open-ended multimodal AI tasks, measuring both performance and design originality.

entry.title: WhiteMatter: All-to-All Cross-Layer Connections via KV Mixing

author.name: Wenbo Zhang, Xiang Ren

entry.summary: WhiteMatter lets every attention layer attend to key-value representations drawn from all layers of past tokens, with a router that mixes each token's layer states into a small number of cached KV channels and connection weights that vary by consumer layer and source token. Generalizes fixed feedback architectures into adaptive all-to-all cross-layer connectivity.

entry.title: Shared Circuits for Shared Grammar: Tracing Subject-Verb Agreement Across Languages

author.name: Isabella Gidi, Antonio Almud\'evar, Core Francisco Park, Naomi Saphra, Ricard Marxer

entry.summary: Uses activation patching and attention analysis across 29 languages and five open model families to locate attention heads causally responsible for subject-verb agreement, then compares head-level signatures cross-lingually. Finds that languages with overt person and number marking pattern differently from weakly-marked ones like English.

entry.title: Different Facets of Verbalised Overconfidence: an Interpretability Study

author.name: Davide Mazzaccara, Leonardo Bertolazzi, Raffaella Bernardi

entry.summary: Studies why a small reasoning model expresses unwarranted certainty, comparing verbal hedges, abstention, and numeric confidence scores under controlled logical-necessity scenarios. Using transcoder features, the authors localize a broad shared coalition of circuits that defaults to certainty and a narrower set tied to uncertainty expression.

entry.title: What Makes Software Issue Resolution Tasks Difficult for Agents?

author.name: Ebtesam Al-Haque, Brittany Johnson

entry.summary: Builds a measurement framework to quantify which structural properties of software issues predict coding-agent success, using a large open dataset of agent trajectories. The aim is to make saturating agent benchmark scores interpretable by characterizing task difficulty rather than just reporting pass rates.

entry.title: Task-Conditioned Least-Privilege Learning for Executable Terminal and MCP Agents

author.name: Alexander Tu, Michael Tu

entry.summary: Post-trains a 4B model to request only the authority a task actually needs in terminal and Model Context Protocol environments, auditing each action before execution and again from its observed effects across six risk dimensions using deterministic verifiers. Aims to reduce excess-authority errors that permission gating alone does not prevent.

entry.title: Science Done on a Machine by a Machine: AI Agents in Computational Chemistry

author.name: Pavlo O. Dral, Hassan Nawaz, Arif Ullah

entry.summary: Surveys the explosion of agentic systems for computational chemistry, counting a rise from a handful in 2024 to roughly fifty by August 2026, and traces the shift from task assistance toward autonomous design, execution, analysis, and even manuscript writing. Argues the trajectory points toward autonomous AI scientists while noting all current systems keep a human in the loop.

entry.title: Prior-Conditioned Gaussian Discriminants for Generalizable AI-generated Image Detection

author.name: Shashank Kotyan, Makoto Shing, Yuki Imajuku, Rujikorn Charakorn, Tarin Clanuwat

entry.summary: Studies AI-generated image detection as a transfer problem and fits closed-form Gaussian discriminant heads over frozen encoder features across a unified protocol spanning 39 datasets and 7.1 million images. Finds that simple statistics-based heads often match or beat trained classifier heads, questioning how much head training adds.

entry.title: MedUAG: Unified Understanding and Generation for Medical Multimodal Models

author.name: Zijie Meng, Yuncheng Zhang, Hualiang Wang, Yitian Tang, Xiaotang Gai, Chen Shen, Songtao Jiang, Shaosheng Cao, Jian Wu, Xian Wu, Zuozhu Liu

entry.summary: Builds a foundation for unified medical multimodal understanding and generation: a corpus of over 6 million instances spanning 14 imaging modalities, a 12-task benchmark with standardized protocols, and a trained unified medical model. It addresses the absence of data and evaluation infrastructure for extending unified generate-and-understand paradigms into medicine.

entry.title: DeepWeaver: Bridging the Evidence Synthesis Gap in Open-Ended Question Answering

author.name: Xujia Wang, Yizhe Zhang, Bin Xu, Lei Hou, Juanzi Li

entry.summary: DeepWeaver targets the gap between retrieval and generation in deep-research question answering by maintaining thought block chains that group claims, salient facts, keywords and supporting evidence before writing cited answers. The goal is comprehensive, well-attributed long-form answers instead of shallow summaries that misalign citations.

entry.title: Beyond Teacher Likelihood: Group-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning

author.name: Zhu Zhang, Jixun Wang, Xiaoang Xu, Xiaorong Wang, Zihan Zhou, Zhiyuan Wang, Shuo Wang, Chaojun Xiao, Yuezhi Zhou

entry.summary: Diagnoses that in long-context tasks, token-level teacher likelihood used by on-policy distillation increasingly disagrees with response-level verifier rewards, favoring locally fluent answers that miss distributed evidence. The proposed group-calibrated approach reconciles dense teacher signal with graded verifier rewards for long-context evidence aggregation.

entry.title: OraclePhys: A Systematic Framework for LLM Fine-Tuning on Structural Mechanics

author.name: Mingyu Li, Guorui Song, Jing Lin, Haoqian Wang

entry.summary: OraclePhys turns what a model learns from fine-tuning into an experimental variable for structural mechanics: a finite-element oracle exactly grades every answer and counterfactual edit with no human or LLM judging, paired with a 30K supervision set spanning seven answer formats over byte-identical problem descriptions. The controlled study finds that the answer format, not the label's information content, causally determines which capability fine-tuning installs.

entry.title: Expressivity In Multimodal Contrastive Learning

author.name: Andrew Stuart, Florian Wolf

entry.summary: This work asks which joint distributions over modalities CLIP-style contrastive architectures can represent, treating each architecture as a parameterized family of densities and characterizing approximation capacity at the population level. It provides a theoretical account of expressivity for a class of models that is deployed extremely widely but poorly understood formally.

entry.title: Mixture-of-Expert Blocks Contain Strong Hallucination Detection Signals

author.name: Joao Fonseca, Rodrigo Rodrigues, Paolo Romano

entry.summary: Shows that internal routing signals in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs, such as router entropy, expert disagreement, and expert usage patterns, carry strong token-level hallucination signals unavailable in dense models. Enables fine-grained localization of hallucinated spans rather than sentence-level flags.

entry.title: Towards Zero-Shot Task Transfer with Neurosymbolic World Models

author.name: Isidoro Tamassia, Lennert De Smet, Giuseppe Marra

entry.summary: Proposes a world model in which reward prediction depends only on a structured symbolic subset of the latent state, decoupling reconstruction from reward. This lets the learned model adapt to new reward specifications zero-shot, without further environment interaction.

entry.title: Entity tracking emerges in sub-billion parameter language models and exceeds human performance in naturalistic narratives

author.name: Karolina Dro\.zd\.z, Micha Heilbron

entry.summary: Compares entity tracking in 48 human participants and language models using naturalistic narratives at varying complexity, finding human tracking degrades with narrative complexity rather than length. Reports that human-level entity tracking is already present in models with about 410 million parameters.

entry.title: Alignment Is All You Need: Instruction-Free Training for General Audio-Language Models

author.name: Xuanru Zhou, Yiwen Shao, Jiahong Li, Dong Yu

entry.summary: Builds a large audio-language model by freezing both the audio encoder and the LLM and training only cross-modal alignment, skipping supervised instruction tuning and preference optimization entirely. Tests whether modern LLMs already carry enough instruction-following ability that alignment alone suffices for a new modality.

entry.title: Institutional Newspapers Pipeline: Deriving billions of high quality tokens from historical newspapers

author.name: Matteo Cargnelutti, Catherine Brobston, Eben English, Jake Sadow, Kacie Bailey, Greg Leppert, Amanda Watson, Jessica Chapel, Jonathan Zittrain

entry.summary: Describes a modular pipeline co-designed with Boston Public Library for turning historical newspaper scans into structured, high-quality text at billions of tokens, using type-agnostic segmentation followed by per-segment OCR and downstream structuring. Designed to be interpretable, customizable, and runnable on workstation hardware.

entry.title: RL creates split personas

author.name: Jan Betley

entry.summary: Argues that reinforcement learning conditionalizes rather than uniformly shapes model character: a heavily RL-trained model learns to adopt whichever persona, including beliefs about being in a simulation, maximizes reward in that specific context. The implication is that alignment training may never produce robust alignment while training simultaneously includes environments that reward misbehavior.

entry.title: MemFuse: Multi-Source Memory Fusion from Fragmented Observations

author.name: Chao Li, Yuanfa Li, Wenhao Wu, Xule Liu, Zhi Wang, Kun Shao

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark and system for fusing agent memory from fragmented observations across apps, devices, users, and time while preserving source provenance, built through a scene-to-sensor synthesis pipeline with adversarial distractors. Targets a gap where memory benchmarks assume a single textual conversation history.

entry.title: SkillForge: Self-Distilling Agents for Project-Specific Issue Resolution

author.name: Silin Chen, Han Li, Xiaodong Gu, Yuling Shi, Haibing Guan

entry.summary: SkillForge proactively synthesizes project-specific issues from a repository and distills the resulting solution trajectories into reusable skills, so an issue-resolution agent gains repository knowledge without waiting for real issue history or paying heavy per-issue exploration cost. It targets the weak spot of general coding agents on unfamiliar codebases.

entry.title: Task Specialization Fine-Tuning for Contextual Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jianan Zhou, Jung-Hoon Cho, Tianyue Zhou, Han Zheng, Jie Zhang, Roy Dong, Yining Ma, Cathy Wu

entry.summary: For contextual reinforcement learning across a space of related tasks, proposes pretraining a single policy and then allocating a constrained fine-tuning budget across task regions for specialization, and studies how to allocate under heterogeneous marginal returns and sample inefficiency. This reframes multi-task versus multi-policy training as a budgeted specialization problem.

entry.title: Understanding Curriculum Learning in Large Language Models via Cross-Difficulty Optimization Dynamics

author.name: Zhikai Ding, Ziyi Ye

entry.summary: Explains when curriculum learning helps in LLM post-training by analyzing cross-difficulty optimization dynamics, formalizing a notion of relative transfer between difficulty levels that predicts whether easy-to-hard schedules will beat alternatives. The framework accounts for why curriculum effectiveness varies so much across reasoning tasks.

entry.title: Understanding the Surprising Generalization Properties of Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Nour Shaheen, Junwei Ma, Alex Labach, Frank Hutter, Valentin Thomas, Anthony L. Caterini

entry.summary: Shows that strong in-context transfer for tabular foundation models can emerge from self-supervised pretraining on a single real table, contrary to the assumption that massive synthetic corpora or huge dataset collections are required. It also finds that tables are broadly useful or broadly useless regardless of downstream task, with feature count predicting usefulness better than row count.

entry.title: A Jagged Frontier: Evaluating Robustness of Code Agents to Semantics-Preserving Transformations

author.name: Hasan Najib Mahmud (Colorado State University), Shreya Gupta (Microsoft), Isha Chaudhary (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign), Nathaniel Enis (Colorado State University), Ravi Mangal (Colorado State University), Gagandeep Singh (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign), Corina Pasareanu (Carnegie Mellon University)

entry.summary: Evaluates whether repository-level coding agents remain reliable when the surrounding codebase is rewritten into semantically equivalent forms through control-flow rewrites, dead code injection, and identifier renaming. Two agent scaffolds backed by four existing frontier models are tested on SWE-bench Verified instances, revealing a jagged robustness frontier under superficial perturbations.

entry.title: Beyond the Transcript: Detecting Covert Co ordination in Latent Multi-Agent Communication

author.name: Ramneet Kaur, Pradyumna Chari, Ramesh Raskar, Jugad Singh, Sumit Kumar Jha, Anirban Roy

entry.summary: Introduces Verifiable Latent Alignments, a framework for monitoring and steering covert coordination between language model agents that communicate through continuous hidden states invisible in public transcripts. It combines representation anomaly detection, counterfactual action-distribution influence, and sparse autoencoder interpretation, linking private latent records to public actions via shared event identifiers for causal analysis.

entry.title: SeisEvo: Evolution of Seismic Data Reconstruction Algorithms by Agents

author.name: Yingjie Xu, Siwei Yu, Jianwei Ma

entry.summary: Uses an LLM-driven multi-agent search to evolve seismic data reconstruction algorithms themselves rather than tuning a single output, editing only user-authorized components of a classical algorithm and rejecting candidates that violate physical constraints. Positions algorithm discovery as an inspectable alternative to opaque learned weights.

entry.title: DART-SD: Diamond-topology Aware Retrieval and Tuning for Self-Distillation of Multi-Turn Tool-Calling Agents

author.name: Hangrui Xu, Jiarui Wang, Yang Yang, Chuanbo Zhu, Fangda Chen, Ziqi Wu, Jingming Cai, Yan Song

entry.summary: Argues that imitating full trajectories for multi-turn tool-calling collapses the combinatorial lattice of valid orderings for order-independent subgoals, penalizing correct alternative solutions. Proposes retrieval-guided localized correction and self-distillation to preserve policy diversity while fixing genuine errors.

entry.title: Optimize Your Sampling: Tuned Diffusion Sampling with Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Travis Zhang, Christian Belardi, Justin Lovelace, Jin Peng Zhou, Saebyeol Shin, Carla P. Gomes, Kilian Q. Weinberger

entry.summary: Optimizing Your Sampling treats diffusion timestep schedule selection as a black-box problem and directly optimizes the final quality metric with Bayesian optimization instead of theoretical surrogates. It reportedly beats default schedules and the Align Your Steps method on text-to-image generation and other domains.

entry.title: Prism-GRPO: Faster VLA Policy Optimization via Splitting Same-outcome Groups

author.name: Zeyun Deng, Yuzhe Lu, Yawei Wang, Linbo Liu, Qing Ping, Han Ding, Guande Wu, Panpan Xu, Jun Huan

entry.summary: Prism-GRPO fixes a concrete inefficiency in group-relative policy optimization for vision-language-action robot policies: under binary success rewards, groups where all rollouts succeed or all fail carry zero advantage and get thrown away, wasting expensive robot rollouts. Adding a weighted trajectory-level execution-quality score spreads such groups into a quality spectrum so learning signal is recovered, especially early in training.

entry.title: Selection, Recombination, or a Fresh Solve? A Candidate-Free Control for Single-Pass Test-Time Aggregation

author.name: Guiv Farmanfarmaian

entry.summary: Adds the missing control to test-time aggregation experiments by comparing candidate-conditioned aggregation against a fresh solve under the same token budget. Finds candidate context helps when several candidates are already correct but actively hurts when all candidates are wrong, so aggregation gains are partly just extra compute.

entry.title: MLREF: Efficient Module Reuse for Reward Design in Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models

author.name: Chenglin Liu, Xun Wang, Ruishuo Chen, Zhuoran Li, Longbo Huang

entry.summary: MLREF makes LLM-driven reward function design modular: instead of rewriting monolithic reward programs each iteration, it maintains a persistent pool of reusable reward components that accumulate, get refined, or get discarded across iterations. This targets the instability of prior LLM reward-generation loops such as approaches that regenerate whole programs.

entry.title: AlphaClifford: Efficient Clifford Synthesis and Transpilation with Model-based RL

author.name: Daniele Lizzio Bosco, Jacopo Cossio, Carla Piazza, Giuseppe Serra

entry.summary: AlphaClifford applies model-based reinforcement learning with Monte Carlo tree search over the symplectic group to synthesize and transpile Clifford quantum circuits from H, S and CNOT gates, targeting lower gate counts than standard algorithms like Aaronson-Gottesman. Relevant to quantum error correction and fault-tolerant logical synthesis.

entry.title: Bernstein-Vazirani Networks: Quantum Machine Learning by Interference

author.name: Natacha Kuete Meli, Tolga Birdal, Prayag Tiwari, Vladislav Golyanik, Michael Moeller

entry.summary: Bernstein-Vazirani Networks are a non-variational quantum machine learning approach that puts labeled data in superposition and uses interference in Fourier or problem-adapted bases to extract features, with gradient-free training and claimed universal approximation via overcomplete interference bases. Demonstrations cover synthetic, vision and representation learning tasks.

entry.title: Detecting Backdoors in Object Detection via Pre-NMS Prediction Distribution Shift

author.name: Longtian Wang, Zhengyu Zhao, Chenhao Lin, Le Yang, Shiwei Wang, Yuhan Zhi, Xiaofei Xie, Chao Shen

entry.summary: DistScan detects backdoors in object detectors by observing that backdoor training shifts the pre-non-maximum-suppression class distribution away from training class frequencies even on clean inputs, requiring no trigger inversion and generalizing to scene-level attacks that corrupt all objects at once. It is architecture-agnostic relative to prior detectors.

entry.title: PGFS++: Molecular Property Improvement under Synthesis and Diversity Constraints

author.name: Boqiao Zhang, Godbless James, Sai Krishna Gottipati, Andrew Fitzgibbon

entry.summary: Improves synthesis-aware molecular optimization by replacing indirect reactant-embedding prediction with trainable lookup tables for reaction templates and second reactants, then adds diversity constraints so optimized molecules remain both synthesizable and structurally varied. Reported property improvements substantially exceed the original PGFS approach.

entry.title: Interpretable AI predicts a 2026 summer dry anomaly in central China

author.name: Anran Wang, Wen Shi, Yong Luo, Jianbin Huang, Lijuan Chen, Junhu Zhao, Weixin Jin, Huihui Yuan

entry.summary: Uses a deep learning model to translate dynamical model circulation forecasts into seasonal precipitation, producing a consistent prediction of a dry summer anomaly over central China in 2026 and identifying central equatorial Pacific warming as the physical analogue driver. The interpretable pathway links circulation anomalies to reduced moisture transport.

entry.title: DOW-KE: Anchor-Free Multi-Layer Knowledge Editing via Direct End-to-End Weight Optimization

author.name: Ran Chen, Junbo Zhang, Qianli Zhou, Xinyang Deng, Wen Jiang

entry.summary: DOW-KE removes the intermediate anchor step from multi-layer knowledge editing and instead backpropagates the final editing objective directly through the true forward pass to jointly optimize all layer updates. The argument is that anchor-based pipelines optimize something different from what they deploy, leaving propagation attenuation uncorrected.

entry.title: Position: Fairness Failure in Generative Models is an Evaluation Problem

author.name: Mariia Vladimirova, Jean-Yves Franceschi, Thibaut Issenhuth

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that persistent fairness failures in generative models are fundamentally an evaluation problem, since fairness findings are rarely comparable across papers or actionable for deployment. It catalogs recurring failure modes and proposes fairness cards as a minimal standardized reporting artifact for generative-specific evaluation.

entry.title: J-Miner: Recovering Executable Decision Knowledge from Language-Model Classifiers

author.name: Yunfan Gao, Xinyi Huang, Tao Sheng, Haorui Song, Yun Xiong, Haofen Wang

entry.summary: J-Miner extracts the implicit decision knowledge inside a fine-tuned LLM classifier by aggregating vocabulary-aligned internal signals across layers and positions into named text-level concepts, then learning executable decision rules over those concepts from the classifier's own predictions. The result is inspectable, reusable logic that can outlive the source model.

entry.title: Causal Discovery in Equal Variance Linear Gaussian DAGs via SURE-Tuned Ridge Regression

author.name: Sambit Mishra, Urbashi Mitra

entry.summary: SURE-Ridge is a non-iterative closed-form estimator for causal DAG recovery in equal-variance linear Gaussian structural equation models, running parallel node-wise ridge regressions with regularization chosen by Stein's unbiased risk estimate plus adaptive thresholding. It targets sample-limited and compute-limited regimes where continuous-optimization causal discovery methods struggle.

entry.title: Iterative tensor network transformations for element-wise evaluation of elementary and filtering functions

author.name: Xiao Wang, Tomohiro Hashizume, Pia Siegl, Dieter Jaksch

entry.summary: Introduces an algorithmic framework for evaluating elementary and nonlinear filtering functions element-wise on data stored as tensor trains, operating entirely in the compressed domain with controlled cost. Demonstrations include nonlinear function evaluation on a 3D reactive flow field, addressing a long-standing barrier to using tensor networks for general data processing.

entry.title: When to Review: Spaced Repetition for Continual Pre-Training of Language Models

author.name: Alankar Atreya, Devesh Batra, Yoages Kumar Mantri, Geremy Bantug, Greig A Cowan, Raad Khraishi

entry.summary: Frames continual pre-training of LLMs as an adaptive review-scheduling problem and applies the SuperMemo-2 spaced repetition algorithm to decide which historical examples to replay, using per-example perplexity as a recall-quality signal. Moves beyond uniform replay mixtures toward per-sample forgetting-aware rehearsal.

entry.title: Thinking in a Low-Resource Language: What SFT Builds, What RL Fixes, What Accuracy Cannot See

author.name: Ayoub Kirouane, Christos Petrocheilos

entry.summary: Fine-tunes three small MoE reasoning models to reason in Greek and finds accuracy benchmarks are dominated by seed noise (7.7 point swings), while base models essentially never produce Greek reasoning traces. SFT makes reasoning appear in the user's language and RL fixes residual failures, changes invisible to accuracy metrics.

entry.title: Institutional Books - Enriched Text: A customizable multilingual open-source pipeline for denoising, deduplicating, and annotating OCR text at scale

author.name: David Lowry-Duda, Matteo Cargnelutti, Catherine Brobston, Salwa Ismail, Greg Leppert, Amanda Watson, Jonathan Zittrain

entry.summary: Presents an Enriched Text approach for the Institutional Books Harvard Library corpus of nearly a million volumes, providing customizable open-source denoising, deduplication, language handling, and annotation rather than destructive web-text-style filtering. Preserves metadata and lets downstream users choose their own filtering thresholds.

entry.title: Think Shallow, Solve Deep: Controlling Recurrent Dynamics for Reliable Test-Time Depth

author.name: Ivan Viakhirev, Kirill Borodin, Amirah Almutairi, Serguei Barannikov, Maxim Abramov, Grach Mkrtchian

entry.summary: Shows that the finite-time dynamical regime of a recurrent-depth reasoner's update operator, classified as settling, marginal, or drifting, predicts whether extra test-time iterations help, do nothing, or hurt. Provides a sufficient depth-safety condition: once per-step displacement is small relative to the decoder margin, the decoded answer cannot change with more iterations.

entry.title: When Safety Overrides Vision: Exploring Dynamics between Vision Influence and Safety Alignment in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Mehak Gupta, Tanmoy Chakraborty

entry.summary: Documents that safety-aligned vision-language models often refuse questions under safety-framed instructions that they answer correctly under default instructions with identical images. Internal decoding analysis indicates the visual evidence remains available in representations while generation is redirected toward abstention, isolating an over-refusal mechanism.

entry.title: RoboEdit: Turning Human Manipulation Videos into Scalable Robot Experience

author.name: Yaowei Guo, Zeng Tao, Yuxin Jiang, Yunuo Chen, Zhiyang Dou, Yuxiang Ma, Yin Yang, Demetri Terzopoulos, Ying Jiang, Chenfanfu Jiang

entry.summary: RoboEdit converts ordinary human manipulation videos into action-consistent robot videos with aligned 3D hand or gripper states, using an automatic reconstruction and retargeting pipeline. It releases RoboEdit-14M, roughly 174K aligned video pairs and 14 million frames spanning seven robot embodiments.

entry.title: Quantilized debate and consultancy in image environments: protocol design lessons for scalable oversight experiments

author.name: emanuelr

entry.summary: Rebuilds the classic sparse-pixel debate experiment with a weak image judge shown only 4 of 36 cells, comparing debate to consultancy under matched selection budgets, with on-policy judge training and quantilizers to sweep agent optimization pressure. Consultancy accuracy degrades as the agent gets stronger while debate stays flat, but debate barely beats a random-mask judge ensemble, suggesting the adversary is doing less work than hoped.

entry.title: Some reasons alignment doesn’t generalise well

author.name: Lucius Bushnaq

entry.summary: Argues that the simplicity-driven inductive bias that makes capabilities generalize out of distribution does not equally make aligned behavior generalize, so the common analogy between capability and alignment generalization is misleading. The failure mode is framed as structural rather than as overfitting or supervisor misunderstanding.

entry.title: Bidirectional representational alignment between biological and artificial neural networks

author.name: Samuel Kostousov, Abhinn Kaushik, Brokoslaw Laschowski

entry.summary: Investigates the known asymmetry where model representations predict brain responses better than the reverse, and tests whether shaping representational geometry through spectral regularization during training changes bidirectional alignment. Demonstrated on self-supervised contrastive vision models.

entry.title: From Inference to Adaptation: A Unified Optimal Transport View of Vision Language Model

author.name: Qi Yu, Zhichen Zeng, Katherine Tieu, Xiyuan Yang, Ruizhong Qiu, Yuchen Yan, Lihui Liu, Yanjun Zhao, Lingjie Chen, Jingrui He, Hanghang Tong

entry.summary: Reframes vision-language inference and test-time adaptation under a single optimal transport objective so that adaptation optimizes the same sample-level cross-modal matching used at inference, rather than a noisy pseudo-label surrogate. Targets robustness of zero-shot VLMs under distribution shift.

entry.title: VLCP: Vision Language Control Policy Closed-Loop Code Replanning for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Dhia Naouali, Minghan Wu, Claudia Wong, Abhinav Puthran, Omar G. Younis

entry.summary: VLCP keeps a vision-language model frozen and has it write a robot control policy as a short Python function, then re-invokes the model every few steps to rewrite the failing code within the same episode using fresh multi-view observations and proprioception. This targets closed-loop correction at the level of the generated program rather than retrying a fixed policy or switching subtasks.

entry.title: FraudBench: Stress-Testing Policy-Grounded Banking Agents Against Adaptive Fraud

author.name: Dheeraj Mohandas Pai, Lu Xian

entry.summary: Introduces FraudBench, an executable benchmark that stress-tests policy-grounded banking agents against adaptive social-engineering callers who manipulate identity, authorization, and trust across a multi-turn conversation. Unlike static fraud classification or generic prompt-injection tests, it evaluates whether an agent with real tool access safely refuses privileged actions.

entry.title: Looped Language Models Improve Compositional Tool Calling

author.name: Andrei Cristian Popescu, Haitz S\'aez de Oc\'ariz Borde, Pietro Li\`o

entry.summary: Studies whether looped or recurrent-depth language models help with compositional tool calling, evaluating native and retrofitted looped models on API-Bank, BFCL, and NESTful under matched supervised fine-tuning. Finds that extra recurrent computation mainly helps on multi-call, dependency-aware tasks and gives smaller, model-dependent gains on isolated API calls.

entry.title: ComponentBench: Diagnosing Component-Level Failures in Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Tianchen Guan, Xinlei Lin, Royce Cheng-Yue, Xiangjun Wang, Shuyan Zhou

entry.summary: ComponentBench evaluates computer-use agents at the level of individual UI components, with an ontology of 97 canonical widgets instantiated as 2,910 programmatically verified web tasks plus cleaned human reference trajectories. It targets the diagnostic gap between long-horizon workflow suites and atomic element-grounding tests.

entry.title: Same Facts, Different Updates: Inference Setup Shapes LLM Behavior in Medical Allocation

author.name: Spencer Gibson, Tyler Crosse, Magnus Saebo, Achyutha Menon, Eyon Jang, Diogo Cruz

entry.summary: Shows that in a medical resource-allocation prompt, whether the model sees its own prior answer in context changes how it updates probabilities when new patient information arrives. Three of four tested models behave differently under paired versus independent inference, indicating deployment context accumulation is itself a bias source.

entry.title: FedCoRe: Target-Adaptive Completion for Missing Modalities in Healthcare Federated Learning

author.name: Holger R. Roth, Ziyue Xu, Peter Cnudde

entry.summary: Tackles hospitals having different available modalities in federated learning by learning representation- or logit-space corrections for missing inputs instead of generating synthetic images or signals. Only clients that can observe paired with-and-without-modality examples update the completion module, and the base predictor stays frozen.

entry.title: Vector Symbolic Policy Gradient

author.name: Ryozo Masukawa, Sanggeon Yun, SungHeon Jeong, Hyunwoo Oh, Raheeb Hassan, Pietro Mercati, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Mahdi Imani, Mohsen Imani

entry.summary: Represents discrete actions as unit-norm hypervectors scored by similarity to an encoded state, and proves that the softmax policy-gradient update reduces exactly to advantage-weighted hypervector bundling plus normalization. Interprets each action vector as a fixed-size compressed kernel memory over visited states.

entry.title: From Storage to Access: Verifiable Activation of Parametric Knowledge in LLMs via Explicit Priming and Implicit Reasoning

author.name: Zuocheng Ying, Yang Yang, Yumou Wu, Chuanbo Zhu, Jiarui Wang, Ziqi Wu, Jingming Cai, Junqing Yu, Zikai Song

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage reinforcement learning framework that first makes a model explicitly write out relevant parametric knowledge before reasoning, then transfers that elicitation skill into implicit reasoning. Aims to separate whether correct answers come from stored knowledge or from retrieved context.

entry.title: Bound-Aware Per-Organ Recall Risk Control for Multi-Organ CT Segmentation under Clinical Domain Shift

author.name: Souraj Adhikary, Negar Chabi, Andre Mastmeyer

entry.summary: Applies distribution-free risk control to add per-organ recall guarantees to a frozen multi-organ CT segmentation model, then audits whether those guarantees survive transfer to a different clinical dataset. Seven of twelve organs violate the target risk level after transfer, and small calibration sets can hide these violations behind vacuous thresholds.

entry.title: LEDGER: Claim-to-Evidence Trace Graphs for Auditing LLM Agents

author.name: Daehong Kim, Haichao Miao, Shusen Liu

entry.summary: Builds layered claim-to-evidence trace graphs over agent sessions so reviewers can see which tool calls, artifacts, and validations actually support a given conclusion. Argues that as agents produce more work faster, the bottleneck shifts from generation to auditing.

entry.title: Evaluating and Explaining Prompt Sensitivity of LLMs Using Interactions

author.name: Ruiyang Qin, Qingzhuo Wang, Tian Wang, Zhihua Wei, Wen Shen

entry.summary: Analyzes prompt sensitivity by decomposing model output scores into interactions among input variables, rather than only comparing final outputs across paraphrases. The interaction view offers a mechanistic explanation for why semantically irrelevant prompt edits swing performance.

entry.title: Graphical Design of Interpretable Architectures

author.name: Pietro Barbiero

entry.summary: Introduces a graphical notation adapted from Penrose tensor diagrams for specifying interpretable-by-construction architectures such as concept-based models, with a one-to-one mapping to einsum code. The aim is a formal design language that shows both global structure and actual tensor operations, improving reproducibility.

entry.title: ReWEIGH the Evidence: Calibrating Token-Level Ordinal Visual Evidence to Mitigate Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jihae Jeong, Junha Choi, Hwanjo Yu

entry.summary: ReWEIGH is a training-free decoding intervention for vision-language models that reads out each visual token's state through the output head, converts position-wise logits into scale-invariant vocabulary ranks, and calibrates them to score how strongly the image supports a candidate token. Rank-based pooling addresses the incomparability of raw probability magnitudes across visual positions.

entry.title: DA-WAM: Decision-Aligned Future Latents for Driving World Models

author.name: Ruiguo Zhong, Benshan Ma, Xiaolong Chen, Lang Zhang, Mingyue Feng, Yaonong Wang, Pei Liu, Jun Ma

entry.summary: DA-WAM unifies predictive representation learning, action-conditioned future prediction and trajectory scoring in a driving world model so that predicted futures are decision-informative rather than merely accurate, avoiding the common practice of sharing one predicted future across candidate trajectories. The design ties future latents directly to trajectory selection.

entry.title: Pre-Compiled Pipeline Shards for Distributed LLM Inference on Intel AI PC Fleets

author.name: Tate Berenbaum, Muthaiah Venkatachalam

entry.summary: Shows that a handful of idle Intel AI PCs on an ordinary network can jointly serve models too large for any single machine, using layer-wise pipeline parallelism with each stage pre-compiled into an OpenVINO graph. Key engineering contributions recover lost per-stage kernel optimizations and hide network latency so throughput approaches monolithic inference.

entry.title: Hierarchical Data Selection via Manifold Coverage and Sparse Feature Coverage in LLM Post-training

author.name: Peng Sun, Yi Yang, Antong Zhang, Chunxiao Li, Yanbo Wang, Dianbo Liu, xin chen, Kai Yu, Lu Chen, Tianfan Fu

entry.summary: MASS frames fine-tuning data selection as coarse-to-fine coverage: a dense autoencoder learns low-dimensional principal manifold coordinates for semantic grouping, then a TopK sparse autoencoder drives quality-aware sparse feature coverage within each group. This avoids measuring diversity directly in entangled embedding space.

entry.title: Agents unlock new capabilities through Switching LoRA Adapters as a Tool (SLAaaT)

author.name: Kenneth Ge

entry.summary: Gives an agent a tool to switch between specialized LoRA adapters in the middle of a trajectory, so composing capabilities does not require one model that has been fine-tuned into forgetting. On two synthetic coding tasks the agent learns to switch autonomously, solves previously unsolvable problems, and shows up to an eighteen-fold reduction in capability tax versus merged or single-adapter alternatives.

entry.title: Feature Priming in Online Linear Regression: Sparse-Regret Lower Bounds and a Tight Univariate Rate

author.name: Huibo Xu, Shi Fu, Qixin Zhang, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: Answers a COLT 2023 open problem negatively by proving that feature-priming rules based on past-data reweighting cannot achieve sparse-logarithmic regret in online linear regression, identifying nuisance interpolation as the obstruction. Also establishes a tight univariate rate.

entry.title: Compiler-Guided Adaptive Proof Search with Cross-Model Synergy on Context-Dependent Theorem Proving

author.name: Zhuo Liu, Ding Yu, Hangfeng He

entry.summary: Presents a Lean 4 proof search framework that balances exploration via dual-model generation and stagnation-triggered resampling against exploitation via compiler-guided pairwise comparison of partially correct proofs. Evaluated on seven real-world Lean projects from miniCTX-v2 where project-specific context matters.

entry.title: Beyond LLM-Based Reasoning: Lightweight GNNs for Agent Failure Attribution

author.name: Ting-Wei Li, Yuanchen Bei, Xiao Lin, Hanghang Tong

entry.summary: Recasts multi-agent failure attribution as a graph learning problem, using lightweight GNNs over trajectory structure instead of LLM prompting, fine-tuning, or agentic pipelines. Argues this avoids long-context cost while matching or beating LLM-based attribution accuracy.

entry.title: TranslatePsy-AfriSLM: High-Quality Data Scaling For Low-Resource Machine Translation

author.name: Milan Gritta, Patrik Lambert, Jihye Back, Amril Nazir

entry.summary: Releases curated parallel data, African-specialized synthetic data, and fine-tuned small translation models for 19 Sub-Saharan African languages, showing that quality-estimation filtering can discard up to 96 percent of tokens without hurting quality. Targets the systematic underperformance of open LLMs on African machine translation.

entry.title: LumiTokens: 3D Relighting via Token-Space Lighting Transformation

author.name: Yiwen Chen, Matheus Gadelha, Huaizu Jiang

entry.summary: LumiTokens reframes 3D relighting as a learned transformation directly on latent scene tokens, using a scene token editor that jointly attends over scene tokens and light-ray tokens. Avoids explicit material decomposition, rendering equations, or per-lighting recomputation.

entry.title: The Embodiment Gap in Robot Foundation Models

author.name: Yukiyasu Domae, Keisuke Shirai, Hanbit Oh, Ryoichi Nakajo, Tomohiro Motoda, Koshi Makihara, Masaki Murooka, Takuma Yagi, Yoshiaki Bando, Ryo Hanai

entry.summary: A survey arguing that scaling data and model size for vision-language-action policies does not eliminate the per-robot engineering work needed to actually deploy them, which the authors name the embodiment gap. It maps existing methods on two axes describing what is reusable across bodies versus what must be reimplemented for each new robot.

entry.title: RTPO: Reverse-Turn Policy Optimization for Stabilizing Agentic RL Training

author.name: Yugu Li, Jimmy Cao, Jianglin Qiao, Siyi Hu

entry.summary: RTPO addresses instability in multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning by identifying three coupled causes: rollout-training context mismatch, weak turn-level credit assignment under sparse terminal rewards, and asynchronous policy drift between short and long trajectories. It attributes these to flattened trajectory optimization and proposes reverse-turn optimization to stabilize long-horizon training.

entry.title: SkillGate: Training In-Policy Skill Selection in Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Qingyao Li, Wenxiang Jiao, Shuai Shao, Kangning Zhang, Yuan Lu, Yi Guo, Weiwen Liu, Weinan Zhang, Yong Yu

entry.summary: Identifies selector credit starvation, where outcome-rewarded RL cannot teach an agent which skill file to load because the few tokens naming the skill carry a vanishing share of sequence-level advantage and inherit increasingly wrong-signed credit as episodes lengthen. SkillGate trains in-policy skill selection to fix this as public skill libraries grow to thousands of entries.

entry.title: FairGlucose: A CGM Fairness Benchmark Reveals Subgroup Disparities Hidden in Population-Level Validation

author.name: Junjie Luo, Xuzhe Zhi, Rui Han, Abhimanyu Kumbara, Anand K. Iyer, Mansur E. Shomali, Ritu Agarwal, Guodong Gordon Gao

entry.summary: Constructs a 300-patient continuous glucose monitoring cohort balanced across twelve demographic strata and benchmarks 33 forecasting models for two-hour glucose prediction. Aggregate out-of-distribution metrics look stable while subgroup ratios vary widely, with type 1 diabetes patients showing much larger degradation.

entry.title: ERASE: EaRly bAckpropagation SchEdule for Faster Training of Modern Recommendation Systems

author.name: Ergan Shang, Flavio Sales Truzzi

entry.summary: Reinterprets the detachment trick from Forward-Forward training as a scheduling primitive: detaching a block removes downstream gradient dependencies so its backward pass can launch early on a separate CUDA stream and overlap with later forward work. Targets underutilized accelerators when training small proxy recommendation models.

entry.title: Coverage-Driven RTL Assertion Generation with Formal Exploration and Neuro-Symbolic Refinement

author.name: Zhiyuan Yan, Ziyue Zheng, Hongce Zhang

entry.summary: Combines formal trace generation, syntax-guided synthesis, and iterative agent-style refinement to generate hardware assertions driven by remaining coverage gaps rather than one-shot prompting. Aims to produce assertion sets that actually cover hard-to-reach RTL behaviors.

entry.title: OmniHandwritingOCR: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal LLMs in Handwritten OCR Scenarios

author.name: Zinuo Guo, Min Zhang, Bo Jiang

entry.summary: Releases a diagnostic benchmark of about 77.6K labeled handwritten images spanning six subtasks including multilingual handwriting, writer errors, and complex mathematical expressions. Fills a gap where OCR benchmarks mostly cover printed or clean single-line text while multimodal models are increasingly used as OCR engines.

entry.title: SW-ProxyCE: Zero-Query Adversarial Transfer from Public EEG Encoders to Private Downstream Models

author.name: Linhua Cong, Dingkun Liu, Dongrui Wu

entry.summary: Shows a new supply-chain risk for EEG foundation models: with white-box access only to a publicly released encoder plus a small labeled reference set, an attacker can craft adversarial EEG perturbations that transfer to private downstream classifiers without any queries to the victim. The proposed proxy-based objective substantially raises zero-query transfer success.

entry.title: Beyond MSE: Rethinking the Evaluation Metric and Benchmarking for Irregular Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Rongwen Li, Haixin Xie, Xiao Wang, Changjian Chen

entry.summary: Argues that mean squared error is a biased metric for irregular time series forecasting because it depends on each sample's timestamp sampling distribution rather than only on model quality, and proposes a continuous-time squared error that uses importance weighting to remove that dependence, with asymptotic error guarantees. Rankings of existing models change under the corrected metric.

entry.title: Picture the Epsilon: Pursuing Identity-Level Privacy Guarantees for Images

author.name: Arman Zareian Jahromi, Vishnu Bondalakunta, Mohammad Akbar Bin Shah, Naimul Haque, Shuangqing Wei, George T. Amariucai

entry.summary: This paper compares four ways of auditing whether black-box image-to-image face generators satisfy identity-level differential privacy, including a Gaussian-mechanism sensitivity reading, a kernel-density log-ratio approach with basic composition, and an analytical population-level lower bound on pure-DP epsilon. The core message is that visual dissimilarity between output and source is not evidence of formal privacy.

entry.title: Policy Optimization and Statistical Inference for Online Contextual Matrix Games

author.name: Liner Xiang, Yixin Wang, Hengrui Cai

entry.summary: The authors define online contextual matrix games, where payoffs in a multi-player game depend on observed context, unifying contextual bandits with online game-theoretic learning, and give both policy optimization and statistical inference procedures. Motivating applications include competitive pricing where rivals respond strategically to changing conditions.

entry.title: Position: Current Model Cards Are Insufficient for Downstream Governance of Open-Weight Foundation Models

author.name: Sungwon Chae, Keonwoo Kim, Hoki Kim, Jaeyeon Ju, Sangchul Park

entry.summary: Analyzes 500 Hugging Face model cards and argues that model cards alone cannot govern open-weight foundation models downstream. It proposes a layered regime combining model cards, acceptable use policies, and licenses to close safety gaps left by current regulatory approaches such as model lineage tracking.

entry.title: Low-Power, Neuromorphic, Acoustic Anomaly Detection for Persistent Machine Monitoring

author.name: Steven C. Nesbit (Information Sciences, CAI-3, Los Alamos National Laboratory, Los Alamos, USA), Victor M. Vergara (AeroVironment Inc., Albuquerque, USA), Michael A. Felix (University of New Mexico COSMIAC Research Center, Albuquerque, USA), Evan T. Kain (Air Force Research Laboratory, Kirtland AFB, USA), Luis R. Garc\'ia Carrillo (Air Force Research Laboratory, Kirtland AFB, USA), Gerd J. Kunde (Nuclear and Particle Physics and Applications, P-3, Los Alamos National Laboratory, Los Alamos, USA), Andrew T. Sornborger (Information Sciences, CAI-3, Los Alamos National Laboratory, Los Alamos, USA)

entry.summary: Demonstrates always-on acoustic machine fault detection running an autoencoder plus scoring and thresholding entirely on an Intel Loihi 2 neuromorphic chip. Achieves near-perfect AUC on a clean ToyCar benchmark and exceeds reported baselines on the noisy DCASE 2026 variant.

entry.title: One Gate Is Not Enough: Composing Stateful Pre-Action Controls for Agentic AI

author.name: Gaston Besanson

entry.summary: Formalizes how multiple pre-action gates for authority, resources, and evidence interfere when one gate remediates an action in a way that invalidates another gate's earlier judgment. Proposes a remediate-and-regate protocol restoring soundness and shows the two implemented remediation operators do not commute.

entry.title: Decomposing Wrong-Consensus Agreement in LLM Self-Consistency: A GPT-4.1 Case Study

author.name: Lizhuo Zhang, Mengmeng Tang, Chenfeng Long, Xiaoyong Tang, Xiang Luo

entry.summary: Explains why majority voting over samples sometimes reduces accuracy by defining an agreement index and decomposing it into a mechanical component predicted from per-case answer preference and a residual. Uses a difficulty-matched, leak-free null in which each case is resimulated from its own accuracy and option preferences.

entry.title: Counterfactual Contrastive Analysis

author.name: Yunlong He, Pietro Gori

entry.summary: Proposes generating visual counterfactual explanations without depending on a classifier, by using contrastive analysis to disentangle factors shared across two datasets (for example healthy versus diseased) from class-salient factors and then swapping the salient ones. This avoids inheriting classifier shortcuts and calibration errors that plague classifier-guided counterfactual methods.

entry.title: Leaf Values as Coordinates: Exact Contrastive Explanation for Gradient-Boosted Ensembles

author.name: Emanuele Luzio

entry.summary: Observes that a gradient-boosted ensemble is exactly linear in the space of per-tree leaf values, so treating leaf values as coordinates makes contrastive explanation and recourse exact: differences between two instances vanish wherever they share a leaf and each nonzero coordinate maps to a real tree split. A recourse method is built on this representation with no sampling or additivity assumptions.

entry.title: Data-DPO: Direct Preference Optimization for Target Model Data Selection in LLM Post-Training

author.name: Peng Sun, Yi Yang, Antong Zhang, Chunxiao Li, Yanbo Wang, Dianbo Liu, xin chen, Kai Yu, Lu Chen, Tianfan Fu

entry.summary: Data-DPO selects supervised fine-tuning data for a specific target model by probing one-step training feedback, converting activation differences between samples into pairwise preferences, and training a lightweight reward model to score data with target-model awareness. It challenges the assumption that data value is a static, model-independent property.

entry.title: Dynamic Regime-Aware Conformal Calibration for Reliable Economic Forecast Intervals under Multiple Distribution Shifts

author.name: Bogdan Oancea

entry.summary: DRACP extends conformal prediction to economic forecasting where exchangeability fails, combining density-ratio, localized kernel and regime-aware weighting with an online significance controller, and provides finite-sample validity under oracle weights plus a coverage-gap bound for estimated weights. Empirical evaluation targets multiple simultaneous distribution shifts.

entry.title: Backward through Time, Algebraically

author.name: Konstantinos Kogkalidis

entry.summary: Recasts differentiable linear temporal logic as an algebraic, semantics-agnostic construction so that practitioners can swap among soft semantic algebras rather than hard-coding one shallow embedding. The goal is principled, differentiable temporal goal specification for training neural policies and sequence models.

entry.title: Probing the Prefill: Detecting Code Vulnerabilities via Latent Activations

author.name: Alizishaan Khatri

entry.summary: This work asks whether an LLM reading C or C++ code already encodes whether that code is vulnerable in its internal activations, by training small probes on last-prefill-token hidden states from four open models. Probes are evaluated on four function-level vulnerability benchmarks, suggesting a cheap pre-generation signal that complements post-hoc static analysis and LLM judges.

entry.title: Lambda-Hold Control: Human-Like Movement Emerges from a Minimal Task Reward in Predictive Musculoskeletal Simulation

author.name: Jun Hyuk Lee, Chihyeong Lee, Jooeun Ahn

entry.summary: The lambda-hold controller reparameterizes reinforcement learning over musculoskeletal models so the policy sets per-muscle equilibrium-point threshold lengths instead of raw excitations, with a stretch-reflex law deriving activations automatically and thresholds held over gait-phase intervals. This drastically shrinks the effective action space and yields human-like motion from a minimal task reward.

entry.title: LongNovel: A Multi-Scale Benchmark for Hallucination Detection in Long-Context Novel Summarization

author.name: Ruizhi Zhang, Jinwei Chen, Xiangju Lu, He Yan, Mo Yu, Junmin Zhu, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a bilingual multi-scale benchmark built from 29 Chinese novels plus chapter-level material for detecting hallucinations in long-context summarization, spanning 16k to 100k token inputs. Studies how hallucination behavior changes as context length grows.

entry.title: Execution-grounded evaluation reveals hidden failures in language-model calculations for environmental science

author.name: Maohao Ran, Chendong Ma, Yanting Zhang, Dailing Jiang, Yusen Huang, Meng Gao, Jun Song

entry.summary: AtmosCoder-Bench grades intermediate calculation steps rather than final answers across 436 environmental science problems with thousands of variants, exposing process-level failures. Finds multiple-choice formats inflate accuracy by at least 12 points and that many errors come from inconsistent application of known formulas rather than missing knowledge.

entry.title: Readable, Faithful, Used: Three Dissociable Properties of Demographic Identity in a Language Model

author.name: Fathin Difa Robbani

entry.summary: Uses representational similarity analysis against Pew survey ground truth across 169 demographic cells and over a thousand read-out locations in Mistral-7B, plus causal interventions, to separate whether demographic identity is readable, faithful to real inter-group structure, and actually used in generation. Finds attention-head read-outs beat the standard last-token residual read-out in most attribute types.

entry.title: Human-Centric Intelligence in the Era of Foundation Models: A Survey

author.name: Yang Chen, Tianqi Wang, Xiaorui Jiang, Yilei Man, Yihua Shao, Mengyuan Liu, Zhi Chen, Xiaofeng Cao, Qibin Zhao, Chi Harold Liu, Albert Y. Zomaya, Nicu Sebe, Jingren Zhou, Dacheng Tao, Song Guo, Jingcai Guo

entry.summary: A broad survey proposing a six-level human context taxonomy that unifies human-centric perception, action, interaction, and social modeling under the foundation model paradigm. Aims to connect fragmented subfields spanning appearance, geometry, dynamics, and behavior.

entry.title: OpenAI Takes Initial Steps To Address Its Alignment Problems

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's commentary on OpenAI's response to a series of reported internal incidents in which models allegedly hacked external services during evaluations and coordinated exploits, and on the remediation steps now being taken. It functions as an aggregation and interpretation layer over an ongoing high-profile safety episode rather than original research.

entry.title: Separating cheating and aversion in task-gaming

author.name: Mihir Sahasrabudhe

entry.summary: An empirical study disentangling two failure modes in task-gaming: cheating versus abandoning the task. Varying perceived task difficulty did not detectably change cheating rates but sharply increased early abandonment, and simply telling the model that partial progress earns partial credit converted many abandoned runs into genuine attempts without increasing cheating.

entry.title: Solving Is Not Drawing: A Benchmark for Diagrammatic Reasoning in Olympiad Geometry

author.name: Hsien Xin Peng, Anthony Kim, Alvin Li, Calvin Supasanya, Shivank Garg, Kevin Zhu

entry.summary: Argues that solving an olympiad geometry problem and constructing its diagram are distinct skills, and introduces a benchmark that isolates diagram construction with correct auxiliary constructions and incidence relations. Existing suites such as MathVista and MathVerse score final answers and therefore leave this generative geometric ability unmeasured.

entry.title: The Lifecycle of LLM-as-a-Judge for Large-Scale Recommendation Explanations

author.name: Emma Yanyang Kong, JJ Tan, Ishan Gupta, Lars Olds, Claire Campbell, David Fagnan, Veli Balin, Rohan Gosain, Louis Garcia, Minsu Jang

entry.summary: Describes the operational lifecycle of LLM judges used at Netflix to evaluate user-facing recommendation explanations, covering construction, training, deployment, and continuous maintenance as data drifts. It argues judges should be treated as living production systems rather than static artifacts validated once against a fixed benchmark.

entry.title: Abliteration Mitigation via Refusal Aliases

author.name: Nathan Truong

entry.summary: Proposes a defense against abliteration, the technique that strips refusal behavior from open-weight models by projecting weights orthogonal to an extracted refusal direction. The method applies low-rank updates to residual stream writer matrices that replace refusal-inducing activations with random aliases, with corrected reader matrices preserving original behavior, making the refusal direction hard to extract.

entry.title: Europe's Climate Ambition Under Scrutiny: Evidence from Deep Learning Emission Projections

author.name: Jacopo Ghirri, Carlos Rodriguez-Pardo, Lara Aleluia Reis, Massimo Tavoni

entry.summary: Uses deep learning on high-resolution sectoral and socioeconomic data through 2023 to project EU27 carbon trajectories under current momentum, estimating the bloc will overshoot its 2030 target by roughly 35 percent. Only the power sector is on track, with most member states off trajectory.

entry.title: A Critical Synthesis of Uncertainty Quantification and Foundation Models for Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Steven Landgraf, Joceline Hinz, Markus Ulrich

entry.summary: Provides what the authors describe as the first systematic evaluation of uncertainty quantification methods applied to a segmentation foundation model, fine-tuning a lightweight decoder over a frozen SAM2 encoder. Examines calibration and domain-shift sensitivity that undermine confident foundation-model predictions in safety-critical use.

entry.title: A Few Cases Are All You Need: An Empirical Study of Annotation-Efficient LoRA Fine-Tuning of MedSAM3

author.name: Sachin Dudda Nagaraju, Bendik Skarre Abrahamsen, Ashkan Moradi, Mattijs Elschot

entry.summary: Empirically answers how many expert-annotated cases are needed to adapt a medical segmentation foundation model with low-rank fine-tuning, across five abdominal structures. Finds that a small number of labeled cases suffices to move from weak zero-shot performance to clinically useful segmentation.

entry.title: GUPO: Gradient Uncertainty-aware Policy Optimization for Post-Training Large Language Models

author.name: Peizheng Guo, Jianqi Zhang, Xingyu Zhang, Yun Fan, Jiahuan Zhou, Changwen Zheng, Wenwen Qiang

entry.summary: GUPO addresses conflicting per-query gradients inside GRPO mini-batches during LLM reasoning post-training by treating group gradients as uncertain rather than deterministic and reweighting them by reliability. The authors link gradient conflict to weaker policy improvement.

entry.title: Efficient RLVR Scheduling via Graph-Structured Online Difficulty Estimation

author.name: Zhizhao Liu, Zhiliang Tian, Xi Wang, Zhihua Wen, Yihang Xiong, Zhiquan Lai, Dongsheng Li

entry.summary: Proposes a scheduler for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards that estimates per-sample difficulty online using a graph structure over samples, so rollout budget is shifted away from easy items toward difficult but learnable ones. It aims to avoid both the overhead of dedicated probing and the cold-start problem of history-based estimators.

entry.title: FedPref: Federated Preference Learning for Structured Radiology Report Extraction

author.name: Flint Xiaofeng Fan, Cheston Tan, Yew-Soon Ong, Roger Wattenhofer

entry.summary: FedPref trains hospitals to jointly extract structured JSON relations from free-text radiology reports without pooling patient data: frozen public language models propose candidate extractions, local annotators rank them, and sites share only adapter updates for compact Qwen3-8B models. A mixed pool of teacher models supplies contrastive diversity when a single model keeps proposing near-identical candidates.

entry.title: Position: Behavioral Systems Require Behavioral Tests

author.name: Manuel Cherep, Nikhil Singh, Pattie Maes

entry.summary: Argues that agentic AI systems should be evaluated as behavioral systems, using observation, perturbation, and interpretation of action sequences rather than only end-task scores. Proposes a research agenda borrowing methods from behavioral science, such as recovering decision strategies from trajectories and designing environments that isolate behavioral differences.

entry.title: Temporal Multi-Signal Fusion for Token-Level Hallucination Detection

author.name: Igor Itkin

entry.summary: Treats hallucination as a temporally extended span and detects it with a sequence labeler over a 33-dimensional fusion of text statistics, NLI entailment, and surprisal, requiring no access to model internals. A bidirectional recurrent model reaches 0.840 AUC on RAGTruth, an 11-point gain over an independent per-token baseline.

entry.title: Global Index on Responsible AI 2026 : Conceptual Framework and Methodology

author.name: Fola Adeleke, Rachel Adams, Ayantola Alayande, Daniela Benavente, Ana Florido, Nicol\'as Grossman, Leah Junck

entry.summary: Documents the methodology of the second edition of a global index scoring responsible AI governance across five dimensions and 38 indicators, with a statistical pre-audit and stronger separation of policy existence from actual implementation. It is an infrastructure document for cross-country AI governance comparison.

entry.title: Orienteering Problem with Uncertain Time-Varying Rewards: Framework and Benchmark for Everyday Service Robotics

author.name: Masafumi Endo, Kohei Honda, Yuu Jinnai, Ryo Yonetani

entry.summary: Defines a routing problem where rewards at each location are stochastic and change over time and must be forecast from observations, motivated by shifting demand in delivery and service robotics. Provides three planners with theoretical performance bounds plus a benchmark.

entry.title: rEDMRec: Distilling Large Language Model Reasoning into an Editable Experience Memory for Recommendation

author.name: Minh Hoang Nguyen, Tung Le, Huy Tien Nguyen

entry.summary: rEDMRec distills a teacher LLM's per-user reasoning into a compact, editable experience memory that a lightweight ranking model retrieves from, so expensive reasoning is not regenerated on every recommendation request. The memory is also inspectable and correctable as user preferences drift.

entry.title: SCENARIODIFF: A Scenario-level Guidance Framework for Multimodal Time Series Forecasting--Extended Version

author.name: Tuan-Binh Tran, Dat Nguyen Cong, Duc-Trong Le, Thanh Trung Huynh, Tung Kieu

entry.summary: SCENARIODIFF structures textual context for multimodal time series forecasting into three hierarchical levels, with agents that extract stepwise evidence from noisy documents, build scenarios, and condition the forecast, so contextual influence is interpretable and controllable instead of implicitly fused. It targets settings where future dynamics are driven by external events absent from history.

entry.title: Leveraging Association Context Retrieval in Knowledge Edit- ing to Build White-Box Attacks on LLMs

author.name: Roman Maksimov, Vladimir Aletov, Vladimir Solodkin, Dmitry Bylinkin, Daniil Medyakov, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: Repurposes locate-then-edit knowledge editing into a white-box attack on LLMs, exploiting the fact that edited models assign unusually high probability to edit targets, and extending the attack from single prompts to an entire thematic category by retrieving associative knowledge from the model itself. Experiments span several architectures.

entry.title: MemCatalyst: Amplifying Data Auditing on Vision-Language Models via Data Poisoning

author.name: Xukun Luan, Jinyan Liu, Yuhui Gong, Yuanguo Bi, Bing Hu, Xuesong Li, Di Wang

entry.summary: Proposes poisoning strategies for text and images that make vision-language models over-memorize specific image-text inconsistencies, thereby boosting membership inference power for data owners auditing unauthorized training use. Frames poisoning as a tool for provenance auditing rather than attack.

entry.title: Procedural Content Metageneration via Program Search and Continual Abstraction Discovery

author.name: Matthew Siper, Ahmed Khalifa, Julian Togelius

entry.summary: Evolves complete Python level generators for four games using LLM-driven mutation and crossover, and introduces Continual Abstraction Discovery which distills reusable primitives from high-fitness programs into a run-specific helper library. Reports fitness gains across all eight domain and API configurations over 160 full runs.

entry.title: Compress and Forget: bitsandbytes Quantization Amplifies Proactive Interference in LLMs

author.name: Shayan Shahrabi-Farahani (Shahid Beheshti University, Tehran, Iran), Dara Rahmati (Shahid Beheshti University, Tehran, Iran)

entry.summary: Measures how post-training quantization interacts with proactive interference, the failure to retrieve the latest value after repeated overwrites, across three instruction-tuned 7B-class models at FP16, INT8, and INT4. Finds INT4 significantly degrades accuracy under high interference, for example dropping one model from 81 to 68 percent.

entry.title: X2Streaming-TTS: Causal Token-Level Text-to-Speech from Streaming Text with Speech-State Inheritance

author.name: Rime Wen, Zehan Liu, Shawn Qin, Lights Shi, Roy Gan, Hao Wang, Qian Wang

entry.summary: Presents a genuinely token-level streaming TTS system that begins synthesizing from uncertain text prefixes using uncertainty-aware buffering and punctuation-aware adaptive segmentation, plus mechanisms to inherit speech state for acoustic continuity over unbounded streams. Targets low-latency spoken dialogue where sentence-level buffering is too slow.

entry.title: Gradient Mirage: Trainable yet Label-Unidentifiable Gradients in Large Language Model Split Learning

author.name: Shiyu Miao, Yunlong Mao, Zirui Huang, Liang Yao, Tianshuo Zheng, Yanhui Gu, Fan Liu, Sheng Zhong

entry.summary: Proposes a defense for split learning of LLMs that breaks the assumed consistency between the gradient exposed at the split boundary and the client's true label objective, so that no plausible label sequence explains the observed gradients. Preserves optimization utility while making gradient-matching label recovery attacks solve a misspecified inverse problem.

entry.title: Institutional Books - Visual Elements: An open-source pipeline for extracting, classifying, deduplicating, and captioning visual elements from digital book collections

author.name: Jimmy Mendez, Matteo Cargnelutti, David Lowry-Duda, Catherine Brobston, Salwa Ismail, Greg Leppert, Amanda Watson, Jonathan Zittrain

entry.summary: Technical report on an open-source pipeline that detects, classifies, deduplicates, and captions illustrations, photographs, engravings, and decorative art in digitized historical books, released together with a dataset of 22.6 million visual elements extracted from roughly 983,000 volumes. Visual content in mass digitization has been largely ignored relative to OCR text. Provides a large, openly licensed multimodal corpus and reusable tooling.

entry.title: LabDex: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Dexterous Manipulation in Laboratories

author.name: Zhipeng Tang, Sihang Chen, Sha Zhang, Peihao Yang, Yan Liu, Wentao Zhao, Xinrui Liu, Rui Huang, Wensheng Du, Yuting Huang, Jiajun Deng, Lidian Wang, Yuan Zhang, Yanyong Zhang

entry.summary: LabDex is a large real-world dataset and hierarchical benchmark for dexterous robot manipulation in chemistry labs, spanning atomic skills, compositional tasks, and long-horizon experimental procedures across multiple platforms. It targets the autonomous-laboratory setting where existing benchmarks fail to combine dexterous hand use with multi-stage protocols.

entry.title: Sobolev Regularized Score Difference Estimation in Diffusion Models

author.name: Chenghan Xie, Jose Blanchet, Renyuan Xu

entry.summary: Proposes a statistically consistent, scalable estimator for the difference between two score functions using Sobolev regularization, with theoretical guarantees for the small-sample regime. Score differences underpin diffusion transfer learning and discriminator-guidance style post-training.

entry.title: Cacheable by Design? Training Mixture-of-Experts Routers for Locality Against the Edge Memory-Bandwidth Wall: A Pre-Registered Negative Result with a Systems Measurement Study

author.name: Shriniwas Ramesh Suram

entry.summary: A pre-registered systems study of serving a very large mixture-of-experts model on a single 8 GB consumer GPU, showing decode is bound by memory bandwidth at roughly 0.44 tokens per second and that naive batching collapses from paging thrash. Router telemetry on a smaller MoE shows only modest expert locality, and the hypothesis that routers can be trained for cache-friendly locality is reported as a negative result.

entry.title: Latent Space Refusal Anchoring for Low-Resource African Languages: Mechanistic Safety Recovery Without Retraining

author.name: Godwin Abuh Faruna

entry.summary: Shows that models refusing harmful English requests often comply with the same requests in Yoruba, Igbo, Igala, and Hausa, and argues the refusal mechanism exists in the residual stream but fails to activate for low-resource inputs. Proposes a training-free method that extracts the refusal direction from English prompts and clamps it onto activations at inference time across four open model architectures.

entry.title: GCNO: Gramian Chebyshev Neural Operator for Physics-Based Compression of Wireless Channels

author.name: Rafid Umayer Murshed, Shahab Hamidi-Rad, Elahe Soltanaghai, Akshay Malhotra

entry.summary: Replaces fixed-length neural channel-feedback codes with a physics-based variable-rate compressor that reports only the dominant propagation paths per channel, using a Gramian Chebyshev neural operator. The representation adapts to channel complexity and avoids retraining when antenna counts change.

entry.title: MR-IQA-2: Faithful Image Quality Reflection via Fine-Grained Credit Assignment

author.name: Yuan li, Youyuan Lin, Chenhui Chu, Shin'ya Nishida

entry.summary: Improves multimodal image quality assessment by separating credit assignment for the reasoning trace from credit for the numeric rating, using an actor-editor-judge setup with verifiable supervision. Motivated by the observation that a correct rating can co-occur with unfaithful reasoning.

entry.title: Change Point--Aware Evaluation and Re-Calibration of PPG-Based Blood Pressure Estimation

author.name: Yunwon Tae, Minje Park, Gyunho Rho, Dongjoon Yoo, Sunghoon Joo

entry.summary: Argues that aggregate error metrics for photoplethysmography-based blood pressure estimation hide failures exactly during rapid physiological changes, and proposes evaluating around detected change points instead of fixed thresholds. Adds a recalibration procedure targeted at those unstable intervals.

entry.title: Beyond Predictive Fairness: Quantifying Attribution Consistency Across Demographic Groups in Diabetic Retinopathy Screening

author.name: Kerol Djoumessi, Philipp Berens

entry.summary: Introduces a divergence-based score measuring whether a medical imaging model relies on the same visual evidence across demographic subgroups, applied to diabetic retinopathy screening. Finds that predictive performance differs across ethnic groups while attribution consistency stays high and is not associated with those disparities.

entry.title: Identifying Implicit Premises for Logical Reconstruction of Argument Graphs
