author.name: Xuyao Feng, Anthony Hunter

entry.summary: Proposes a neuro-symbolic pipeline where LLMs generate candidate implicit premises for enthymemes, which are then translated into logical formulae and checked with a theorem prover to establish entailment or contradiction between statements. This bridges NLP argument mining and symbolic abduction for reconstructing argument graphs.

entry.title: Rethinking Irregular Time Series Forecasting from the Perspective of Basis Functions

author.name: Rongwen Li, Changjian Chen

entry.summary: Revisits basis-function approaches to irregular time series forecasting, identifying a non-vanishing asymptotic bias when timestamp sampling density is ignored and a lack of adaptability in predefined bases, and proposes a formulation that corrects both. It targets healthcare and meteorological settings with sparse, non-uniform observations.

entry.title: No Gaussian Required: Contrastive Inverse Dynamics for JEPA World Models

author.name: Jack Boylan, Chris Hokamp

entry.summary: Argues that JEPA-style world models do not need a Gaussian-matching regularizer to prevent representation collapse, and instead proposes an action-contrastive masked transition objective where the anti-collapse pressure comes from distinguishing real transitions using action information. It is positioned directly against the SIGReg mechanism used in recent latent world models.

entry.title: Composing Flow-Matching Energies with Known Physics: Generation, OOD Detection, and Inversion on PDE Fields

author.name: Yixuan Sun, Anirban Samaddar, Sandeep Madireddy

entry.summary: Shows that flow matching models with a potential-induced velocity field give an explicit scalar energy at every transport time whose gradient is the learned score, effectively yielding trainable energy-based models without an intractable partition function. The additive energy structure then allows composing the learned prior with known PDE physics at inference for generation, OOD detection, and inversion on physical fields.

entry.title: Information Spreading in Diffusion Models from Effective Field Theory

author.name: Navonil Neogi, Nabil Iqbal

entry.summary: The authors apply effective field theory from physics to convolutional score-matching diffusion models, arguing that locality as an inductive bias makes field-theoretic tools appropriate for describing denoising dynamics. They show that mutual information between image locations grows as a simple Brownian-motion effective theory predicts, on a toy model and on MNIST.

entry.title: Temporal Leakage in Financial News NLP: A Multi-Architecture Audit with a Regime-Specific M&A Signal

author.name: Chenhao Xue, Raslen Guesmi, Siwei Feng, Yucheng Gong, Jacob Xavier Sundram, Jordan Pang, Lan Wang, Julian Kaljuvee

entry.summary: An audit of nearly fifty thousand financial news articles across sixteen feature-model combinations shows that random rather than chronological train-test splits inflate correlation-based performance by factors of roughly one to six, with larger models leaking more. Only merger and acquisition news survives as a genuine regime-specific predictive signal once leakage is controlled.

entry.title: SPACE: Sample-cloud Predictive Adaptive Conformal Ellipsoids for Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Baishi Li, Kelvin J. L. Koa, Ke-Wei Huang

entry.summary: SPACE is a conformal calibration wrapper for probabilistic multivariate time-series forecasters that builds prediction ellipsoids from the geometry of the current forecast sample cloud rather than from a fixed window of past residuals. This makes coverage guarantees more responsive to distribution shift and avoids contamination from stale regimes.

entry.title: JSL-DC: A Word-Level Japanese Sign Language Dataset with Linguist-Derived Descriptions for Distinguishing Confusable Signs

author.name: Ken Takaki, Asuka Ando, Misa Suzuki, Uiko Yano, Masaya Tsujimoto, Bill Neubauer, Ananay Vikram Gupta, Rose Shao, Matthias Hoppe, Sahir Shahryar, Celeste Mason, Kai Kunze, Yohei Oseki, Yoshihiro Kawahara, Thad Starner

entry.summary: Introduces JSL-DC, the largest Japanese Sign Language dataset by video count (36.7K videos, 19 Deaf signers, 270 words) with a lexicon chosen by Deaf and Coda linguists for parent-child communication and linguist-derived descriptions to disambiguate confusable signs. The Deaf-centric collection process and multi-signer coverage target generalization to new users. Directly enables sign language learning tools for hearing parents of deaf children.

entry.title: Position: Multi-Agent Systems Should Prioritize Concurrency Control

author.name: Xin Yang, Letian Li, Zimo Ji, Terry Jingchen Zhang, Wenyuan Jiang

entry.summary: Reframes many LLM multi-agent failures as classical concurrency bugs: agents read and write shared state while long inference windows create stale reads, lost updates, and inconsistent outcomes. It argues frameworks should adopt explicit conflict detection, isolation guarantees, and structured resource access as first-class design elements.

entry.title: FinSkillBench: Evaluating AI Agents and Domain Skills for Investment Management

author.name: Jermyn Zhen Yong Bek, Zhuang Qiang Bok, Zhongtian Sun

entry.summary: Introduces FinSkillBench, an evaluation suite with 12 subtasks and 2,603 episodes covering portfolio construction, risk management, and fundamental analysis for investment management agents. Each episode supplies point-in-time inputs, hidden ground truth, and a task-specific verifier, and compares agents with no skills, curated skill packs, and other conditions.

entry.title: FACET: Preserving Source Intent and Executable State in Terminal Task Synthesis

author.name: Kou Shi, Zun Wang, Qisheng Su, Shiting Huang, Ziao Zhang, Zhen Fang, Qingnan Ren, Jin Liu, Yu Zeng, Yiming Zhao, Lin Chen, Zehui Chen, Feng Zhao

entry.summary: FACET is a framework for synthesizing executable terminal-agent training tasks that keeps the instruction, initialized environment, reference solution, and verifier mutually consistent. It reconstructs source material into coherent skills to avoid unsolvable or wrongly graded tasks that arise when multi-stage synthesis discards dependencies and state transitions.

entry.title: Preference Reasoning under Indeterminacy in Large Language Models

author.name: Hadi Hosseini, Samarth Khanna, Xiyuan Wang

entry.summary: Formalizes preference reasoning under indeterminacy for LLM agents along epistemic axes (incomplete or partially expressed preferences) and structural axes (no solution exists under standard social choice concepts). Across a task hierarchy, state-of-the-art models are shown to struggle when correctness is not well defined rather than merely hard.

entry.title: A Theory of Post-hoc Debate Judgement

author.name: Xiang Yin, Adam Dejl, Antonio Rago, Lihu Chen, Francesca Toni

entry.summary: Develops a formal theory of post-hoc debate judgement, applicable wherever agents argue by presenting pros and cons and an external LLM judge determines the outcome. It defines properties such as reproducibility, robustness, and groundedness that judges may be required to satisfy, then tests judges against them.

entry.title: Robust Risk Under Evolving Uncertainty: A Wasserstein Counterpart of the Entropic Value-at-Risk

author.name: Deep Kumar Ganguly, Jan K\v{r}et\'insk\'y

entry.summary: Introduces a Wasserstein counterpart of the entropic value-at-risk for agents learning under model uncertainty, replacing the relative-entropy ambiguity ball with an optimal-transport ball. This allows the risk measure to hedge against catastrophes the nominal model assigns zero probability, which entropic measures provably cannot reach.

entry.title: Self- and Other-Labels Induce Bidirectional Bias in LLM Judges

author.name: Songeun Chae, Min Kim, Donghoon Jung, Seojin Choi, Seohyon Jung

entry.summary: Disentangles genuine self-preference in LLM judges from stylistic confounds by having ten models evaluate narrative constraint selections that carry no model-specific writing fingerprint but retain a recoverable model signature. Blind and labeled conditions produce distinct results, revealing bidirectional bias from both self-labels and other-labels.

entry.title: TTSD-FAR: Test-Time Self-Distillation with Fisher-Anchored Restoration for Missing-Modality Emotion Recognition in LVLMs

author.name: Muhammad Haseeb Aslam, Alessandro Koerich, Marco Pedersoli, Ali Etemad, Eric Granger

entry.summary: Handles missing or noisy modalities at test time in large video-language emotion recognition by combining self-distillation with a Fisher-information-anchored restoration step, since entropy-minimization test-time adaptation does not transfer to autoregressive models. Addresses partial observation as a distribution shift with no ground-truth supervision.

entry.title: Physics-Unrolled Neural Operator for Wireless Field Modeling

author.name: Rafid Umayer Murshed, Saif Ur Rahman, Mingyue Tang, Elahe Soltanaghai

entry.summary: Predicts high-fidelity indoor radio maps from cheap low-fidelity inputs using a three-stage physics-unrolled neural operator cascade, explicitly handling the residual Monte Carlo noise in affordable finite-ray training labels. Aims to avoid expensive full simulations for coverage planning and localization.

entry.title: The Role of Grid Cells in Reducing Spatial Aliasing in Hippocampal Place Representations

author.name: Alexander Johnson, Obadah Ghizawi, Ali A. Minai

entry.summary: Shows in a computational hippocampus model that adding grid cell inputs disambiguates locations whose boundary-derived sensory patterns are otherwise identical, reducing spatial aliasing from environmental symmetry. Supports the view that internally generated periodic codes complement geometry-driven inputs.

entry.title: The Impact of CutMix on Reliability and Robustness in Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Steven Landgraf, Markus Ulrich

entry.summary: Isolates the effect of the widely used CutMix augmentation on segmentation calibration, uncertainty quality, and robustness rather than only accuracy, across a CNN and a transformer architecture. Motivated by evidence that semi-supervised methods built around CutMix can degrade reliability.

entry.title: From Threat Intelligence to Detection: Knowledge-driven Enrichment and Template-based Rule Grounding for Automated Sigma Rule Generation

author.name: Sepehr Ghaffarzadegan, Boubakr Nour, Makan Pourzandi, Mourad Debbabi, Chadi Assi

entry.summary: Presents an automated pipeline that converts cyber threat intelligence reports into platform-independent Sigma detection rules, using knowledge-driven enrichment plus template-based grounding to keep generated rules syntactically valid and deployable across SIEM systems. It targets the scaling bottleneck of manual rule authoring against fast-evolving APTs.

entry.title: Detecting and Discriminating Operator Misspecification in Hybrid PDE-Parameter Learning: a Reference-Free Instrument, with Discrimination Bounded In Sample

author.name: Eric Fock

entry.summary: Constructs a reference-free statistical instrument that, from a single fit and without ground truth, distinguishes whether a hybrid PDE-plus-parameter estimator has the wrong operator from the case where the parameter is simply unidentifiable. Pre-registered thresholds and controlled experiments on a parabolic inverse problem show high sensitivity to misspecification and silence under mere non-identifiability.

entry.title: Study-Strategy Clusters from EdNet Logs Track Engagement, Not Mastery

author.name: Qingchuan Lyu, Yingxin Li, Albert Yang

entry.summary: Tests the common learning-analytics assumption that unsupervised clusters of tutoring-system logs correspond to learner types predictive of learning, using EdNet logs from 5000 learners with a bootstrap-stable hierarchy of eight study strategies and a temporal split of early behavior versus later outcomes. Early strategy clusters predict later engagement but not mastery.

entry.title: Delta2Gamma: Band-Wise Adaptive Contrastive Learning of EEG for Alzheimer's Disease Detection

author.name: Chanwoo Park, Chanwoo Kim

entry.summary: Delta2Gamma is a self-supervised EEG framework for Alzheimer's screening that decomposes each recording into the five canonical frequency bands, gives each band its own encoder, projection head and adaptively predicted contrastive temperature. The motivation is scalable, low-cost dementia screening from noisy, weakly labeled EEG.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Reward Specification and Benchmark Reliability in GRPO-based LLM Unlearning

author.name: Rub\'en Balbastre, Juan Manuel Ordu\~na, Mariano P\'erez

entry.summary: An empirical study of how reward design shapes GRPO-based LLM unlearning, comparing lexical suppression, anti-refusal shaping, rubric-based broad answering, and refusal contrast, with and without supervised warm-up. It highlights an underspecified third behavior: answering target-adjacent questions at a general level rather than leaking, evading, or refusing, and questions whether standard forget-score benchmarks measure real unlearning.

entry.title: The concentration game: Bayesian updating, regret, and information

author.name: Akshay Balsubramani

entry.summary: A theoretical paper casting online learning as a zero-sum game between a learner and nature, where the game value simultaneously yields Bayesian updating, exact exponential-weights regret accounting, and a variational form underlying many concentration inequalities. Gibbs or Bayes weights appear as the unique equalizing strategy, with log-partition functions serving as value functions.

entry.title: Teach and Grow: An Agent-Centered Architecture for General Robot Learning

author.name: Chang Nie, Zhe Liu, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: Teach-and-Grow Learning proposes an agent-centered alternative to monolithic vision-language-action models: a multimodal agent converts a handful of successful demonstrations into reusable closed-loop Skill Blocks, so novel objects or embodiments can be handled by composing skills rather than by collecting data and retraining. The paper frames the recurring cost of policy updates and regression testing as a retraining tax.

entry.title: High-Flux Count-Free Single-Photon 3D Cameras

author.name: Kaustubh Sadekar, Vivek K Goyal, David Maier, Atul Ingle

entry.summary: Shows that compressive acquisition schemes for single-photon avalanche diode 3D cameras, while solving the data bandwidth bottleneck, worsen dead-time and pile-up distortion because the photon detection history is discarded. The authors develop a high-flux, count-free approach that reconciles compressive capture with distortion correction. Relevant for practical deployment of single-photon LiDAR in bright conditions.

entry.title: SoftVTBench: A Deformation-Aware Visuo-Tactile Dataset and Benchmark for Deformable-Object Manipulation

author.name: Bowen Jing, Mingxin Wang, Ruiyang Hao, Chenchen Ge, Hanwen Shen, Junjie He, Yang Cui, Yiming Hou, Weitao Zhou, Jiawei Wang, Minglei Li, Dandan Zhang, Ding Zhao, Houde Liu, Xiaofan Li, Si Liu, Ping Luo, Haibao Yu

entry.summary: SoftVTBench provides 4,000 expert demonstrations with synchronized multi-view RGB, dual-finger tactile images and marker motion, proprioception, and language for deformable-object manipulation, including rigid twins of deformable assets. It scores physical interaction quality such as slip and excessive compression rather than only task success.

entry.title: The Deontic Gap: Large Language Models and the Modal Language of Obligation

author.name: Daniel Hart, Sarah Allred, Joseph Abbas, Morenike Alugo

entry.summary: Compares deontic modal usage such as must and should in AI-generated text against contemporary human corpora and historical Ngram baselines across eleven models. Finds LLMs consistently underuse positive obligation modals, patterning more like formal published prose than present-day speech.

entry.title: TokenPowerSandbox: Evidence-Gated CPU-First Screening for Energy-Aware LLM Serving

author.name: Chenxu Niu

entry.summary: Introduces an energy-aware LLM serving workflow that uses a cheap CPU-resident projector plus short GPU probes and evidence gating, with frozen models and pre-declared holdouts to prevent overfitting energy predictions. Reports roughly 6 to 7 percent energy prediction error on a single H100 vLLM deployment.

entry.title: Discretizing Continuous Time Series for Imputation with Masked Diffusion Training

author.name: Dongbin Kim, Seungyun Lee, Geonwoo Shin, Jaewook Lee

entry.summary: MDTIM reframes time series imputation as masked discrete diffusion: values are discretized, a MASK token keeps missing entries structurally separate from observations, and the model predicts original values directly instead of predicting added noise. This addresses two limitations of continuous diffusion imputers.

entry.title: Benchmarking Classical and Transformer-Based Models for Document Sensitivity Classification

author.name: Aleesha Zainab, Muhammad Ahmed Khalid, Faheem Ullah Khan, Asifullah Khan

entry.summary: Benchmarks classical and transformer models for classifying organizational document sensitivity and highlights label leakage, where residual classification markers inside documents let models exploit surface shortcuts and inflate reported accuracy. The authors release a curated dataset designed to remove these shortcuts.

entry.title: EMAN: Optimization-Driven Capacity Growth through Path Emergence in Multi-Task Learning

author.name: Chenlei Fang, Jingchen Li, Hongzong LI, Qingyao Li, Yixuan Zhang, Huarui Wu, Haobin Shi, Chunjiang Zhao

entry.summary: EMAN proposes a multi-task network that begins as a single computation path and instantiates a new independent path only when persistent optimization evidence (surfaced through latent relative phases and multiple decision signals) indicates capacity is needed, rather than expanding at task boundaries or on conflict signals. It targets structural over-specification in multi-task architectures.

entry.title: MultiSigBERT: Beyond Survival Analysis through Multimodal and Sequential Modeling in Oncology

author.name: Paul Minchella, St\'ephane Chr\'etien, Guillaume Metzler, Lo\"ic Verlingue, R\'emi Vaucher

entry.summary: MultiSigBERT performs multimodal sequential survival modeling in oncology by converting free-text clinical reports into sentence embeddings and combining them with numerical and structured variables using path signature representations of patient trajectories. It aims to exploit temporal dynamics that single-modality survival models ignore.

entry.title: From Abductive Explanations to Global Logical Rules for Node Classification in SGCs

author.name: Bryan Lima Cavalcante, Thiago Alves Rocha

entry.summary: Extracts global logical rules explaining node classification in simple graph convolution networks by first computing minimal abductive explanations per node and using them as an intermediate representation, rather than deriving rules from explanatory subgraphs that carry node-specific redundancy. The claim is more general and compact rules.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning as (Discrete) Potential Theory

author.name: Christopher Connolly

entry.summary: Reviews and develops the correspondence between reinforcement learning under a fixed policy and discrete potential theory, suggesting this lens could yield better sample efficiency and formal constraints, with a sketch of extension to the nonlinear (policy-improvement) case. It is largely a conceptual and expository contribution.

entry.title: rl-triton: High-Performance Triton GPU Kernels for Reinforcement Learning Credit Assignment

author.name: Lars Simon Zehnder

entry.summary: An open-source Triton kernel library that recasts seven RL credit-assignment estimators (GAE, V-Trace, Retrace, TD-lambda, discounted returns, eligibility traces, prefix sums) as a single first-order linear recurrence solved by a parallel associative scan in logarithmic depth. Algorithm-specific coefficients are fused on-chip.

entry.title: A Constant-Competitive Algorithm for Dynamic Mixture-of-Experts Serving

author.name: Ian D'Ambrosio (Nth Research Collective)

entry.summary: A theoretical result on dynamic mixture-of-experts serving, the problem of deciding which expert replicas to hold on GPUs as request patterns shift. The author proves the randomized competitive ratio is constant, improving on a prior square-root-log bound, using a reduction to chasing convex bodies with sparse covering constraints.

entry.title: Margin-Regularized Structured Semantic Alignment for Brain-Language Correspondence

author.name: Jiaqi Wang, Huawen Hu, Shu Zhang

entry.summary: MD-SigLIP aligns brain recording embeddings with text embeddings in a shared space using a margin-regularized contrastive objective, so decoding becomes retrieval rather than free generation. The motivation is to separate genuine neural signal from content that a language model simply invents, which is a persistent credibility problem in brain-to-text work.

entry.title: Lymphocyte Mimicry Correction via Region-Level Tissue Reasoning and Unbalanced Optimal Transport

author.name: Xiang Li, Yuqi Wang, Casey C. Heirman, Jihye Heo, Kyle J. Lafata

entry.summary: Loki-OT resolves cell-type confusion in pathology images by taking density priors that a multimodal LLM infers from surrounding tissue regions and propagating them down to individual cell predictions through unbalanced optimal transport. It bridges cell foundation models, which lack context, and pathology MLLMs, which cannot operate per cell.

entry.title: Reflex-Guard: A Low-Latency Guardrail for LLM Prompt Safety Using Dense Semantic Embeddings

author.name: Istiaque Ahmed, Afia Anjum Borsha, Ranat Das Prangon, Abu-fuad Ahmad, Thi Hong Tran

entry.summary: Proposes a locally-run prompt safety guardrail using compact sentence embeddings and a bank of fast binary classifiers, targeting sub-100ms latency versus the several hundred milliseconds typical of LLM-judge or cloud moderation APIs. Also avoids sending user prompts to external moderation endpoints.

entry.title: Toward the Optimal Regret-Instability Trade-off in Multi-Armed Bandits

author.name: Kaifei Wang, Yinyu Ye, Han Zhong

entry.summary: Formalizes a trade-off between worst-case regret and allocation instability across independent bandit runs, proving a finite-time lower bound on their product and introducing a tunable UCB variant that traces the frontier. Instability is defined as the largest standard deviation of terminal arm pull counts.

entry.title: MAVEN: A Macro-Societal Value Evaluation Framework of Multimodal Content with Compact Aligned Evaluators

author.name: Zijuan Zhao, Zheren Fu, Hou Xia, Licheng Zhang, Yi Liu, Zhendong Mao

entry.summary: MAVEN is a hierarchical framework with 6 primary dimensions and 72 indicators, grounded in human-rights instruments and cultural value theory, for evaluating whether multimodal content aligns with macro-societal values. Includes a human-verified benchmark and compact aligned evaluator models with soft-match scoring.

entry.title: Stability-Aware Feature Design for Robust Watermark Detection in Machine-Generated Text

author.name: Sina Mansouri, Mohit Marvania, Abolfazl Safikhani

entry.summary: Proposes a watermark detection score that combines global and local z-statistics with run-length higher-order statistics, autocorrelation, and stability across successive paraphrases. Targets the known degradation of watermark detectors on short and repeatedly paraphrased text.

entry.title: Efficient INT8 Inference of Small NLP Models on Server CPUs with PyTorch Native Stack

author.name: Weiwen Xia, Yuxin Cui, E Cao

entry.summary: Integrates SmoothQuant into TorchAO and optimizes the resulting INT8 CPU inference path through TorchInductor graph fusion and kernel selection across oneDNN, AVX512_VNNI, and AMX backends. Reports up to 5.8x end-to-end throughput speedup on BERT-family encoders with negligible accuracy loss.

entry.title: Learning What to Fail On: Failure-Mode Contextual Bandits for Adversarial Data Curation

author.name: Roie Kazoom, Ofir Cohen, Rami Puzis, Asaf Shabtai, Ofer Hadar

entry.summary: Frames adversarial training-data curation as a contextual bandit over clustered failure modes, where a policy learns which failure types to sample for retraining based on validation rewards balancing robustness gains, forgetting, and cost. Candidate examples come from retrieval-augmented generation filtered by an LLM judge ensemble.

entry.title: Structure, Association, and Decision Value: Representation-Based Difficulty Estimation for Adaptive Inference in African-Language NLI

author.name: Toheeb Ogunade

entry.summary: Tests whether internal representation statistics can serve as example-level difficulty signals for adaptive inference in NLI across 15 African languages, and reports a negative result. Also documents that the English configuration of AfriXNLI shares 1,047 of 1,050 examples verbatim with XNLI evaluation data, invalidating it for XNLI-trained checkpoints.

entry.title: Comment-level Topic Drift Analysis in the Reddit Corpus

author.name: Steven Morse, Daniel Runfola, Trenton W. Ford

entry.summary: Applies embedding-based dynamic topic modeling to 12.7 billion Reddit comments from 2006 to 2022 to quantify semantic drift at the comment rather than document level. Contributes scalability modifications and a null model comparison test to filter spurious apparent dynamics.

entry.title: To Go Far, Go Together: Diverse Preferences Induce a Curriculum for Reward Optimization

author.name: Taehyung Kim, Jongeun Choi

entry.summary: Argues that accurate per-user reward models are insufficient for fair alignment because some users' rewards are simply harder to optimize from the initial policy, creating a new underserved group. It shows a diverse user population can induce a natural curriculum that makes hard-to-optimize preferences reachable.

entry.title: Diffusion Models for High-Dimensional Clustered Data: Intrinsic-Dimension Adaptivity via Bayesian Classification

author.name: Yuga Iguchi, Paul Fearnhead

entry.summary: Analyzes diffusion models on high-dimensional data made of multiple clusters each with its own low-dimensional structure, interpreting denoising as a dynamical Bayesian classifier over mixture components. Results connect phase-transition style qualitative accounts of denoising with quantitative adaptivity to intrinsic dimension.

entry.title: 34% of the US public is now aware of AI xrisk, and the curve is steepening

author.name: otto.barten

entry.summary: Reports a longitudinal open-ended survey series finding that 34 percent of a US sample spontaneously names AI among their top three human extinction risks, up from 7 percent in late 2022, with the fastest jump in the most recent interval. The method avoids leading questions by asking respondents to list extinction risks unprompted.

entry.title: A circuit prior in NN-bayes

author.name: Kaarel

entry.summary: Slides from a talk establishing that Bayesian learning over neural networks, even when arbitrarily overparameterized, carries an implicit circuit prior under certain prior scalings, so functions implementable by small circuits are learnable from little data. The deck also lists open problems in neural network learning theory.

entry.title: Natural Language Transcoders

author.name: anwenh

entry.summary: Proposes natural language transcoders, which extend natural language autoencoder ideas by verbalizing the difference between the input and output of a stack of transformer layers into a text explanation, then reconstructing that delta from the explanation alone. The aim is automatic natural-language descriptions of multi-layer computation rather than single-activation features.

entry.title: Safety Alignment Illusion: The Cross-Lingual Safety Gap in LLMs

author.name: Namya Bhatnagar

entry.summary: Documents that English-centric safety alignment leaves non-English inputs comparatively unprotected, producing stereotype-reinforcing outputs in Indian languages and in spoken dialogue settings. Introduces INCLUDE, a multilingual benchmark quantifying Indian-centric sociocultural bias and cross-lingual safety failure.

entry.title: Can a Lightweight Multimodal Model Estimate LLM Reasoning Performance? A Study for Compute-Optimal Document Inference

author.name: Zishan Ahmad, Vishal Vaddina

entry.summary: Introduces BudgetDoc, a multimodal benchmark that supervises model-budget-performance trade-offs on document tasks, and DRB, an approximately one-billion-parameter pre-flight estimator that predicts which model and reasoning budget will suffice. Dynamic allocation matches or beats always-maximum-budget baselines in most tested configurations while cutting inference cost.

entry.title: Competence, Not Accuracy: A Diagnostic for Reference-Free Judge Gates in Skill Optimization

author.name: Chenle Chen, Yangbo Wei, Chao Yao, Shaoqiang Lu, Junhong Qian, Chen Wu, Lei He

entry.summary: Asks whether a reference-free LLM judge gate carries usable signal before it is placed in a skill-optimization loop, formalizing the judge as a latent solver whose evaluation capacity is bounded by its own ability to solve the task. This yields a closed-form diagnostic predicting when judge scores separate correct from incorrect answers, extending text-space skill optimization beyond verifiable-reward tasks.

entry.title: Metrics That Write Themselves: Evolving an Evaluator from Its Own Blind Spots

author.name: Xing Zhang, Yanwei Cui, Guanghui Wang, Zhihao Lin, Peiyang He

entry.summary: Evolves an automatic evaluator as a pool of small Python operators that each flag one named defect or abstain, then vote, targeting domains such as report generation where no reliable metric exists. Direct prompting yields highly redundant operators, so EvalCEGAR imports counterexample-guided abstraction refinement from program verification to search for cases the current pool cannot distinguish.

entry.title: Nine Emotion Centroids: A Label-Free Valence Axis That Transfers Across Four Modalities

author.name: Yousef Radwan

entry.summary: Finds a single internal valence direction in frozen encoders using only nine emotion category names and about fifty short narratives each, roughly 1,500 fewer labels than supervised probing. The same top principal direction recovers most supervised sentiment performance and appears in vision, audio, and human-brain encoders that were never jointly trained.

entry.title: Composed Historical Image Retrieval by Modeling Temporal Representations

author.name: Adri\`a Molina Rodr\'iguez, Oriol Ramos Terrades, Josep Llad\'os Canet

entry.summary: Learns image representations that explicitly decompose a temporal dimension from other visual content, so historical photo collections can be retrieved by composed queries mixing content and time. Argues that constraining embeddings to a single temporal axis would cost too much expressiveness, so the temporal factor is separated instead.

entry.title: Intercepting the Kangaroo: Experimental Astrolinguistics with Constructed Lexicons, Active Probing, and Large Language Models as Informants and Hypothesis Proposers

author.name: Francesco Cordella, Mauro Cappelli

entry.summary: Turns speculative astrolinguistics into an experimental setup: two LLMs are given deliberately incompatible constructed lexicons (one encoding shape, color and motion, another fusing color with motion and lacking shape) and a scripted orchestrator must align their category systems. Across hundreds of runs the authors operationalize translation indeterminacy as a silent misreference failure mode and test protocols that mitigate it.

entry.title: Position: AI Leaderboards Are Underserving the Global South: A Case Study from India

author.name: Sourav Banerjee, Saikat Saha

entry.summary: Contends that AI leaderboards fail Global South users not from a lack of regional benchmarks but from an absence of independent governance, conflict-of-interest rules, and metric evolution mechanisms. It uses India as a case study and points to existing suites such as IndicSUPERB, MILU, IrokoBench, and AlGhafa that leaderboards do not incorporate.

entry.title: Adversarial Review: Structured Disagreement for Grounded Agentic Code Review

author.name: Eric S. Qiu, Joyce Gill

entry.summary: Proposes Adversarial Review, a minimal three-role coding protocol where a main agent works with a reviewer and a critic that audits the review through structured disagreement before edits are made. It reports the highest pass rate among tested configurations on LiveCodeBench while avoiding the overhead of large agent teams.

entry.title: Performance Drift Detection in Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS) for IoT Environments

author.name: Deepak Kanneganti, Sajib Mistry, Sheik Mohammad Mostakim Fattah, Erik Elmroth, Aneesh Krishna, Monowar Bhuyan

entry.summary: Proposes a drift detection framework for clients of cloud ML APIs who cannot see internal data or parameters, using a surrogate extraction model to track when service behavior or data distributions change. Targets IoT deployments where both data drift and silent provider updates degrade performance.

entry.title: Epistemic Subordination: Generative AI and the Infrastructure of Knowledge

author.name: Gilad Abiri, Emanuel V. Towfigh

entry.summary: Legal and theoretical argument that generative AI does not merely emit biased outputs but installs the dominant culture's way of knowing as the default infrastructure of knowledge, absorbing minority epistemologies while structurally subordinating them. Traces implications across several legal domains where discrete bias audits would be inadequate.

entry.title: SIDScope: A Diagnostic Resource for Semantic-ID Interfaces in Generative Recommendation

author.name: Jiandong Ding, Huijie Qin, Tiandeng Wu, Yi Cao

entry.summary: Provides diagnostic tooling for semantic-ID mappings that connect item tokenizers to generative recommenders, checking provenance, coherence, structural properties, and how generated code paths resolve to real items. Evaluated across nine tokenizer exports from seven families on Amazon and Yelp data.

entry.title: Understanding Multilingual Medical ASR Adaptation Through Layer-Wise Analysis

author.name: Souranil Kahali, Rituparna Bose, Abner Hernandez, Tomas Arias-Vergara, Andreas Maier, Ning Ma, Paula Andrea Perez-Toro

entry.summary: Analyzes how fine-tuning Whisper models for multilingual medical speech recognition reshapes encoder representations, comparing zero-shot, English-only, German-only, staged, and joint bilingual adaptation via layer-wise probing. Goes beyond word error rate to characterize where in the encoder adaptation actually happens.

entry.title: Mr.Dec: Daily-Scale Longitudinal Multimodal Modeling for 30-Day Readmission Prediction

author.name: Minjun Kim, Jong Hak Moon

entry.summary: Mr.Dec predicts 30-day hospital readmission by modeling each admission as a chronological sequence of daily multimodal events, feeding day-level electronic health record updates and imaging or note signals into a transformer decoder instead of compressing history into a static vector. Daily granularity is intended to capture evolving clinical risk.

entry.title: Deep Learning for Cross-Border Electricity Price Forecasting: A Comparative Study

author.name: Hadeer Elashhab, Sai Srijan Papineni, Marvin Dorn, Veit Hagenmeyer, Benjamin Sch\"afer

entry.summary: A comparative study of deep learning models for day-ahead electricity price forecasting across multiple interconnected markets using public data, motivated by the absence of standardized benchmarks that makes progress claims in this field hard to verify. The authors aim for a reproducible evaluation framework rather than a new architecture.

entry.title: How smoothing the affinity matrix affects neighborhood preservation in t-SNE

author.name: Shirin Mohebi, Guillaume Bied, Jefrey Lijffijt

entry.summary: Studies how sharpening or smoothing the t-SNE affinity matrix via a row-wise power transform affects neighborhood preservation at different scales, showing the transform is equivalent to rescaling Gaussian bandwidths while preserving sparsity and rank order. This gives practitioners a principled knob for local versus global structure.

entry.title: Physics-Informed and Hybrid Machine Learning in Additive Manufacturing: Application to Fused Filament Fabrication

author.name: Berkcan Kapusuzoglu, Sankaran Mahadevan

entry.summary: Compares three ways to inject physics knowledge into deep networks predicting bond quality and porosity in fused filament fabrication: physics constraints in the loss, simulation outputs as extra inputs, and pretraining on simulation before updating with experimental data. The study quantifies which hybridization strategy best enforces physical consistency with limited experimental data.

entry.title: CORAM: Coherent Orthogonal Rotation for Model Merging

author.name: Xinyi Sui, Ziran Liu, Nam Ling, Wei Wang, Wei Jiang

entry.summary: CORAM merges finetuned expert models by slicing weight matrices into rows, expressing each expert slice via SVD in the base model frame, and averaging the resulting factors on their respective manifolds with an amplification term to counteract shrinkage. It targets the limitation that linear weight arithmetic and single orthogonal transforms cannot capture update geometry.

entry.title: Wasted large language models: A life cycle thinking approach

author.name: Erik Johannes Husom, Maria Emine Nylund, Ophelia Prillard

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that efficiency gains in language models are being eaten by rebound effects (Jevons paradox) and proposes treating models as products with a life cycle, applying the EU waste hierarchy of prevention, reuse, recycling, recovery and disposal to model development. It reframes sustainability from per-inference energy metrics to governance of model proliferation.

entry.title: CTIFoundry: An Agent-Native Corpus Scaffold for Cyber Threat Intelligence

author.name: Yutong Cheng, Changze Li, Qian Cui, Wei Ding, Lingzhi Wang, Yan Chen, Peng Gao

entry.summary: Argues that the bottleneck for agentic cyber threat intelligence is the corpus substrate rather than model capability, since threat reports are still packaged as opaque chunks behind embedding indexes. CTIFoundry builds an agent-native scaffold that materializes a deterministic ontology graph across CVE, CWE, CAPEC, and related knowledge bases for multi-step investigation.

entry.title: Language Models for Portuguese: A Systematic Mapping Study

author.name: Jhessica Silva, Carlos Caetano, Helena Maia, Breno Bernard Nicolau de Fran\c{c}a, Sandra Avila, Helio Pedrini

entry.summary: A systematic mapping of the Portuguese language model ecosystem, consolidating scattered information from papers, technical reports, and model repositories into one survey of models and data resources. It documents how multilingual coverage remains uneven across languages.

entry.title: Formal Verification of Romanov's Triplet Logic: A Verified Filter for Sliding-window 3-CNF with Application to Structured Formulas

author.name: Dmitry V. Alexandrov

entry.summary: Provides the first machine-checked formalization in the Rocq proof assistant of a triplet-based combinatorial framework originally motivated by Boolean satisfiability, verifying its core structures and a clause-by-clause encoding for a sliding-window fragment. The verified result is a sound filter for structured formulas rather than a general SAT breakthrough.

entry.title: GrabVG: Graph-Attentive Binding for Visual Grounding in UAV Imagery

author.name: Chaowei Wang, Yan Di, Jingjun Sun, Baozhe Liu, Jiaxu Tian, Yuheng Li, Guangqian Guo, Shan Gao

entry.summary: GrabVG tackles referring-expression grounding in UAV bird's-eye imagery, where many small, similar and densely packed objects create visual redundancy and topological ambiguity, by adding graph-attentive binding that exploits spatial topology among candidate instances. Reported gains focus on crowded aerial scenes.

entry.title: Causal Local States: Scalable Simultaneous Causal Network Inference and Forecasting for Dynamical Systems

author.name: Jonas Braun, Fabian Fischbach, Daniel K\"oglmayr, Sebastian Baur, Christoph R\"ath

entry.summary: Causal local states jointly infers an approximate Granger-causal interaction network and forecasts dynamics, selecting a per-node neighborhood instead of relying on one global threshold or fixed neighborhood size. This is designed for heterogeneous coupled dynamical systems where a single hyperparameter cannot fit all nodes.

entry.title: Picard Proximal Monte Carlo for Parallel Bayesian Imaging with Score-Based Generative Priors

author.name: Deliang Wei, Evan Bell, Wenhan Guo, Yifan Chen, Yu Sun

entry.summary: PiX-MC parallelizes posterior sampling for Bayesian imaging inverse problems by combining proximal Langevin dynamics with Picard iteration, exposing parallelism across time discretization nodes for multi-GPU execution. It leverages the fact that many imaging likelihoods have cheap proximal operators.

entry.title: SGHA: Evidence-Grounded Research Problem Discovery with Local Language Models

author.name: Sarvesh Gharat, Junpei Komiyama

entry.summary: Presents a pipeline for generating research problems using locally hosted language models with explicit evidence grounding, motivated by auditability and confidentiality concerns with proprietary frontier models. Aims to make the evidential basis of AI-generated hypotheses inspectable rather than opaque.

entry.title: Artifact-centered Claim-aware Observability for Autonomous Scientific Agents

author.name: Xiangyu Yin, Ming Du, Michael H. Prince, Mathew J. Cherukara

entry.summary: Argues that logging model calls is insufficient for auditing autonomous scientific agents and proposes observability centered on artifacts and the claims they support, plus the relations among them. Motivated by failures that are distributed across evidence, candidate selection, and plan changes.

entry.title: Figurative and Cultural Knowledge in LLMs: Investigating Cross-Domain Transfer through Fine-Tuning

author.name: Mena Attia, Mona Diab, Thamar Solorio

entry.summary: Tests whether fine-tuning on cultural data improves figurative language understanding and vice versa across four models and six Arabic datasets covering proverbs, poetry, and cultural commonsense. Finds poetry tuning yields a small but statistically significant idiom comprehension gain not reproduced by a general Arabic control.

entry.title: OmniAlign: A Unified Multilingual Aligner for Word and Sentence Alignment

author.name: Mengpeng Yang, Jingxu Yang, Chao Chen, Tian Xia, Yabo Sun, Qiang Liu

entry.summary: OmniAlign is a single lightweight encoder-based model that performs both word-level and sentence-level cross-lingual alignment, deriving word alignments from token similarity matrices and many-to-many sentence alignments from embeddings. Removes the need to run separate tools per granularity in multilingual long-text settings.

entry.title: MissDiag: Diagnostic Evaluation of Incomplete-Knowledge Robustness in KGQA and KG-RAG

author.name: Hang Wang, Hang Dong, Lu Liu, Chuanru Ren

entry.summary: MissDiag decomposes robustness evaluation for knowledge-graph QA and KG-RAG so that degradation can be attributed to the type of missing evidence, the system's behavioral response, and the answer-matching protocol separately. Replaces aggregate score-drop reporting with a diagnostic breakdown.

entry.title: Introducing the Privacy-HSD Trade-off: Hate Speech Detection, but not at the Cost of Privacy

author.name: Stephen Meisenbacher, Vlad Garbuz, Chirill Donos, Maxim Dnestreanschii, Gabriel Creanga, Andreea-Elena Bodea, Thomas Lampert, Jana Diesner

entry.summary: Shows that hate speech detection models may achieve performance partly by encoding authorship signals, creating a privacy risk for the people whose posts are analyzed. Benchmarks text privatization techniques including a new domain-specific method and formalizes a privacy versus detection trade-off.

entry.title: Falcon Perception-HD: High Density Perception via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Sofian Chaybouti, Yasser Dahou, Ngoc Dung Huynh, Reda Alami, Hilde Kuehne

entry.summary: Falcon Perception-HD applies GRPO-style reinforcement learning to post-train an autoregressive open-vocabulary perception model, replacing token-level cross-entropy with rewards aligned to precision and recall, and solving perception-specific issues like rewards over set-structured outputs and multi-head sampling control. Reports that RL unlocks behaviors SFT does not, particularly for dense multi-entity localization. Extends the RLVR playbook from reasoning to grounded perception.

entry.title: Revisiting the "Push-T" Robot Manipulation Task with Agentic Robotics

author.name: Shuangyu Xie, Kaiyuan Chen, Ken Goldberg

entry.summary: Revisits the Push-T manipulation benchmark by prompting an LLM coding agent (Claude Code with the existing Claude-Fable-5 model) to write an algorithmic controller with no demonstration data, and compares the resulting code-as-policy against visuomotor imitation learning. The agent apparently located the 2D gym simulation online and iteratively used simulated experiments to learn push mechanics, reportedly reaching 100 percent success. Raises pointed questions about benchmark contamination and about what imitation-learning benchmarks actually measure.

entry.title: Progressive Experience Fusion for Multi-Task World Model Control in Endovascular Navigation

author.name: Harry Robertshaw, Maxence Boels, Nikola Fischer, Sebastien Ourselin, Christos Bergeles, Alejandro Granados, Thomas C Booth

entry.summary: Applies a multi-task TD-MPC2 world model with Progressive Experience Fusion to autonomous endovascular catheter navigation, reporting 74 percent success versus 37 percent for soft actor-critic and 65 percent for base TD-MPC2 across five subtasks and ten anatomies. Adds an adaptive planning-horizon heuristic and patient-specific fine-tuning.

entry.title: Dream2Reward: Transition-Alignment Reward Models from Positive Demonstrations for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Haoyu Zhang, Zecui Zeng, Bin Wang, Lusong Li, Liang Lin, Long Cheng

entry.summary: Dream2Reward learns a language-conditioned latent transition field from successful demonstrations only, then scores observed motion by directional and magnitude agreement with the predicted successful displacement. This penalizes wrong-direction, overshooting, and stalled behavior that progress-based reward models mistakenly reward.

entry.title: GEAR: Generative Expansion and Real Anchoring for Two-Stage Distillation of Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Qi Qin, Jiajie Zhu, Dali Chen, Yuzhao Zhang, Jia-Xing Han, Yu Su, Peng Zhang, Ying Yan, Yifan Sun

entry.summary: GEAR distills in-context tabular foundation models into small MLP or tree students in two stages: first training on teacher predictions at synthetic query points to widen coverage, then re-anchoring to real labels with out-of-fold teacher predictions to avoid leakage. The goal is CPU-deployable predictors without the latency and memory of context-dependent inference.

entry.title: UMER: Unifying Embedding and Ranking via Pair-Aware Discriminative Reasoning for Universal Multimodal Retrieval

author.name: Libiao Chen, Xiyang Liu, Yanheng Wei, Tao Wang, Zhenyu Tang

entry.summary: UMER unifies embedding-based retrieval and reranking for universal multimodal retrieval by introducing pair-aware discriminative reasoning that compares a query against candidates jointly rather than encoding each in isolation. This is intended to separate true positives from semantically confusable hard negatives that item-wise chain-of-thought embedding methods miss.

entry.title: SuTRA : Structurally-Unified Tokenization with Root Awareness

author.name: Vaibhav Rathore, Siddhant Gole, Dadhichi Telwadkar, Rooshil Bhatia, Maulik Ruparel, Siddharth Surekha, Neha Bhargava

entry.summary: SuTRA is a morphology-aware tokenizer for Indic languages that preserves akshara (orthographic syllable) indivisibility and penalizes merges that cross root and affix boundaries, countering what the authors call morphological shattering by frequency-based subword methods. It ships with a new morphological segmentation dataset for Hindi, Marathi, and Gujarati.

entry.title: When Do LLMs Actually Help? Evaluating LLMs as Data Quality Annotators

author.name: Praphulla Lal Shrestha

entry.summary: Tests whether an LLM annotator beats rule-based baselines on e-commerce entity matching and brand mislabeling, finding zero-shot LLM performance essentially tied with a simple rule baseline. A few-shot prompt that looked better on a small validation sample degraded full-scale F1, a cautionary result about prompt selection on small samples.

entry.title: What Can Artificial Intelligence Learn from Medicine? Generative Analogies and Reliable Machine Learning Systems

author.name: Emanuele Ratti, Lena Zuchowski

entry.summary: A philosophy-of-science analysis arguing that the frequently invoked parallel between clinical translation in medicine and building reliable ML systems is a generative analogy, and unpacks which epistemic warrants actually transfer. Aims to give the reliability discourse in ML a firmer conceptual footing.

entry.title: Aslema at NADI 2026: Augmentation through Fewshot for SLU

author.name: Tajwaar Shafiq, Hunzalah Hassan Bhatti, Shammur Absar Chowdhury, Firoj Alam

entry.summary: A shared-task system for Tunisian Arabic dialect spoken language understanding that compares zero-shot omni LLMs against fine-tuned models and augments training with LLM-generated dialectal utterances rendered through voice cloning. Fine-tuning plus synthetic speech improves both intent accuracy and slot filling.

entry.title: An Omitted Mode Is a Rare Rule: The Sampling-Verification Danger Law in Continuous Code World Models

author.name: Javier Aguilar Mart\'in

entry.summary: Analyzes what it actually certifies when an LLM-synthesized executable world model is accepted because it reproduces sampled transitions, deriving that the chance all sampled rollouts miss a rare critical event decays only geometrically in the number of samples. Demonstrates that planners exploit the resulting mode-blind models to near-total regret on hybrid control instruments and proves a Lipschitz-based localization budget.

entry.title: Institutional Prestige as Geographic Bias in Large Language Models: Evidence from Three Factorial Experiments with Bootstrap Confidence Intervals

author.name: Maikel Leyva-Vazquez, Florentin Smarandache

entry.summary: Runs three factorial experiments across four LLMs and 4,320 API calls to separate applicant name ethnicity from institutional prestige and country of origin in hiring-style evaluations. Finds a robust institution-tier gradient and a smaller country effect, while name-origin effects are statistically indistinguishable from zero.

entry.title: Learning-State-Aware Dynamic Generative Data Augmentation on Small-Scale Datasets

author.name: Ting Xiang, Chenxi Deng, Jinhui Zhao, Bingting Jiang, Ke Zhang, Changjian Chen, Zhuo Tang

entry.summary: LSADA adapts generative data augmentation to the downstream model by building a per-sample learning state that sets augmentation strength and varies edits by image region, aiming to balance diversity against class-semantic fidelity on small image datasets. It extends dynamic, feedback-driven augmentation beyond task-agnostic strategies.

entry.title: Pessimistic Meta-Induction and Its Limits: Lessons from Frequentist Statistics and Machine Learning Theory

author.name: Hanti Lin

entry.summary: A philosophy of science paper that attacks the pessimistic meta-induction argument against scientific realism by targeting its inductive step, using convergence-to-truth criteria drawn from frequentist statistics, learning theory and formal epistemology. It argues ordinary enumerative induction can converge everywhere while meta-induction cannot converge almost everywhere.

entry.title: OOD Detection for EEG-based Machine Learning in High-Risk Environments

author.name: Philipp Bomatter, Henry Gouk

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark for out-of-distribution detection on EEG data and evaluates a broad set of detectors not just in isolation but by their effect on two downstream clinical decision tasks. The motivation is overconfident failure of EEG models under distribution shift in high-risk deployments.

entry.title: Fourth-Moment Geometry of Rademacher Sums

author.name: Peigan Gao, Jian Qian

entry.summary: A probability-theory paper determining how higher moments of normalized Rademacher sums depend on fourth-order mass, yielding sharp Gaussian stability and Khintchine-type constants and settling several stated conjectures. The extremizer is the flat coefficient vector.

entry.title: Policy-Invariant Reward Shaping from LLM Feedback: A Framework for Hybrid RL Agents

author.name: Christophe D. Hounwanou, John Emeka Eze, Ya\'e U. Gaba

entry.summary: Formalizes the common hybrid design where an LLM plans and an RL controller acts as a goal-augmented MDP, and proves that using bounded LLM progress scores as a potential function preserves the set of optimal policies even when the LLM scores are wrong. Numerical checks include an adversarial potential scaled twenty times the base reward.

entry.title: Why GPT-Style Models Do Not Directly Transfer to Symbolic Music: Compression in the Wrong Coordinate System

author.name: Yi Wang

entry.summary: A conceptual argument that transferring GPT-style tokenization to symbolic music fails because musical regularities are not predictively compressible in the usual note or chord coordinate system. The paper frames an effectiveness versus losslessness tradeoff and argues the real research problem is finding the right representational coordinates, not larger reusable musical units.

entry.title: VA-Judger: Reward Modeling from Human Preference Feedback for Joint Video-Audio Generation

author.name: Yinming Huang, Shuyuan Tu, Xi Yan, Zihan Yang, Jianhua Han, Xu Hang, Yu-Gang Jiang, Zuxuan Wu

entry.summary: VA-Judger builds a large human-preference dataset for joint video-audio generation and trains a unified reward model, arguing that combining separate audio quality, visual fidelity, and synchronization metrics invites reward hacking and misses cross-modal semantic and temporal coherence. The learned judge is intended for RL post-training of video-audio generators. Directly targets the alignment bottleneck for multimodal generation.

entry.title: Beyond receptive fields: sequence-pooled normalization can supply most of a sequence labeler's context

author.name: Qing Tian

entry.summary: Shows analytically, from the normalization layer Jacobian, that when a convolutional sequence labeler computes normalization statistics along the sequence at inference time, it opens a sequence-spanning information path that bypasses the convolutional receptive field and supplies global context. On a synthetic task with computable optima, that leaked global summary accounts for most of the model's usable context. Undercuts common locality and streaming-horizon claims based on receptive fields.

entry.title: Real-Time Control-Constrained DDP for Underactuated Balancing of Legged Robots

author.name: SeongWon Nam, Hyunyong Lee, Hansol Kang, Jiman Park, Yeongwoo Son, Bumsu Yi, Jaeyoung Oh, Hyouk Ryeol Choi

entry.summary: Introduces ABC-DDP, a differential dynamic programming variant that handles control constraints via accelerated projected gradient steps, avoiding repeated KKT inversions, plus a virtual constraint enabling feasibility-driven multiple shooting from infeasible starts. It targets real-time model predictive control for strongly underactuated balancing legged robots.

entry.title: Inference and Uncertainty Quantification for Streaming $r$-PCA

author.name: Haoshu Xu, Hongzhe Li

entry.summary: Provides sharp operator-norm convergence rates for streaming rank-r PCA via Oja's algorithm under sub-Gaussian data and derives distributional inference for the resulting subspace estimator beyond the rank-one case. The rate matches a proven minimax lower bound up to log factors in the spiked covariance regime.

entry.title: SESSE: Sketch, Expand, Sort, Summarize, Evaluate -- LLM-as-Judge Evaluation via Structured Decomposition

author.name: Dae Lee, Mihai Delgeanu, Adel Youssef

entry.summary: SESSE is a training-free framework that decomposes holistic A/B judge preferences into structured sub-questions mined from the judge's own error cases, without oracle answers or hand-written rubrics. On a thousand-example RewardBench slice it approaches chain-of-thought and fine-tuned specialist judge accuracy while offering per-criterion vote evidence.

entry.title: Impact of Iterative Fine-Tuning on Transcription Accuracy in Complex Historical Sanskrit Manuscripts

author.name: Kartik Chincholikar, Kaushik Gopalan, Mihir Hasabnis

entry.summary: Shows that iteratively fine-tuning a conventional OCR pipeline on the target manuscript at both layout and appearance levels progressively improves transcription of complex historical Sanskrit documents. The self-improving loop adapts to period-specific scripts, textures, and imaging noise.

entry.title: Which Negatives Matter? Ask Your Text Encoder: Adaptive Similarity Margins for Dense-Caption Retrieval

author.name: Haoyue Liu, Ye Chen, Zhichao Wang, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: Diagnoses premature saturation of the InfoNCE objective in dense-caption retrieval, reporting that loss collapses and gradients hit exact zero in a large fraction of batches during the first epoch because near-duplicate captions dominate. Proposes HN-CLIP, which uses text-encoder-derived adaptive similarity margins to keep hard negatives contributing gradient signal.

entry.title: Verifiable abstention makes AI leak diagnosis accountable in water distribution networks

author.name: Tianwei Mu, Yue Wang, Mingzhe Yuan, Manhong Huang, Wenhong Wang, Xuerui Yin, Qing Luo, Min Xiao, Hui Yang, Jun Li, Dan Xue

entry.summary: Recasts water leak localization as decision-making with verifiable abstention, where a physics-grounded executor falsifies hypotheses against a digital twin and an independent supervisor with an LLM auditor certifies, requests more evidence, or abstains. Reported decision precision on acted events rises from 32 percent under forced prediction to 96 percent.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction for Molecular Properties under Label Shift

author.name: Hyeonsu Lee, Juyeon Kim, Erkhembayar Jadamba, Seungjin Choi, Hyunjin Shin

entry.summary: Adapts conformal prediction to label shift for molecular property prediction, reweighting nonconformity scores so that coverage guarantees hold when the experimental label distribution differs from training. The goal is calibrated uncertainty intervals for high-stakes drug discovery decisions.

entry.title: Training-Free Human-in-the-Loop Anomaly Detection via Memory Bank Correction

author.name: Ayusha Abbas, Saram Abbas, Kabita Adhikari

entry.summary: Presents a gradient-free workflow where a factory operator corrects a PatchCore anomaly detector by directly editing its memory bank, inserting reviewed normal patches through a self-calibrating novelty gate. From only ten reference samples, corrections recover a large fraction of the gap to a fully trained detector.

entry.title: Intent-Driven Dynamic Chunking: Segmenting Documents to Reflect Predicted Information Needs

author.name: Christos Koutsiaris

entry.summary: Intent-Driven Dynamic Chunking uses an LLM to hypothesize the queries a document is likely to answer, then applies dynamic programming to segment the document so that chunks align with those predicted information needs. The goal is to avoid splitting answers or padding chunks with noise in retrieval and RAG pipelines.

entry.title: Network Denoising Revisited: A Ricci-Flow-Inspired Graph Diffusion Method

author.name: Ye Fang, Chuan-Xian Ren

entry.summary: Ricci-Diffusion denoises noisy graphs by letting edge-level discrete curvature modulate the diffusion kernel, producing a Ricci-flow-like evolution that respects non-Euclidean graph geometry. This contrasts with standard similarity-driven diffusion that assumes homogeneous information transport.

entry.title: Online Generalized Sparse Regression: How Does Overparametrization Help?

author.name: Shuoguang Yang, Qiang Sun

entry.summary: Develops an online cardinality- and rank-constrained regression framework with closed-form updates, bounded memory, and statistical guarantees, covering online sparse linear regression and low-rank matrix sensing. Also analyzes how overparametrization aids online sparse recovery.

entry.title: Looking Beyond the Scale: Do Surgical Skill Models Learn Transferable Representations Across Assessment Rubrics?

author.name: Hanna Hoffmann, Felix von Bechtolsheim, Stefanie Speidel, Rebecca Hisey

entry.summary: Systematically tests whether vision models trained to score surgical skill learn transferable proficiency representations or dataset-specific artifacts, comparing supervised transfer, sharpness-aware minimization, and self-supervised or contrastive pretraining across two datasets and rubrics. Finds cross-rubric transfer is a real limitation rather than a solved problem.

entry.title: Harnessing Magnitude-Only and Complex Measurements for Improved Dynamic MRI Reconstruction with Learned Priors

author.name: Mahdi Saberi, Ya\c{s}ar Utku Al\c{c}alar, Merve G\"{u}lle, Chetan Shenoy, Mehmet Ak\c{c}akaya

entry.summary: Observes that k-space magnitude measurements are highly consistent across time frames in steady-state dynamic MRI and exploits this as auxiliary information in a physics-driven reconstruction with learned priors. Provides complementary signal for accelerated reconstruction without extra scan time.

entry.title: Primitive Representation Learning for Unsupervised Dynamic Contrast Enhanced MRI Reconstruction

author.name: Veronika Spieker, Wenqi Huang, Cemre Ariyurek, Liam Timms, Daniel Rueckert, Onur Afacan, Julia A. Schnabel, Sila Kurugol

entry.summary: Introduces a scan-specific, training-data-free reconstruction for dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI that represents the scene with geometric primitives and disentangles anatomy, contrast dynamics, and residual motion into separate temporal bases. Achieves competitive quality with interpretable components.

entry.title: Grading the Graders: Verification Autonomy Levels (L0-L5) for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yajie Yin

entry.summary: Notes that the verification literature overloads the word level to mean at least five different things and proposes Verification Autonomy Levels, a single-axis taxonomy classifying schemes by where the verification specification originates and what a verdict guarantees. Ranges from LLM self-declaration up to deterministic formal anchors.

entry.title: More Context, Same Budget: Dual-Bounded Relational Recall Beyond Top-K Retrieval

author.name: Thomson D. Nguy

entry.summary: Proposes splitting a fixed retrieval token budget between relevance-ranked seed passages and bounded graph-adjacent neighbors, arguing this recovers more required evidence than flat top-k at identical cost. Reports complete recovery of official supporting-evidence sets across 7,405 HotpotQA FullWiki questions.

entry.title: When Readability and Source Retention Diverge: An Evaluability Gap in AI Translation

author.name: Chenchen Mao, Hanjing Shi, Haiyan Jia, Emily Wegrzyn, Dominic DiFranzo

entry.summary: A factorial human study with 306 participants finds that readable AI translations can create an evaluability gap where overall quality judgments do not track how faithfully the source is preserved, even when the source is displayed. Also examines how these appraisals connect to trust and willingness to disclose AI use.

entry.title: StateTrace: An Object-Centric Framework for Hidden-State Spatiotemporal Reasoning in Long Videos

author.name: Yu Han, Wenhao Li, Yichao Cao, Hongyan Xu, Shuo Yang, Shan You, Xiu Su

entry.summary: Defines hidden-state spatiotemporal reasoning, the problem of inferring what happened to objects while they are invisible in long videos, and proposes StateTrace, an object-centric memory that stores trajectories, inter-object relations, and state transitions for retrieval at question time. Addresses the failure of video LLMs to distinguish invisible from unknown. Structured memory augments rather than retrains the video model.

entry.title: EgoHRV: Continuous Heart Rate Variability Estimation from Egocentric Systems for Autonomic Response and Skill Assessment

author.name: Berken Utku Demirel, Christian Holz

entry.summary: EgoHRV estimates heart rate and, more ambitiously, beat-to-beat heart rate variability from the gaze cameras already built into egocentric headsets, using a 3D backbone with a low-high decomposition module to recover the blood volume pulse despite motion and noise. This adds an autonomic physiological channel to egocentric behavior analysis for stress, engagement, and skill assessment. Extends remote photoplethysmography into wearable eye-tracking hardware.

entry.title: Decision-Metric Alignment in Latent World Models: Diagnostics and Action-Conditioned Objectives for MPC Planning

author.name: Jiawei Wang, Ke Rui, Yushen Zuo, Yichun Feng, Minglei Li

entry.summary: Points out that a JEPA-style latent world model can decode task variables well and still fail as an MPC cost, because Euclidean latent distance to a goal may not rank action sequences by real task progress, a property the authors name decision-metric alignment. They introduce rank-correlation diagnostics on random plans and during CEM search, analyze sufficient conditions involving encoder distortion and rollout error, and propose action-conditioned objectives. Directly targets the gap between representation quality and planning utility.

entry.title: A Unifying Relational Perspective on Expressive Lottery Tickets

author.name: Lorenz Kummer, Samir Moustafa, Anatol Ehrlich, Franka Bause, Marco Nennstiel, Przemys{\l}aw Andrzej Wa{\l}\c{e}ga, Nils Morten Kriege

entry.summary: Generalizes the strong expressive lottery ticket hypothesis from static graph neural networks to multi-relational and temporal ones using relational Weisfeiler-Leman, proving that sufficiently overparameterized relational GNNs contain sparse subnetworks preserving 1-RWL expressivity. It also lower-bounds the probability that random pruning finds such a subnetwork and reformulates common temporal GNNs as relational ones.

entry.title: Concerns About Personas, Multi-Agent Alignment, and Role Theory

author.name: Davidmanheim

entry.summary: Applies sociological role theory to the current LLM-persona framing in alignment, arguing that because roles in humans are context-dependent, negotiated, and multiply held, hoping for one robustly aligned persona to bootstrap safety misunderstands how roles behave. The post then sketches resulting multi-agent alignment problems.

entry.title: Q-Learning With World Models

author.name: Perry Dong, Yueru Jia, Chelsea Finn, Dorsa Sadigh

entry.summary: Already covered in yesterday's Research section, Argues that world models should be used to improve value learning rather than to generate imagined rollouts for direct policy optimization, avoiding compounding model bias that worsens with horizon and visual complexity. The method integrates learned dynamics into off-policy Q-learning, aimed at sample-efficient real-world robot learning and RL fine-tuning of vision-language-action policies.

entry.title: Self-prompting and cross-model consensus enable reproducible data extraction from scientific literature with large language models

author.name: Valentin Romanov, Monique Bax, Steven Niederer

entry.summary: Tests four escalating workflows for extracting nuanced contextual data from scientific papers with browser-based frontier models, finding strong performance given expert prompts, near-parity when models write their own prompts, and poor autonomous literature discovery with missed or hallucinated references. Cross-model consensus is proposed to make extraction reproducible.

entry.title: Pathology Transport: Optimal-Transport Explanations for Clinical Data, and When Their Heatmaps (Fail to) Localize Disease

author.name: Lalit Kumar

entry.summary: Trains an optimal-transport rectified flow between healthy and diseased clinical distributions to produce per-patient counterfactuals and label-free attribution maps, then explicitly tests whether the resulting heatmaps actually localize disease. Reports strong unsupervised malignancy scoring on tabular biomarkers while being candid about localization failures.

entry.title: Evaluating RL Explainability Methods by How Much They Help Fix Bugs in Agents

author.name: Ram Rachum, Yotam Amitai, B\'alint Gyevn\'ar, Reuth Mirsky, Cameron Allen

entry.summary: Proposes EvalXRL, a benchmark that judges explainable RL methods by whether an LLM coding agent can use their explanations to diagnose and repair a deliberately broken RL agent, measured by recovered reward. It is a position and design paper rather than a completed evaluation.

entry.title: Domain-Adapted Molecular Language Models for Efficient Search of Make-on-Demand Libraries

author.name: Henrik Wille, Luis-Finley Sch\"utz, Felix Strieth-Kalthoff

entry.summary: Benchmarks four pretrained molecular language models as encoders across six virtual libraries in drug discovery, materials, and catalysis, finding that classic fingerprints are a consistently strong baseline while pretrained embeddings vary widely. Domain adaptation is shown to substantially close the gap.

entry.title: MoRAX: Mobility-based Representation Augmentation for Geospatial Foundation Models

author.name: Ya Wen, Jixuan Cai, Yulun Zhou, Alec Kirkley

entry.summary: MoRAX augments geospatial foundation model embeddings, which are dominated by Earth-observation imagery, with functional structure derived from human mobility flows, in a way intended to transfer beyond the single city where mobility data was collected. It keeps the base model coverage while adding human-activity signal.

entry.title: Continuous-Time Reinforcement Learning for Controlled Hawkes Jump-Diffusions

author.name: Tomasz R. Bielecki, Thibaut Mastrolia, Haoze Yan

entry.summary: Develops continuous-time reinforcement learning for stochastic control of multivariate Hawkes-driven jump diffusions, which are non-Markovian because of path-dependent intensity memory. The authors give a Markovianization procedure using mixtures of exponential kernels, prove convergence of the approximation and value function, and derive deterministic policy gradient methods.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Agents as Dynamic Graph Transformation: A Survey and New Perspective

author.name: Yuanyuan Xu, Wenjie Zhang, Yin Chen, Xuemin Lin, Ying Zhang

entry.summary: A survey recasting self-evolving LLM agents as dynamic graph transformation problems, where memories, tools, skills, workflows, and inter-agent links form a topology that changes over time. It argues existing graph-agent and self-evolving-agent surveys each miss the coupling between agent state and graph structure.

entry.title: Governance Records as Supervision: Verifier-Selected Self-Training for Structured Workflow Repair

author.name: Jesus Salas

entry.summary: Tests whether governance records from machine-verifiable workflows, which link task contract, attempt, verifier decision, and accepted output, can serve as training supervision. Plans accepted by an independent planning verifier are used to self-train the same model for reliable one-shot execution on held-out PlanBench replanning cases, improving accepted plans from 1 to 57 out of 80.

entry.title: Improving Natural-Language Combinatorial-Optimization Accuracy in Resource-Constrained Language Models via Formal Abstractions

author.name: Shrenil Shaun Sharma, Avi Sharma

entry.summary: Introduces SDDL, a neuro-symbolic pipeline that translates natural-language scheduling problems into solver-aligned representations of tasks, resources, constraints, and objectives, delegating search to a deterministic compiler and solver. The goal is to keep small, resource-constrained models feasible on combinatorial scheduling where direct generation violates constraints.

entry.title: FinRCA-Bench: Benchmarking Evidence Retrieval and Reasoning for Financial AI Systems

author.name: Pratik Ghawate

entry.summary: FinRCA-Bench is a deterministic synthetic benchmark of 2,250 accounts-payable-to-bank reconciliation cases across 14 operational tables, with 1,500 injected failures in 15 causal categories plus hard negatives. It is designed to disentangle whether financial reasoning failures stem from bad evidence retrieval over relational links or from reasoning itself.

entry.title: What is Missing from AI Post-Training AI: An Empirical Analysis

author.name: Joy Jia Yin Lim, Xin Huang, Hao Peng, Yaxi Lu, Xin Cong, Zhong Zhang, Maosong Sun, Yankai Lin

entry.summary: Eureka compiles long-horizon tasks into dynamic obligation graphs with explicit acceptance semantics, forming specialized macro-agents through receding-horizon planning and cost-benefit-gated architecture evolution. It reports completing all 170 recursive tasks and generating nearly 4,000 certificates with no false acceptances, alongside theoretical results on regret and serializability.

entry.title: NE-BERT: A Multilingual Language Model for Nine Northeast Indian Languages

author.name: Badal Nyalang

entry.summary: NE-BERT is a multilingual encoder trained on roughly 8.3 million sentences covering nine Northeast Indian languages plus Hindi and English, using weighted sampling and a custom unigram tokenizer. It reports large perplexity reductions over IndicBERT-V2 and MuRIL and better tokenization fertility than mBERT across all nine target languages.

entry.title: Fractional Decay KV-Cache: Ownership-Aware Memory Management for Improved Inference Relevancy in Dialog Systems

author.name: Sukanta Ganguly

entry.summary: Proposes FD-KVC, a KV cache eviction scheme with dual scoring channels: cumulative attention importance similar to heavy-hitter methods, plus a recency-weighted relevance channel with temporal decay and reinforcement-style updates. The design aims to keep historically important tokens while adapting quickly when dialog topics shift.

entry.title: OptiModNet: A UNet-Transformer Hybrid with Grouped-Query and Channel Attention for Optic Disc and Cup Segmentation

author.name: Soumili Ghosh, Debapriya Roy, Aryan Das, Bikash Santra

entry.summary: Proposes a UNet-transformer hybrid using grouped-query and channel attention for optic disc and cup segmentation in glaucoma screening, aiming for cross-dataset consistency at low compute. Motivated by deployment in resource-limited clinical settings.

entry.title: RoBell-RVFL: A Robust Generalized Bell Random Vector Functional Link Network

author.name: A. Rahaman, A. Quadir, M. Tanveer

entry.summary: RoBell-RVFL is a randomized neural network for imbalanced and noisy tabular data that applies a bell-shaped robust loss with dual sample-level weighting, preserving minority samples while down-weighting outliers and mislabeled points. It targets limitations of oversampling and simple class weighting.

entry.title: Tight Bounds for Data-driven Multiple Hyper-parameter Tuning with Structured Loss Function

author.name: Anh Tuan Nguyen, Viet Anh Nguyen

entry.summary: Establishes sharper (and matching lower-bound) pseudo-dimension results for learning-theoretic guarantees when tuning several hyperparameters at once, using real algebraic geometry to count connected sign cells instead of sign vectors. It tightens sample-complexity bounds in the data-driven algorithm design framework.

entry.title: MITRE-SAGE: A Multi-Agent Cybersecurity Question-Answering Model

author.name: Ali Habibzadeh, Farid Feyzi, Reza Ebrahimi Atani

entry.summary: MITRE-SAGE is a multi-agent retrieval-augmented generation system for cybersecurity question answering that fuses semantic retrieval with structural knowledge from the MITRE framework to reduce hallucination. The goal is more reliable and interpretable analyst support under alert fatigue and time pressure.

entry.title: Digital Twin-Based Intrusion Detection for Vehicle Powertrain CAN Bus Systems

author.name: Araf Rahman, M Sabbir Salek, Mashrur Chowdhury

entry.summary: The authors build a digital twin of a vehicle powertrain using a shared-encoder LSTM trained on seventeen decoded signals from real Hyundai and Kia CAN logs, then flag intrusions as residuals between predicted and observed physical behavior. The aim is to catch payload-manipulation attacks that preserve normal message timing and frequency and therefore evade conventional CAN intrusion detectors.

entry.title: DocClaw: A Unified Agentic System for Intelligent Document Processing

author.name: Siqi Xiang, Zhipeng Xu, Yufei Liu, Junhao Ji, Qing Liu, Zulong Chen, Zhibo Yang, Chunyan Miao, Shijian Lu

entry.summary: DocClaw unifies OCR, document question answering, and key information extraction as a single agent-document interaction loop, where an agent perceives content, gathers task-relevant information, and iteratively refines intermediate results instead of running task-specific pipelines. Includes industrial co-authors alongside academic groups. Represents the shift from specialized document models toward general agentic document processing.

entry.title: Frozen DINO Localizes Image Edits Without a Localizer

author.name: Zane Kumar, Vishal Jain, Bernhard Kainz

entry.summary: TRAIL shows that patch-token drift in a frozen DINO encoder under a single global Haar perturbation functions as a localization map for AI image edits, reaching 0.903 patch AUROC versus 0.912 for a mask-supervised localizer on a small CocoGlide split and transferring unchanged to Poisson interpolation edits. No localizer training or edit masks are required. Suggests forensic localization capability is already latent in self-supervised features.

entry.title: USR-Drive: Unified Driving Scene Representation via Joint Denoising of 3D Gaussians and Boxes

author.name: Li-Heng Chen, Haokai Pang, Chengye Su, Jiarun Liu, Qifeng Chen, Ziqian Ni, Jianxin Huang, Shi-Sheng Huang, Hongbo Fu, Sheng Yang

entry.summary: USR-Drive jointly denoises 3D Gaussians and object bounding boxes in one conditional generative framework, so that dynamic scene reconstruction and instance-level 3D detection constrain each other instead of being solved separately from posed multi-view driving video. Reconstruction gains geometric supervision from boxes while detection gains dense geometric grounding. Aims at a unified spatial representation for autonomous driving.

entry.title: Subgroup performance analysis of adaptation strategies for chest X-ray foundation models

author.name: Dhruv Gupta, Emma A. M. Stanley, Fabio De Sousa Ribeiro, Sujal Desai, Ben Glocker

entry.summary: Tests how three parameter-efficient adaptation strategies on a frozen chest X-ray foundation encoder (linear head on the CLS token, an MLP, and attention pooling over multi-layer patch features) affect both pathology classification accuracy and subgroup disparities across race, sex, and view, on a demographically balanced MIMIC-CXR test set.
