entry.summary: BrainNorm is a normative brain MRI foundation model trained with language-image contrastive pretraining on roughly 66,000 healthy structural scans, producing an atlas-parcel latent space with age-conditioned healthy trajectories. Deviation from these trajectories supports brain-age gap estimation and multi-disease classification across six external cohorts.

entry.title: Differentiable Voronoi Ray Tracing Beyond Rasterization Speeds

author.name: Bernardo Taveira, Carl Lindstr\"om, Joakim Johnander, Fredrik Kahl

entry.summary: VoroTracing analyzes what actually limits throughput in differentiable Voronoi ray tracing (traversal length, per-cell work, memory locality) and co-designs representation, optimization and GPU execution to reach speeds competitive with or exceeding rasterization. Ray-based rendering natively supports distortion, rolling shutter and depth-of-field effects that rasterizers need special extensions for.

entry.title: VLCP: Vision Language Control Policy Closed-Loop Code Replanning for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Dhia Naouali, Minghan Wu, Claudia Wong, Abhinav Puthran, Omar G. Younis

entry.summary: VLCP keeps a frontier vision-language model frozen and has it write a short Python control function as the robot policy, with no demonstrations or fine-tuning. Unlike prior closed-loop schemes that retry a fixed policy or switch subtasks, it periodically re-observes multi-view images and proprioception and rewrites the failing control code within the same episode. This targets code-level rather than action-level failure recovery for manipulation.

entry.title: Toward the Optimal Regret-Instability Trade-off in Multi-Armed Bandits

author.name: Kaifei Wang, Yinyu Ye, Han Zhong

entry.summary: This paper formalizes a trade-off in multi-armed bandits between worst-case regret and instability, defined as the largest standard deviation of a terminal arm pull count across runs, proving a finite-time lower bound on their product without the regularity assumptions of prior asymptotic work. It also introduces a tunable algorithm combining a running lower-envelope index with a decreasing pull schedule to navigate the trade-off. Reproducibility of allocations, not just average regret, is increasingly relevant for deployed adaptive experiments.

entry.title: Minimax Optimal Estimator and Improved Error Rate for the MLE in Logistic Regression with Gaussian Design

author.name: Junren Chen, Arya Mazumdar

entry.summary: The authors give the first minimax optimal estimator for the parameter vector in logistic regression with Gaussian design and improve the best known finite-sample error rate for the maximum likelihood estimator, both flowing from a minimax optimal estimator for the parameter norm. They establish a matching lower bound for norm estimation. This sharpens the theory of a workhorse statistical model in the high-signal regime.

entry.title: FedPref: Federated Preference Learning for Structured Radiology Report Extraction

author.name: Flint Xiaofeng Fan, Cheston Tan, Yew-Soon Ong, Roger Wattenhofer

entry.summary: FedPref lets hospitals train small Qwen3-8B adapters for structured radiology extraction by having frozen public models propose candidate JSON outputs that local annotators rank, sharing only model updates rather than patient data. A heterogeneous teacher pool prevents candidate collapse when one model repeats itself.

entry.title: Towards Better Agents for Multi-Turn User Interaction: The Next User Turn Is More Than Context

author.name: Yiwen Zhao, Zhihao Wen, Yuchen Mao, Mingxuan Jiang, Yihao Hu, Pan Wang, Xin Zhang, Wei Wu

entry.summary: FACA extracts credit signals from the next user turn, treating user reactions as noisy local evidence about the preceding agent segment, and adds a locally normalized reaction advantage to the terminal outcome advantage without needing a critic or extra rollouts. It targets the flat-credit problem in interactive GRPO for tool-using dialogue agents.

entry.title: GraphWake: Group Polarization via Memory-Mediated Polarization Cascade in LLM-Agent Communities

author.name: Haoran Bu, Zejian Chen, Litian Zhang, Xi Zhang

entry.summary: Defines a new attack on agent social platforms where an adversary exposes a few agents to stance-reinforcing arguments that persist in their memory and then propagate through public discussion, producing group polarization. Uses memory as the persistence channel and normal discourse as the propagation channel, avoiding prompt tampering or fake echo chambers.

entry.title: Auditing Self-Evolution in Financial Agents: Capability Gains, Security Drift, and Execution-Interface Mismatch

author.name: Jialong Li, Jialing Zhu

entry.summary: Audits three self-evolving agent memory and skill methods in a simulated e-banking environment, finding that benign utility rises while exposure to injected content and unauthorized financial state changes rise faster. Reports that overall attack success increases even when conditional success after exposure falls slightly.

entry.title: Position: Fairness Failure in Generative Models is an Evaluation Problem

author.name: Mariia Vladimirova, Jean-Yves Franceschi, Thibaut Issenhuth

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that persistent fairness failures in generative models are fundamentally caused by non-comparable, non-actionable evaluation practice rather than only by data or modeling choices. It catalogs recurring empirical and conceptual failure modes and proposes Fairness Cards as a minimal standardized reporting artifact for deployment decisions. Aimed at shifting the field from ad-hoc bias probes to reproducible measurement.

entry.title: Foundation Agents Meet Agentic Deep Research: Evidence-Grounded Clinical Code Forecasting

author.name: Junda Wang, Meysam Ghaffari, Akshat Choube, Mohsen Sharifi Renani, Hong Yu, Carlos Morato

entry.summary: ICD-Deepresearch composes structured EHR foundation models with language models, medical search, and ICD dictionaries in a deep-research style agentic workflow to forecast which diagnosis codes will appear at a patient's next encounter. The design compensates for the fact that no single source reveals the future code set by evaluating candidate transitions against linked clinical evidence. It shows agentic research loops applied to prospective clinical prediction.

entry.title: Encoded but Not Actionable: Auditing the Decode-Generate-Steer Gap in Frozen LLMs for Geometric Constraints

author.name: Man Liang, Xinzhao Cheng, Faizan Wajid

entry.summary: The authors probe six frozen decoder-only LLMs on parametric CAD geometry to separate what is linearly decodable from what actually drives generation and can be steered. They find pretraining improves decoding of local pairwise geometric relations while sketch-level constraint status remains weakly actionable, exposing a gap between encoded and usable knowledge.

entry.title: Policy-Invariant Reward Shaping from LLM Feedback: A Framework for Hybrid RL Agents

author.name: Christophe D. Hounwanou, John Emeka Eze, Ya\'e U. Gaba

entry.summary: The paper formalizes hybrid LLM-planner plus RL-controller systems as goal-augmented MDPs and proves that using a bounded LLM progress score as a potential function preserves the set of optimal policies even when the LLM scores are wrong. A small MDP experiment includes an adversarial potential scaled twenty times the base reward.

entry.title: One Score, Two Decisions: Selective Prediction on the Rare-Disease Tail

author.name: Zhaoyang Jiang, Zhizhong Fu, Yunsoo Kim, Zicheng Li, Xuanqi Peng, Fei Teng, Jiacong Mi, Honghan Wu

entry.summary: This paper shows that for rare-disease diagnosis, selective prediction over ranked outputs is bounded by ranking quality first: eight small open-weight LLMs reach at most 4.6 percent top-1 recall on ultra-rare diseases, so even perfect confidence ordering cannot reach 50 percent selective accuracy at 10 percent coverage. It argues for feasibility checks before deploying abstention thresholds.

entry.title: Generative Learning of Separatrices

author.name: Ellis R. Crabtree, Dimitris G. Giovanis, Anastasia Georgiou, George Datseris, Ioannis G. Kevrekidis

entry.summary: This work uses generative models to sample and reconstruct separatrices, the boundaries between basins of attraction in multistable dynamical systems, which are rarely visited by direct simulation. The method aims to work in higher dimensions and without requiring explicit knowledge of the governing equations.

entry.title: Lipschitz Bandits with Arbitrary Feedback Delays

author.name: Yuhao Liu, Yu Chen, Longbo Huang

entry.summary: Extends Lipschitz bandits over continuous action spaces to settings where reward feedback arrives after arbitrary delays, giving elimination-based and EXP3-based algorithms for stochastic and adversarial rewards. Regret bounds scale with a zooming dimension plus a square-root total-delay term.

entry.title: EMASAM: a Computationally Efficient Sharpness-Aware Minimization via EMA-Guided Perturbations

author.name: Tanapat Ratchatorn, Masayuki Tanaka

entry.summary: EMASAM removes the extra gradient computation that makes sharpness-aware minimization twice as expensive by defining the perturbation direction from the gap between current weights and their exponential moving average. This preserves much of the generalization benefit while approaching standard training cost.

entry.title: Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study

author.name: Fanqi Wang, Weisheng Tang, Hairong Qi

entry.summary: Studies how predictable short-horizon parameter updates are during training, using displacement, subspace-residual, and predictor-based probes with null-calibrated readouts on vision training and public Pythia pretraining checkpoints. It finds that normalization parameters and biases behave very differently from weight matrices in terms of temporal redundancy.

entry.title: SubZero+: Efficient Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning via Large Learning Rates

author.name: Ziming Yu, Shuyao Xiao, Xingyu Zhao, Sike Wang, Pan Zhou, Peiyu Zang, Xiangda Yan, Yongjie Yang, Jia Li

entry.summary: SubZero+ stabilizes zeroth-order fine-tuning of LLMs by combining multi-query gradient estimation inside layer-specific low-rank subspaces, a subspace Adam optimizer using in-subspace statistics, and a sign correction ensuring properly distributed random projections. This reduces the estimator variance that makes backprop-free tuning learning-rate sensitive.

entry.title: Second-Moment Memory in Coordinatewise Adam

author.name: Jeonseong Kim

entry.summary: Analyzes the optimization cost of Adam's exponential moving average of squared gradients, showing that long second-moment memory can suppress progress even with finite-variance gradients. It derives a directional bound scaling with the inverse square root of memory length and converts it into an average-stationarity lower bound on a smooth convex problem.

entry.title: Layers Matter: Why Continual Learning Regularization Should Be Layer-Adaptive

author.name: Brian B. Moser, Ahmed Anwar, Tobias Christian Nauen, Shishir Muralidhara, Federico Raue, Ren\'e Schuster, Stanislav Frolov, Andreas Dengel

entry.summary: Argues that continual learning regularizers like elastic weight consolidation should be layer-adaptive because diagonal Fisher importance misses the top-eigenvalue curvature that actually controls forgetting, and layer sensitivity spans orders of magnitude. Under a block-diagonal Hessian assumption the authors prove forgetting decomposes into per-layer terms weighted by each layer's top Hessian eigenvalue.

entry.title: Information Geometry of Message Passing

author.name: Mykola Lukashchuk, Kyrylo Yemets, Alex Ledbetter, \.{I}smail \c{S}en\"oz

entry.summary: The paper shows that the stationary condition of natural-gradient variational inference can be written as an edge-local rule on Forney-style factor graphs, where each edge parameter equals a sum of two projected belief-propagation messages. This yields natural-gradient message passing, allowing each edge to carry its own exponential family while remaining a local computation. It bridges information geometry and probabilistic graphical model inference in a way that could simplify hybrid inference engines.

entry.title: How Many Samples Are Needed to Determine Causal Direction? Sharp Minimax Bounds for Bivariate LiNGAM

author.name: Jikai Jin

entry.summary: Derives sharp minimax sample-complexity bounds for determining causal direction between two linearly related variables, quantifying how difficulty scales with the strength of the structural coefficient and the distance of the noise from Gaussianity. This puts precise numbers on when classical non-Gaussian identifiability becomes statistically hopeless.

entry.title: LaGSplat: Inferring Physics-Governed Interactive Simulation from Monocular Video Using Latent Lagrangian Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Louen Pottier

entry.summary: Infers interactive, physics-governed object dynamics from one or a few monocular videos by making a single low-dimensional latent state serve simultaneously as the generalized coordinate of a learned dissipative Lagrangian and as the conditioning variable of a Gaussian Splatting decoder. Because the splat primitives move with the object, user-applied forces in image space can be pulled back into the latent dynamics at inference, even though no forces were ever observed during training.

entry.title: Architecture-Dependent Causal Transfer of Activation States Across Large Language Models

author.name: Fernando Cardenas Piepereit

entry.summary: Tests whether internal activation states can be transferred causally between architecturally different open-weight LLMs via a learned projection, evaluated at three levels: representational similarity, cross-model retrieval from projected states, and end-to-end effects of injecting projected activations during generation. Alignment beats a random-initialization baseline and is best measured by rank-based metrics, but causal transfer turns out to depend heavily on architecture.

entry.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning for Hemodynamic Management of Sepsis in the ICU: a MIMIC-IV Study with Dual Off-Policy Evaluation

author.name: Marc P\'erez-Roig, David Fern\'andez-Narro, Carlos S\'aez

entry.summary: Learns offline RL policies for fluid and vasopressor dosing in sepsis from nearly 37,000 ICU stays, but centers the contribution on trustworthy evaluation: two complementary off-policy estimators plus reliability diagnostics and clinician-agreement analysis. The framing acknowledges that off-policy value estimates for clinical policies are often fragile and optimistic.

entry.title: MIRROR: Multimodal Intelligent Radiology Reasoning and Observation Reporter

author.name: Vignesh Nagarajan, Sriram Venkatapathy

entry.summary: MIRROR is a radiology reporting prototype that deliberately blinds the language layer to the image: a multi-label classifier plus Grad-CAM localizer produce labels, probabilities, and anatomical regions, and only those structured outputs feed the report writer. Because the text generator never sees pixels, it structurally cannot assert findings the classifier did not produce, making report findings auditable against the probability vector.

entry.title: Q-Interference: Memory-Efficient Phase-Aware Quantum-Inspired Attention

author.name: Emama Nahid, Tahmid Imtiaz Imu, Huayue Gu, Liran Ma, Zhipeng Cai, Honghui Xu

entry.summary: Q-Interference augments each query and key feature with an amplitude and a learned phase so attention scores can be constructive or destructive rather than only measuring similarity, in a fully classical quantum-inspired formulation. The paper addresses the memory blowup of the naive token-pair-feature interaction tensor to keep the mechanism practical for autoregressive language modeling.

entry.title: LIBERO-VIFO: Benchmarking the Capability and Safety of Visual Cue Following in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Zhengyan Qian, Rui Yan, Alex Jinpeng Wang, Jinhui Tang

entry.summary: LIBERO-VIFO benchmarks whether vision-language-action models follow authorized visual cues while ignoring unauthorized ones, defining eight cue families and four protocols that separate cue understanding from execution. Treating unauthorized cue following as a safety failure surfaces a visual prompt-injection style attack surface for robot policies. It moves evaluation beyond coarse task success.

entry.title: Runtime Governance for Agentic AI: Action-Boundary Control with Trusted Provenance and Fail-Closed Execution

author.name: Adam Mazzocchetti

entry.summary: Proposes Aegis, a runtime layer that treats agent tool calls as proposals judged by a trusted policy engine with server-side provenance, fail-closed defaults, and quorum-based authorization for high-risk actions. It reframes agent safety from text filtering to enforcing an execution boundary around side effects.

entry.title: A decodability criterion predicts when hidden-state selection beats majority voting in large language models

author.name: Zhixiang wang, Ziliang Hong, Ulas Bagci

entry.summary: Introduces CASE, a linear gate on answer-token hidden states that picks among sampled candidate answers, along with a decodability criterion predicting when this beats majority voting. The key insight is that voting fails precisely when sampled errors are correlated, and hidden-state probes can be trusted only under measurable conditions.

entry.title: Do LLMs Know a Good Hypothesis When They See One? Logit-Based Energy Scoring Outperforms Prompted LLM-as-Judge for Scientific Hypothesis Ranking

author.name: Swati Rajwal, Sanjay Das, Tirthankar Ghosal

entry.summary: Compares prompted LLM-as-judge ranking against a logit-based energy score derived from the model's intrinsic confidence for identifying the correct scientific hypothesis among distractors, across 1,323 papers in 12 disciplines. Intrinsic scoring roughly doubled top-1 hit rate over listwise prompting.

entry.title: Neuro-symbolic learning over OWL 2 DL via consequence-based compilation to differentiable circuits

author.name: Olga Mashkova, Asaad Mohammedsaleh, Fernando Zhapa-Camacho, Robert Hoehndorf

entry.summary: Baobab compiles a full SROIQ description-logic ontology with a finite ABox into a sentential decision diagram, saturating a propositional core and instantiating nominals, number restrictions, and role axioms over the active domain. This lets neurosymbolic learning preserve classical entailment beyond the usual restriction to the Horn EL fragment.

entry.title: Adaptive Policy Portfolios for Robust Markov Decision Processes

author.name: Kasper Engelen, Sebastian Junges, Guillermo A. P\'{e}rez, Marnix Suilen

entry.summary: Studies portfolios of memoryless randomized policies synthesized offline for robust MDPs, paired with a lightweight online selector that adapts once deployment reveals which environment is actual. Uses robust regret as the quality objective and provides complexity results relative to prior safe policy improvement work.

entry.title: Procedural Content Metageneration via Program Search and Continual Abstraction Discovery

author.name: Matthew Siper, Ahmed Khalifa, Julian Togelius

entry.summary: Evolves complete Python level generators for four games using LLM-driven mutation and crossover, and introduces continual abstraction discovery that extracts reusable primitives from high-fitness programs into a run-specific helper library. A 2x2 design with 160 runs shows the abstraction mechanism improves final best fitness in all eight comparisons.

entry.title: Authorization Before Context: A Model-Neutral Audience Boundary Against Cross-Audience Memory Leakage in Agentic Systems

author.name: Sibo Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes enforcing an audience-membership check at the moment memories are assembled into an agent's prompt, so a fact learned in one social context cannot leak into a reply to a different audience. Each stored item carries the audience present at recording time, the current viewer set is read from channel metadata with a conservative public fallback, and admission requires an anti-monotone subset condition. It formalizes contextual integrity for personal agent memory in a model-agnostic way.

entry.title: Learning Where and What to Lift for Bi-planar X-ray-to-CT Reconstruction

author.name: Yifei Wu, Yicheng Wu, Qiang Ma, Qi Chen, Renyang Gu, Xinyu Liu, Yongsheng Pan, Yong Xia

entry.summary: LiftXR reconstructs CT volumes from only two X-ray views by interleaving explicit recovery of anatomical spatial layout with intensity estimation, on the premise that once regions are localized, predicting their attenuation values becomes far easier. It targets the severe ill-posedness of collapsing depth in sparse-view projection. Potentially reduces radiation dose and imaging cost.

entry.title: Beyond MSE: Rethinking the Evaluation Metric and Benchmarking for Irregular Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Rongwen Li, Haixin Xie, Xiao Wang, Changjian Chen

entry.summary: A companion evaluation paper showing that mean squared error in irregular time series forecasting is confounded by each sample's timestamp sampling distribution, producing biased rankings of models. The authors propose Continuous-time Squared Error, which uses importance weighting to remove that dependence, and prove bounds on its asymptotic estimation error relative to true continuous-time performance. It argues much prior benchmarking in this area is unreliable.

entry.title: SemComp-Bench: Benchmarking Semantic Task Completion in Video Generation

author.name: Keyu Tu, Zhuowei Chen, Mengqi Huang, Yuxin Wang, Jiahao Zhu, Zhendong Mao, Yongdong Zhang

entry.summary: SemComp-Bench defines an outcome-oriented video generation task where success requires achieving an intended end state and maintaining high-level semantic correspondence to a reference image, rather than showing complete intermediate steps or preserving appearance. It ships an evaluation dataset spanning six domains with reference images plus detailed and brief instructions. It shifts video generation evaluation toward task completion semantics.

entry.title: Coarse-to-Fine Multi-Resolution Diffusion Models for Trajectory Generation in Urban Systems

author.name: Wen Ye, Muyan Weng, Chuizheng Meng, Hao Niu, Yizhou Zhang, Yan Liu

entry.summary: MR-Traj generates synthetic human mobility trajectories with a multi-resolution diffusion model that composes coarse and fine spatial-temporal structure instead of only matching global distributions. The goal is privacy-preserving trajectory data whose utility holds up across resolutions used in real urban analyses.

entry.title: Metaplasticity as adaptive gradient preconditioning for incremental learning

author.name: Isabelle Aguilar, Zayn Andre Zainal, Omid Kavehei

entry.summary: SynGAP reinterprets synaptic metaplasticity as adaptive gradient preconditioning to give task-free continual learning without task labels or large replay buffers. It targets the stability-plasticity tradeoff in non-stationary streams with a biologically motivated optimizer-level mechanism.

entry.title: Randomly initialized autoencoders: fixed points and edge-of-chaos

author.name: Leonid Berlyand, Roman Sarapin, Yitzchak Shmalo, Victor Slavin, Sasha Sodin

entry.summary: This mathematical study characterizes autoencoders through their fixed points, analyzing existence, stability, and basins of attraction via contractivity, and links these properties to the edge-of-chaos initialization regime. It offers a dynamical-systems account of when randomly initialized autoencoders behave well.

entry.title: Training and Evaluating Ethical Reinforcement Learning Agents on Per-Episode Distributions

author.name: Prabhjyot Singh, Majid Ghasemi, Mark Crowley

entry.summary: The paper compares four ways to train ethically constrained RL agents in the Craftax survival benchmark, arguing that averaging rewards lets agents concentrate harm in a few episodes. It evaluates scalar penalties, multi-objective weight sweeps, adaptive Lagrangian constraints, and a non-compensatory per-episode utility under expected scalarized returns.

entry.title: Discrete Diffusion Language Models Are Training-Free Multi-Label Classifiers

author.name: Pawan Kumar

entry.summary: The paper uses masked discrete diffusion language models as training-free multi-label text classifiers by scoring yes-or-no questions at a single masked position, one label at a time. It documents a severe slot-position bias when all labels share one prompt and shows per-label scoring removes the asymmetry.

entry.title: Do Uncertainty Signals Help? A Systematic Study of Uncertainty-Aware Decoding with Rollback Mechanisms

author.name: Xianzong Wu, Xiaohong Li, Yuejun Guo, Xinyang Liu, Tianlin Li, Junjie Wang, Qiang Hu

entry.summary: The paper systematically studies uncertainty-aware rollback decoding for code generation, where uncertainty signals flag unreliable spans and generation restarts from an earlier valid prefix without retraining. It asks empirically how much value uncertainty signals actually add at inference time.

entry.title: Quantifying Depth Sufficiency in Residual Neural Networks: A First-Order Criterion

author.name: Zeyu Liu, Jinhao Zhang, Yunquan Zhang, Guangming Tan, Xiang Gao, Fangming Liu, Daning Cheng

entry.summary: This paper defines first-order residual depth saturation under a function-preserving residual-growth protocol and proves that adding depth has first-order value exactly when conditional activation gradients project nonzero onto some admissible residual tangent space. It gives a checkable criterion for whether a trained network is already deep enough.

entry.title: Does 1/2-Tsallis-INF Also Work Well for Best-Arm Identification?

author.name: Jingxin Zhan, Yuze Han, Zhihua Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzes whether the canonical best-of-both-worlds Tsallis-INF regret-minimization algorithm can also reliably identify the best arm, by bounding its failure probability when the empirical best arm is chosen from importance-weighted loss estimates. It probes the tension between regret minimization and pure exploration objectives.

entry.title: High-Dimensional Nonparametric Change-Point Detection via Low-Rank Degree-Three Density Projection

author.name: Guoqing Zhang, Zhaixin Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a nonparametric change-point detection method for high-dimensional data that captures shifts in third-order structure such as skewness and asymmetric interactions, which mean and covariance monitoring miss. It uses a symmetric order-three Legendre feature tensor that isometrically encodes the degree-three density projection while avoiding density estimation.

entry.title: UniFed-VLM: Federated Instruction Tuning for Vision-Language Models with Multiple Heterogeneity

author.name: Pengyu Wang, Baochen Xiong, Xiaoshan Yang, Yifan Xu, Zhang Qimeng, Haifeng Chen, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: UniFed-VLM tackles federated instruction tuning of vision-language models when clients differ simultaneously in tasks, modalities, and model architectures, a setting existing federated methods do not handle. It targets privacy-sensitive domains such as healthcare where centralizing multimodal data is not feasible.

entry.title: Guaranteed Adaptive Modality Acquisition: When the Policy Chooses Its Own Calibration Group

author.name: Melika Baghi

entry.summary: Analyzes conditional calibration when an adaptive policy decides which input modalities are ultimately acquired, so the grouping used for conditional guarantees is itself chosen by the policy rather than fixed in advance. It gives finite-sample constructions for valid pattern-conditional guarantees and a counterexample showing naive approaches fail.

entry.title: AdROD: HyperNetwork-based Adversarially Robust Object Detection for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yuting Wu, Dongfang Guo, Xiangzhong Luo, Qun Song, Rui Tan

entry.summary: AdROD defends camera-based object detectors against physical adversarial attacks by using low-rank hypernetworks to generate a fresh, diverse detector per frame, so attackers cannot obtain the deployed weights in time. It adds a functional-diversity mechanism and claims a parameter footprint of under two percent of standard hypernetworks for embedded automotive deployment.

entry.title: Demystifying Oversmoothing in Sheaf Neural Networks: An Index-Theoretic Criterion

author.name: Junwen Dong, Yuhan Peng, Hao Li, Huitao Feng, Kelin Xia

entry.summary: The paper argues that the dimension of the sheaf Laplacian kernel is a misleading indicator of a sheaf neural network's resistance to oversmoothing, since some configurations inflate that dimension with uninformative constant harmonic sections. It offers an index-theoretic, relative geometric criterion that characterizes genuine anti-oversmoothing capacity.

entry.title: The Trade-off Between Covariate Dependence and Latent Structure in Representation Learning

author.name: Ma{\l}gorzata {\L}az\k{e}cka, Ewa Szczurek

entry.summary: This paper unifies supervised disentanglement approaches and proves an inherent trade-off: when covariates are correlated, one cannot simultaneously enforce one-to-one latent-covariate alignment and latent independence or exclusivity. It clarifies why unsupervised independence objectives give no guarantee of semantic alignment.

entry.title: Pallas: A Proactive KV Cache Migration Framework for LLM Inference in AI-RAN

author.name: Tianhang Ding, Jianchun Liu, Hongli Xu

entry.summary: Pallas proactively migrates the key-value cache for in-flight LLM requests to the predicted target base station before a cellular handover completes, avoiding the choice between persistently higher inter-token latency and a long post-handover interruption. It targets AI-RAN deployments where inference runs at the network edge.

entry.title: Graph Machine Learning: An Opportunity for Power Systems

author.name: Martin Sadric, Sebastian P\"utz, Christian Nauck, Veit Hagenmeyer, Frank Hellmann, Dirk Witthaut, Benjamin Sch\"afer

entry.summary: This survey reviews nearly 800 papers at the intersection of graph machine learning and power systems, covering forecasting, state estimation, optimization, and control, and argues grid topology makes graph structure a natural inductive bias. It positions data-driven methods as the faster alternative to accurate but operationally slow model-based approaches.

entry.title: When Tool-Backed Skill Retrieval Fails: Source-Style Collapse in Executable Capability Retrieval

author.name: Yiqi Liu, Joseph James, Yang Wang, Chenghao Xiao, Chenghua Lin

entry.summary: The paper documents source-style collapse, where a retriever fine-tuned on one slice of a tool-retrieval benchmark fails badly on another slice of the same benchmark even with higher lexical overlap with the gold tools. It shows query-side TF-IDF fingerprints predict which source styles will break the fine-tuned retriever better than semantic or length proxies.

entry.title: From Errors to Proofs: Minimal-Core-Guided Repair for Neuro-Symbolic Constraint Solving

author.name: Dipankar Sarkar

entry.summary: When a language model translates a word problem into a formal specification and the solver finds it unsatisfiable, this method returns a minimal unsatisfiable core of the model's own constraints instead of a generic error message, giving a leakage-free localization of the faulty translation. This turns silent wrong-but-runnable programs into repairable ones on a new constraint benchmark.

entry.title: When do machine-learned exchange-correlation improvements inherit into density-functional tight binding?

author.name: Can Polat, Mustafa Kurban, Erchin Serpedin, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: The paper asks whether machine-learned exchange-correlation functionals that improve band gaps in density functional theory pass their improvements down when used to parameterize cheaper tight-binding models, and finds systematic anti-transfer that moves gaps the wrong way. The explanation is a representational mismatch: modern functionals are orbital-dependent operators while the parameterization channel assumes a multiplicative potential.

entry.title: SkillComposer: Learning Reusable Skills for Natural-Language Robot Programming

author.name: John Woods, Hasti Seifi

entry.summary: SkillComposer is an interactive natural-language robot programming system in simulation that iteratively generates and tests programs, then feeds successful ones into an online library-learning algorithm that compresses recurring function sequences into reusable abstractions. This targets language model failures on multi-step task decomposition and solution reuse.

entry.title: Scale-Consistent Posterior Dynamics for Diffusion Inverse Problems

author.name: Zhaoqiang Liu, Tongyao Pang, Ruibing Wang, Yang Zheng

entry.summary: For solving inverse problems with pretrained diffusion priors, the authors start from a one-parameter family of posterior stochastic differential equations that trade deterministic transport against stochastic exploration without changing marginals, then build tractable likelihood proxies in rescaled clean-image coordinates organized by log signal-to-noise ratio. Projecting diffusion uncertainty through the forward operator yields a noise-conditioned covariance path with endpoint consistency.

entry.title: Improved Regret Analysis for Parallel Gaussian Process Bandit Optimization

author.name: Shion Takeno, Shogo Iwazaki

entry.summary: Improves regret bounds for batched Gaussian process bandit optimization, showing that the multiplicative dependence on batch size can be removed without the initial uncertainty-sampling phase that prior analyses required but that works poorly in practice. It also derives substantially tighter bounds in the noiseless setting.

entry.title: Density-Reweighted Entropic Optimal Transport: Decoupling Geometry from Sampling Density

author.name: Keyi Li, Yuval Kluger, Boris Landa

entry.summary: Points out that entropic optimal transport can match points between two datasets by relative sampling density rather than genuine geometric proximity when the datasets share similar low-dimensional structure but differ in density. The proposed density-reweighted framework lets practitioners discount the density influence to a chosen degree, restoring geometry-driven correspondences.

entry.title: Probing Association Instability with Track-State Perturbations for Clip-Level Active Learning in Query-Propagation Multi-Object Tracking

author.name: Riku Inoue, Shogo Sato, Kazuhiko Murasaki, Tomoyasu Shimada, Toshihiko Nishimura, Ryuichi Tanida

entry.summary: QPID is a clip-level active learning acquisition method for query-propagation multi-object tracking that measures association instability by applying two-sided perturbations to internal track states and observing prediction differences. This targets informative clips that output-level temporal uncertainty criteria miss, reducing the cost of dense box and identity annotation across video.

entry.title: Heterogeneity-Aware Deep Learning for Tumour Classification from Multiparametric MRI

author.name: Yue Xia, Euijoon Ahn, Tian Xia, Yuan Yuan, Michael Fulham, Jinman Kim

entry.summary: Proposes a heterogeneity-aware deep learning framework for tumour classification from multiparametric MRI that automatically generates imaging-derived tumour sub-regions rather than relying on whole-tumour representations or manually drawn sub-regions. The sub-region modeling is applied to both lesion-type diagnosis and molecular-status prediction.

entry.title: Primitive Representation Learning for Unsupervised Dynamic Contrast Enhanced MRI Reconstruction

author.name: Veronika Spieker, Wenqi Huang, Cemre Ariyurek, Liam Timms, Daniel Rueckert, Onur Afacan, Julia A. Schnabel, Sila Kurugol

entry.summary: OYS treats diffusion sampling timestep selection as a black-box optimization problem and uses Bayesian optimization to tune schedules against the target quality metric directly, rather than optimizing theoretical surrogates. It reportedly beats default schedules and a prior schedule-optimization method on text-to-image generation.

entry.title: PDDL-ART: Autonomous Symbolic Abstraction From Demonstration For Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation Using Vision-Language Models

author.name: Disha Kamale, Dmitry Berenson

entry.summary: PDDL-ART uses a vision-language model to autonomously generate task-specific PDDL domain and problem descriptions from a single expert demonstration, a language task description, and a list of action names, without templates, action signatures, or fine-tuning. It adds checks so generated symbolic descriptions are semantically consistent with the demonstration, not merely syntactically valid. This attacks the long-standing domain-engineering bottleneck in symbolic task planning for long-horizon manipulation.

entry.title: UniReflex: Plug-and-Play Force Control for Pretrained Generative Policies via Fast-Slow Reflex

author.name: Yan Huang, Shoujie Li, Ziwu Song, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: UniReflex adds variable impedance force control to frozen generative imitation policies without retraining the backbone, by intercepting latent representations from the action head and driving a fast reflex network. It predicts anisotropic stiffness directions to separate commanded force exertion from response to external contact, guided by force-direction intent recorded during demonstrations. This gives existing diffusion or flow policies contact regulation they normally lack.

entry.title: ControlledShifts: Towards Standardizing Robustness Evaluation in Trajectory Prediction Under Distribution Shifts

author.name: Ingrid navarro, Pablo Ortega-Kral, Yutong Duan, Jonathan Francis, Jean Oh

entry.summary: ControlledShifts standardizes robustness evaluation for autonomous driving trajectory prediction by re-splitting existing datasets into seen and unseen partitions using a shared characterization-and-splitting procedure, so distribution-shift claims can be compared on common axes. It responds to a literature where generalization is validated along fragmented, incomparable dimensions. Standardized shift benchmarks are a prerequisite for measuring real safety progress.

entry.title: Policy Optimization and Statistical Inference for Online Contextual Matrix Games

author.name: Liner Xiang, Yixin Wang, Hengrui Cai

entry.summary: The authors define online contextual matrix games, which combine contextual bandit style feature dependence with multi-player strategic interaction so payoffs evolve with observed context rather than remaining fixed. They provide policy optimization procedures and statistical inference tools for the resulting equilibria, motivated by competitive pricing. It fills a gap between contextual bandits and repeated matrix games.

entry.title: Funding Formal Methods for the Cyberpocalypse

author.name: Max von Hippel

entry.summary: This post argues that AI-driven offensive cyber capability is scaling faster than defense, that offense is structurally easier than defense, and that many sectors are institutionally slow to patch, so philanthropic and public funding should flow into formal methods and verified software. It makes a case for verification as a defense-side force multiplier against agentic and human-directed attacks. The argument is programmatic and funding-oriented.

entry.title: For Claude, capability and dispreferring CDT are the ~same thing. Much more so than for GPT.

author.name: Chi Nguyen

entry.summary: Building on decision-theory benchmarking work, this post reports that for Anthropic models, capability scores and the tendency to disprefer causal decision theory answers are almost perfectly correlated, near 0.95 to 0.97 on two capability measures and also with release date, whereas the correlation is much weaker for OpenAI models. The pattern is claimed to be replicated in Anthropic model cards for existing releases such as Opus 4.7 and Fable 5. It suggests developer-specific coupling between general capability and decision-theoretic disposition.

entry.title: CityReal: Human-Aligned Urban Behavior and City Dynamics Simulation with Large-Scale LLM Agents

author.name: Nicolas Bougie, Xiaotong Ye, Narimasa Watanabe

entry.summary: CityReal simulates urban populations with LLM agents modeled as intention-driven planners that maintain coherent mobility plans and adapt habits over time, rather than making isolated step-by-step choices from few-shot prompts. The aim is to align simulated behavior with a target population instead of reproducing the base model's behavioral priors.

entry.title: Sparse Coverage: Semantic Center Representations for Patent Prior-Art Retrieval

author.name: You Zuo (ALMAnaCH), Kim Gerdes (LISN, Qatent, STL), \'Eric de la Clergerie (ALMAnaCH), Beno\^it Sagot (ALMAnaCH)

entry.summary: Sparse Coverage is an unsupervised retrieval method for patent prior-art search that maps span-level embeddings onto a sparse vocabulary of embedding-space centers chosen by a k-center coverage objective, yielding sparse codes usable with inverted indexes. On CLEF-IP 2013 it matches or beats strong dense patent encoders on document recall. It bridges dense semantics and the efficiency of sparse retrieval for long technical documents.

entry.title: The 10th AI City Challenge

author.name: Zheng Tang, Shuo Wang, David C. Anastasiu, Ming-Ching Chang, Anuj Sharma, Quan Kong, Munkhjargal Gochoo, Jun-Wei Hsieh, Tomasz Kornuta, Zhedong Zheng, Renran Tian, Judah Goldfeder, Fulgencio Navarro, Yuxing Wang, Yizhou Wang, Sameer Satish Pusegaonkar, Anqi Li, Nalin Dadhich, Ridham Kachhadiya, Dhanishtha Patil, Haoquan Liang, Jiajun Li, Han Zhang, Yilin Zhao, Zaid Pervaiz Bhat, Shuyu Yang, Ashutosh Kumar, Rong Wang, Rafael Martin Nieto, Peter Christiansen, Ahmed Abduljawad, Mohanrasu Shanmugam, Nadeem Shaik, Sujit Biswas, Xunlei Wu, Vidya Murali, Rama Chellappa

entry.summary: A summary of the tenth AI City Challenge held with ECCV 2026, covering six tracks spanning multi-camera 3D perception, transportation safety captioning and VQA, traffic anomaly reasoning, text-based person anomaly search, generative traffic video, and privacy-preserving evaluation, with 325 teams from 26 countries. It documents a decade of benchmark evolution in physical AI and smart cities. Useful as a snapshot of community SOTA in transportation perception.

entry.title: Teach and Grow: An Agent-Centered Architecture for General Robot Learning

author.name: Chang Nie, Zhe Liu, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: Teach-and-Grow Learning is an agent-centered robot architecture in which a multimodal agent converts a handful of successful demonstrations into reusable closed-loop Skill Blocks, aiming to avoid the retraining cycle that end-to-end vision-language-action models require whenever they encounter out-of-coverage objects, sensors, or embodiments. The authors frame this recurring cost as a retraining tax on embodied data. It offers a modular alternative to monolithic robot foundation models.

entry.title: NeuroAbs: A Neuro-Symbolic RTL Abstraction Framework for Property Checking Acceleration

author.name: Zhiyuan Yan, Xiaofeng Zhou, Ziyue Zheng, Ziyi Yang, Wenbin Che, Wei Zhang, Yangdi Lyu, Hongce Zhang

entry.summary: NeuroAbs uses an LLM to analyze register-transfer-level hardware designs and propose which signals to abstract, then couples LLM-generated abstractions with symbolic checks to accelerate formal property verification. It aims to replace manual effort or rigid rule-based abstraction heuristics. Applies neuro-symbolic methods to a bottleneck in hardware verification.

entry.title: Learning What Not to Learn: Adversarial Disentangled Prompt Tuning for Robust Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yang Chen, Zhan Zhuang, Yanbin Wei, Zebin Chen, Hua Liu, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: ADAPT tackles the finding that adversarial prompt tuning of vision-language models overfits robustness to seen classes by learning non-generalizable shortcut features. It uses a target prompt alongside a pool of decoy prompts that absorb these pseudo-robust features during training, following a learn-what-not-to-learn strategy. Improves zero-shot adversarial robustness to unseen classes.

entry.title: Explainable AI-Powered Framework for Video-Based Skill Assessment in Cataract Surgery

author.name: Mohammad Javad Ahmadi, Hamid D. Taghirad

entry.summary: The authors release what they describe as the largest cataract surgery video dataset, comprising 2,000 recordings, alongside an explainable computer-vision and signal-processing pipeline that derives objective quantitative indicators of surgical skill. The goal is to supplement or replace subjective human scoring in surgical training. Data scale is the main contribution.

entry.title: Learnware for CSI Feedback: Scene-specific Small Models Can Do Big

author.name: Xiangyi Li, Jiajia Guo, Chao-Kai Wen, Xin Geng, Shi Jin, Zhi-Hua Zhou

entry.summary: The paper applies the Learnware paradigm to 6G channel state information feedback, maintaining a central repository of scene-specific small models each described by a specification so base stations can identify and reuse a suitable model instead of retraining end to end. This targets the generalization-versus-specialization tradeoff between large and small CSI networks. A concrete deployment of model-marketplace ideas in wireless systems.

entry.title: AdaLens: Interactive Storyline for Monitoring and Steering Long-Running Agentic Data Analysis

author.name: Yangtian Liu, Yan Miao, Shuhan Liu, Yunfan Zhou, Dae Hyun Kim, Di Weng, Yingcai Wu

entry.summary: AdaLens is an interactive interface that renders a long-running data-analysis agent as an evolving storyline so users can observe branching reasoning and steer it mid-execution. It targets the observability and steerability gap left by chat-style, turn-by-turn agent UIs.

entry.title: Traceable Trust for action-ready artificial intelligence in bioscience

author.name: Huayu Xin, Yizhi Cai, Mukilan Deivarajan Suresh, Gavin Michael Farrell, Iwona Gajda, Charlie Harrison, Conor Houghton, Mato Lagator, Yang Lu, Virginia Portillo, Reyer Zwiggelaar, Sebastian Lobentanzer

entry.summary: A large interdisciplinary group proposes Traceable Trust, a governance framework for the moment when an AI output is used to authorize a physical laboratory action in the biosciences. It specifies questions about evidence, claimed capability, delegated agency, action thresholds, override authority, and feedback loops.

entry.title: Disentangling Homophily and Rarity: Explaining Failure in Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Preben M. Ness, Fariz Ikhwantri, Dusica Marijan

entry.summary: The authors disentangle whether heterophilic nodes are hard for graph neural networks because of heterophily itself or because they are rare, evaluating six GNNs on five datasets spanning homophily levels. They find homophilic nodes are easier even when rare, undercutting the subgroup-generalization explanation while nuancing aggregation-based accounts.

entry.title: Look Before You Lift: Visual and Quantitative Diagnostics for Topological Deep Learning

author.name: Mathilde Papillon, Guillermo Bern\'ardez, \'Alvaro Ball\'on Barreiro, Marco Montagna, R\'emi Devaux, Antoine Jardin, Nina Miolane

entry.summary: TopoExplorer provides visual and quantitative diagnostics for the lifting step in topological deep learning, using augmented Hasse graph representations so practitioners can inspect the higher-order neighborhoods a lifting actually induces. It converts a commonly black-box preprocessing choice into an inspectable design decision.

entry.title: Understanding and Stabilizing Deep Q-Learning via Controlled Bootstrapping and Regulated Value Dynamics

author.name: Bozhou Chen, Yongyi Wang, Hanyu Liu, Xionghui Yang, Wenxin Li

entry.summary: This study analyzes deep Q-learning instability jointly from three angles: operator-level bias in Bellman bootstrapping, sensitivity of greedy action selection to regression noise, and parameter-dynamics imbalance under heavy data reuse. It identifies a reward-triggered self-reinforcing failure mode and proposes controlled bootstrapping with regulated value dynamics as stabilizers.

entry.title: Beyond Boundary Noise: Aggregated Aleatoric Uncertainty Fails to Capture Presence Ambiguity in 3D Lung Nodule Segmentation

author.name: Simon Baur, Arne Schernich, Ekin B\"oke, Wojciech Samek, Jackie Ma

entry.summary: Across four segmentation architectures with Monte Carlo dropout and deep ensembles on lung nodule datasets, the authors show that entropy-based aggregated aleatoric uncertainty largely reflects boundary disagreement and fails to capture the clinically crucial question of whether a lesion is present at all. External validation on a second cohort supports the conclusion.

entry.title: Spinning Conformal Correlators from Neural Networks

author.name: Manas Dogra, James Halverson, Joydeep Naskar

entry.summary: Building on prior neural-network constructions of scalar conformal field theories, this work constructs spinning conformal fields using the embedding formalism and computes two-, three- and four-point functions, recovering the four-dimensional Maxwell conformal field theory in the infinite-width limit for a particular independent-neuron ensemble. It extends the neural network to field theory correspondence to fields with spin.

entry.title: NeuRoute: Logit-Guided Neural Routing for Billion-Scale Vector Search with Sub-Hour Index Construction

author.name: Xingqiao Wang, Zi Wang, Xiaowei Xu

entry.summary: Introduces a learned binary hashing index for billion-scale approximate nearest neighbor search that uses a small neural encoder to assign vectors to balanced buckets and treats the encoder logits as an uncertainty signal for adaptive query routing. The headline claim is index construction in under an hour at billion scale.

entry.title: Generalized Linear Bandits with Memory

author.name: Heesang Ann, Hyunjun Choi, Taehyun Hwang, Younghoon Shin, Haeju Cheong, Min-hwan Oh

entry.summary: Shows that a previously reported regret rate for linear bandits whose rewards depend on past actions through a finite memory was an artifact of loose analysis, recovering the standard square-root-of-time rate, then extends the sharpened result to generalized linear models with a block-wise algorithm using shrunken confidence bounds. The setting models endogenous non-stationarity such as user fatigue.

entry.title: A Glyph Is Not a Letter, a Token Is Not a Word, a Space Is Not a Space: What the Units of Voynichese Are Not

author.name: Liudmila Rozanova, Alexander Temerev

entry.summary: Tests the three unstated assumptions behind Voynich manuscript analysis, that glyphs are letters, blank-delimited strings are words, and every blank is a word space, against a standard transliteration with prose, cipher, and pseudo-text controls. All three fail in a consistent way: the statistical order lives at token edges and graded boundaries rather than in token succession, and glyph conditional entropy is far too low for one-to-one substitution of any tested plaintext.

entry.title: REChart: Reasoning-Efficient Chart Editing with Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Yuanbang Liu, Chenxi Ruan, Yihan Hou, Qiong Luo, Wei Zeng

entry.summary: REChart studies chart editing with large reasoning models and reports an inverted-U relation between chain-of-thought length and accuracy, where excessive reasoning causes hallucinated visual details and redundant loops. A two-stage training framework with process-level supervision aims to keep reasoning short and grounded.

entry.title: DynaForcing: Overcoming Dynamic Collapse in Self-Forcing Distillation for Streaming Avatar Generation

author.name: Yubo Huang, Sirui Zhao, Xinchen Yao, Zhengye Zhang, Jinyang Huang, Fengqi Cui, Shiwei Wu, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: DynaForcing characterizes dynamic collapse in self-forcing distillation for streaming avatar generation, where the student converges to a nearly static but visually clean solution, tracing it to the mode-seeking reverse KL objective and unanchored self-conditioning feedback. Fixes target both causes to restore lip-sync and expressive motion.

entry.title: Initialization-Free Bundle Adjustment Revisited: A Controlled Experimental Study

author.name: Simon Weber, Mateo de Mayo, Je Hyeong Hong, Carl Olsson, Daniel Cremers, Ronald Clark

entry.summary: This controlled experimental study revisits initialization-free bundle adjustment, combining a C++ implementation of object-space-error formulations with a synthetic generator providing exact ground truth. It asks whether low objective values from variable projection actually correspond to valid metric 3D reconstructions, which prior evaluations did not check.

entry.title: Hierarchical Data Selection via Manifold Coverage and Sparse Feature Coverage in LLM Post-training

author.name: Peng Sun, Yi Yang, Antong Zhang, Chunxiao Li, Yanbo Wang, Dianbo Liu, xin chen, Kai Yu, Lu Chen, Tianfan Fu

entry.summary: MASS selects supervised fine-tuning data for LLM post-training as a coarse-to-fine coverage problem, using autoencoder-learned principal manifold coordinates for semantic grouping and a top-k sparse autoencoder for quality-aware feature coverage within groups. This avoids diversity metrics computed in entangled raw embedding spaces.

entry.title: Lambda-Hold Control: Human-Like Movement Emerges from a Minimal Task Reward in Predictive Musculoskeletal Simulation

author.name: Jun Hyuk Lee, Chihyeong Lee, Jooeun Ahn

entry.summary: The paper introduces a controller for musculoskeletal simulation whose action variable is a per-muscle equilibrium-point threshold length, with muscle excitations generated automatically by a stretch-reflex recruitment law. Holding these thresholds over gait-phase intervals sharply shrinks the effective action space, making RL exploration tractable and producing human-like movement from a minimal task reward. It connects motor-control neuroscience hypotheses to practical RL action parameterization.

entry.title: Embodied-Navigator: Point, Think, Memorize, and Align for Efficient Navigation

author.name: Hongyan Feng, Sunlai Chen, Xuanyu Liu, Miao Pan, Yangfan Xie, Yuxiang Cui, Zhongxiang Zhou, Rong Xiong, Wenqi Zhang, Jianwei Yin, Yueting Zhuang, Xuhong Zhang

entry.summary: This navigation framework (called Embodied-Navigator in the title and TAMP-Nav in the abstract) reformulates embodied navigation as 2D visual prompting, having the VLM select pixels that are then projected into 3D targets for a SLAM controller, thereby matching the model's 2D pretraining priors. It adds adaptive reasoning scheduling and memory management for efficiency. The design avoids forcing VLMs into unnatural discrete action spaces.

entry.title: Tight Sample Bounds for Renyi and Min-Entropy Estimation

author.name: Arman Adibi, Piotr Krysta

entry.summary: The authors characterize the sample complexity of estimating min-entropy and Renyi entropy of order greater than one over a k-symbol alphabet, proving that min-entropy estimation to constant additive accuracy requires order k log k samples, with a simple estimator based on the largest empirical frequency and dyadic-grouping concentration. Lower bounds extend to non-integer orders above roughly 1.001. This completes a picture that was well understood only for Shannon entropy.

entry.title: Price recursion is the rational theory of reward

author.name: Abhimanyu Pallavi Sudhir

entry.summary: Written as part of MATS work, this post argues that market price recursion provides a rational-agent theory of reward, demonstrating formal analogies between markets and Markov decision processes with Bellman updates, and between chain markets and multilayer networks with backpropagation. It positions markets as rationalizing reward in the same way Bayesian inference rationalizes beliefs. It situates the result within a long lineage of market-based RL architectures.

entry.title: Improving the matrix multiplication exponent with modern optimization and AlphaEvolve

author.name: Emilien Dupont, Marvin Eisenberger, Borislav Kozlovskii, Abbas Mehrabian, Francisco J. R. Ruiz, Abigail See, Renfei Zhou, Josh Alman, Virginia Vassilevska Williams, Matej Balog

entry.summary: Already covered in yesterday's Research roundup, Improves the best known upper bound on the matrix multiplication exponent to below 2.371177 by reformulating the optimization problem at the heart of combination loss analysis, designing a new ML-based optimizer for it, and then refining that optimizer with AlphaEvolve. The author list joins Google DeepMind researchers with the complexity theorists who hold the previous records.

entry.title: Quantifying Risk Under Evolving Uncertainty: Belief-Dependent Robustness for Safe Sequential Decision Making

author.name: Deep Kumar Ganguly, Jan Kretinsky

entry.summary: RATTL ties an agent's caution to its epistemic uncertainty by planning against a Wasserstein ambiguity set whose radius shrinks as a Bayesian posterior over dynamics sharpens. Behavior interpolates smoothly between worst-case robustness while ignorant and risk-neutral optimization once the environment is known.

entry.title: Beyond Suspicious Steps: Ontological Trust in Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: An He, Yao Wang, Haibin Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces ontological trust, a measure of whether an agent's evolving trajectory prefix still corresponds to the task the user authorized, rather than whether each individual action looks locally valid. Aims to catch quiet goal drift where every tool call is plausible but the overall objective has shifted.

entry.title: SPACE: Sample-cloud Predictive Adaptive Conformal Ellipsoids for Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Baishi Li, Kelvin J. L. Koa, Ke-Wei Huang

entry.summary: SPACE is a conformal wrapper for probabilistic forecasters that emit sample clouds, constructing adaptive multivariate prediction ellipsoids from the geometry of the current forecast samples rather than from historical residual windows. This avoids stale-regime contamination while retaining online coverage calibration. Relevant to risk-aware multivariate forecasting under distribution shift.

entry.title: Domain-Adapted Molecular Language Models for Efficient Search of Make-on-Demand Libraries

author.name: Henrik Wille, Luis-Finley Sch\"utz, Felix Strieth-Kalthoff

entry.summary: A systematic benchmark of four pretrained molecular language models as encoders across six virtual libraries spanning drug discovery, organic materials, and catalysis, finding that classical molecular fingerprints remain a consistently strong baseline while learned embeddings vary widely by domain. Explicit domain adaptation substantially closes the gap. A useful negative-result-style corrective for chemistry representation learning.

entry.title: Grading Needs a Rubric, Not Intelligence

author.name: Jhen-Ke Lin

entry.summary: The study shows that cheap small models grade open-ended exam answers about as reliably as expensive models when given an explicit rubric extracted once by a frontier model at ingestion. Variance analysis attributes over 95 percent of score variation to the answer itself rather than the grading model.

entry.title: Harnessing Magnitude-Only and Complex Measurements for Improved Dynamic MRI Reconstruction with Learned Priors

author.name: Mahdi Saberi, Ya\c{s}ar Utku Al\c{c}alar, Merve G\"{u}lle, Chetan Shenoy, Mehmet Ak\c{c}akaya

entry.summary: The authors show that k-space magnitude measurements are highly consistent across time frames in steady-state dynamic MRI and use this auxiliary magnitude information alongside complex data in a physics-driven learned reconstruction. This borrows ideas from sparse phase retrieval without extra scan time.

entry.title: P2E-VQ: ECG-linked representation augmentation for PPG via discrete patch retrieval

author.name: Zhongli Wu, Zhuangzhi Gao, He Zhao, Feixiang Zhou, Fu Wang, Jinru Ding, Yuankai Wang, Hongyi Qin, Gregory Y. H. Lip, Bil Kirmani, Yalin Zheng

entry.summary: P2E-VQ improves cardiac prediction from wearable PPG signals by retrieving discrete ECG-linked patch representations instead of attempting ill-posed waveform reconstruction of the ECG. The insight is that faithful signal reconstruction does not necessarily improve downstream diagnosis.

entry.title: Unraveling the Size Determination Mechanism of Nanocrystal Synthesis via Interpretable Neural Networks

author.name: Kai Gu, Haizheng Zhong

entry.summary: NanoEQL is a fully white-box equation-learning network that fits explicit mathematical expressions for how precursors and reaction conditions determine nanocrystal size, using new operators that avoid gradient explosion at singularities. It aims to extract mechanistic insight rather than only predictions from synthesis data.

entry.title: Decision-Driven Regularization: A Blended Model for Learning and Optimization

author.name: Gar Goei Loke, Qinshen Tang, Yangge Xiao, Xun Zhang

entry.summary: For contextual optimization problems, this work shows that integrated predict-then-optimize training can overfit and underperform simple decoupled learning when prediction accuracy is not controlled. It proposes a bi-objective blend that regularizes the decision-focused loss with a prediction-accuracy term.

entry.title: FinFraudBench: A Heterogeneous Graph Benchmark for Financial Fraud Detection

author.name: Yixuan Chen, Hongyu Zhan, Jie Sheng, Weiyu Han, Shuai Chen, Tianyi Zhang, Xiao Tan, Jun Xia

entry.summary: FinFraudBench is a heterogeneous graph benchmark for financial fraud detection that preserves the multi-entity, multi-relational structure of real financial systems across customers, cards, merchants, categories, and locations. It aims to fix the oversimplification in existing homogeneous or single-node-type fraud benchmarks.

entry.title: Invariant Pretraining for Robust Code Representations

author.name: Yifeng He, Yundi Xu, Christopher Castro Gaw Gonzalo, Zili Wang, Hao Chen

entry.summary: Documents that encoder-based code models lose substantial accuracy under semantics-preserving program rewrites, then closes much of the gap with a code-only continued pretraining recipe that applies invariant transformations combined with masked objectives. Evaluation spans four encoders, two tasks, and four datasets.

entry.title: Benchmarking Quantum Machine Learning for Power-System Attack Detection: Evaluation Choices Decide the Outcome Before the Models Do

author.name: Md Rezwanul Islam

entry.summary: Benchmarks quantum kernel and variational classifiers against tuned classical models for power-system attack detection under white-box, transfer, black-box, and poisoning attacks, and finds that eight evaluation and tuning choices each individually flip a headline conclusion. The largest effect comes from whether data splits are made at the row level or by source file.

entry.title: Temporal Graph Prototype-conditioned Conformal Prediction for Fraud Detection

author.name: Xudong Chen, Shengbo Gong, Lu Cheng, Wei Jin

entry.summary: Adapts conformal prediction to edge-level fraud detection on temporal interaction graphs, where fraudulent edges sit in benign-dominated neighborhoods and extreme imbalance leaves too few labeled frauds for class-conditional calibration. Prototype conditioning is used to produce tighter prediction sets while retaining coverage.

entry.title: TransfHAR: Self-Supervised Wrist Representations for On-Demand Activity Recognition

author.name: Aidan Bradshaw, Riku Arakawa, Xin Liu, Karan Ahuja

entry.summary: TransfHAR pretrains on large amounts of unlabeled coarse wrist IMU data such as sitting, walking, and exercise, and shows the learned motion priors transfer to fine-grained manipulative and gestural activities never seen in pretraining. It is implemented as a real-time smartwatch application for on-demand recognition.

entry.title: Deploying Frontier Agentic Technology in MOOSEnger, a Multiphysics-Capable AI Assistant

author.name: Zaid Abulawi, Mengnan Li, Guillaume Giudicelli, Yang Liu, Cody Permann

entry.summary: Extends MOOSEnger, a domain-specific AI agent for a national-lab multiphysics finite-element framework, with a harness aimed at locally hosted models that retrieves repository context, validates generated inputs by running the simulation executable, and stores lessons from failures. The goal is to lower the expertise barrier for multiphysics simulation.

entry.title: NICE: Scale-Stable Perturbations for Graph Neural Network Explanations via Noise Corruption

author.name: Ziluowen Luo, Jun Yin, Ruochen Liu, Ming Cheng, Shirui Pan, Chengqi Zhang, Senzhang Wang

entry.summary: This work identifies scale drift, a systematic contraction of message magnitudes caused by the element-wise masking used in most post-hoc GNN explainers, which compounds across message-passing layers and corrupts the prediction changes used to infer importance. The proposed NICE perturbation replaces masking with noise corruption to keep activation scale stable.

entry.title: ETHOS: Towards a Modular Ethics Framework for Clinical Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Rakesh Sharma, Sydney Pugh, Cameron Beeche, Pankhuri Singhal, Rachel Wu, Margaret Eby, Jeffrey Duda, James Gee, Kyra O'Brien, Hersh Sagreiya, Marina Serper, Victoria Gershuni, Angela Bradbury, Anurag Verma, Eric Eaton, Kevin B. Johnson, Walter Witschey

entry.summary: Presents a modular ethics and oversight framework for clinical multi-agent LLM systems, aiming to turn high-level healthcare AI governance principles from bodies like the WHO into implementable hierarchical oversight components. The large clinical author list from a medical school gives it practitioner grounding.

entry.title: Large Models for Small Devices: Recent Advances and Empirical Analysis of Edge AI Deployment

author.name: Subhransu Das, Jiaming Cheng, Arnav Kumar, Sadia Afrose, Mingzhe Han, Michael Silagy, Shreya Palande, Brijesh Soni, Rajiv Ramnath

entry.summary: Proposes rewarding a conversational recommender for asking questions that measurably reduce its own uncertainty, quantified as entropy over candidate recommendations, rather than relying on ground-truth labels or another LLM judging interactivity. This gives a self-supervised signal for eliciting user preferences over multiple turns.

entry.title: Inferential Evaluation of Surrogate-Derived Models under Covariate Shift

author.name: Longtian Shi, Molei Liu, Doudou Zhou

entry.summary: Tackles how to evaluate a model trained on abundant surrogate labels when it is deployed on a target population where gold-standard outcomes are unobserved and covariates shift. The authors propose cross-fitted estimators that transport information from a small gold-labeled source and a larger surrogate-labeled source to the unlabeled target under conditional transportability.

entry.title: Random Quadratic Form with random forcing: Metastable synchronization by noise

author.name: Anna Shalova

entry.summary: A mathematical analysis of the random quadratic form on a sphere under small Brownian forcing, showing that arbitrarily small noise breaks the intrinsic symmetry and converts partial synchronization into full synchronization over two timescales. The work characterizes the metastable anti-polar configuration reached first and the slower symmetry-driven merger of clusters.

entry.title: MSEditor: Toward Consistent Multi-Shot Video Editing

author.name: Kunyu Feng, Yue Ma, Bingyuan Wang, Yuefeng Wang, Zhiyuan Qin, Hao Cheng, Hao Li, Qifeng Chen, Zeyu Wang

entry.summary: MSEditor targets consistent editing across multi-shot videos, where discontinuous segments with varying viewpoint, scale and pose cause identity drift and error accumulation. The authors repurpose existing single-shot data to build multi-shot training pairs and add cross-shot semantic awareness to maintain subject appearance.

entry.title: DistillPath: An Efficient 22M Distilled Pathology Encoder Approaching Large Foundation Model Performance

author.name: Ramon Kaspar, Andrey Ignatov, Valentina Boeva

entry.summary: DistillPath distills large pathology foundation encoders into a 22M-parameter vision transformer using only teacher class and patch tokens and six thousand public slides, without needing self-distillation heads or billion-tile corpora. The compact encoder approaches large foundation model performance while being far cheaper to run on commodity hardware.

entry.title: aDSL: Agentic 3D Creation via Joint Agent-Program Design

author.name: Rui-Huan Wang, Si-Tong Wei, Jia-Qi He, Heng-Yi Wei, Baoquan Chen, Peng-Shuai Wang

entry.summary: aDSL jointly designs an agent-centric domain-specific language and a role-specialized multi-agent system for programmatic 3D content creation, arguing that LLM agents fail because existing 3D interfaces demand fragile numeric choices rather than semantic and relational reasoning. The DSL exposes spatial relations and constraints that better match LLM strengths.

entry.title: Reuse Before You Retrieve: Diagnosing Headroom and Complementarity for Test-Time Augmentation of Embodied Multimodal Policies

author.name: Yuhwan Jeong, Kuk-Jin Yoon

entry.summary: This paper asks when a deployed frozen VLA policy should be improved by extra sampling versus by retrieving external demonstrations, and formalizes the decision through two measurable quantities: recoverable headroom in the policy's own stochastic rollouts and complementarity of an external action prior. The diagnostic framing gives practitioners guidance instead of defaulting to one intervention. It is a rare attempt to make test-time augmentation choices empirical rather than ad hoc.

entry.title: DeAR: Decentralized Agentic Reasoning via Capability Grounding and Collaborative Thought Navigation

author.name: Xing Wei, Changmeng Zheng, XiaoYong Wei, Xiufen Ye, Qing Li

entry.summary: DeAR replaces centralized orchestration in multi-agent reasoning with peer-to-peer collaboration, using query-dependent capability grounding, targeted thought-map navigation, and adaptive topology updates for error correction. It reports gains over recent baselines across nine multimodal and text QA benchmarks.

entry.title: Depth Enables Local Entropy: Quadratic Depth Dependence in Deep Variation-Norm ReLU Regression

author.name: Tao Jiang, Minbo Gao, Shaowei Cai

entry.summary: Proves that the quadratic dependence on depth in minimax rates for Gaussian regression over deep bounded-variation ReLU architectures is intrinsic, closing a gap of one depth factor between known upper and lower bounds. The construction uses a local packing with bias-corrected approximation and balanced amplification.

entry.title: PACE: Policy-Attested Contract Execution for Safe AI Agents in Decentralized Finance

author.name: Rabimba Karanjai (Larry), Yang Lu (Larry), Richard Williamson (Larry), Hemanth Hm (Larry), Prakhar Mehrotra (Larry), Lei Xu (Larry), Weidong (Larry), Shi

entry.summary: PACE inserts a transaction-level authorization layer between an LLM-driven DeFi agent and on-chain execution, using typed transaction intents, a deterministic policy verifier, and signed policy decision records that cryptographically bind the approved intent, policy version, and simulation result to the transaction actually submitted. This closes the gap where prompt injection changes what gets signed after approval. Practical mitigation for irreversible financial agent actions.

entry.title: Rethinking Irregular Time Series Forecasting from the Perspective of Basis Functions

author.name: Rongwen Li, Changjian Chen

entry.summary: This work revisits basis-function representations for irregular time series forecasting, arguing that ignoring timestamp sampling density introduces a non-vanishing asymptotic bias and that predefined bases lack adaptability. It proposes a reformulation that corrects for sampling density and learns more flexible bases. Relevant to healthcare and environmental sensing where observations are sparse and unevenly spaced.

entry.title: ORPA: Online Residual Policy Adaptation for Robot Manipulation Control with Human Feedback

author.name: Muhammad A. Muttaqien, Tomohiro Motoda, Ryo Hanai, Yukiyasu Domae

entry.summary: ORPA adds a lightweight feedback-conditioned module on top of a frozen imitation-learned manipulation policy that predicts residual joint-space corrections in real time, so execution errors and distribution shift can be fixed without dataset aggregation or full retraining. It targets the brittleness of action-chunking transformer policies under small perturbations. Enables immediate human-in-the-loop correction during deployment.

entry.title: Calibrated Trust, Not Sharper Prediction: An Empirical Test of Uncertainty Fusion

author.name: Surya Saka

entry.summary: The paper stress-tests the popular proposal of fusing evidence graphs, Bayesian odds updating, Dempster-Shafer combination, and conformal prediction for legal outcome prediction on 1000 European Court of Human Rights cases, using two existing frontier models as per-fact evidence estimators. It finds the fusion pipeline does not sharpen discrimination but can improve calibrated trust relative to raw model outputs.

entry.title: PIKFNO: An Interpretable Neural Operator Based on Physics Informed Kernel Function

author.name: Yuan Guo, Hanshu Chen, Zhuojia Fu

entry.summary: PIKFNO builds a neural operator whose trunk is constrained by physics-informed kernel functions derived from the governing equations, aligning it with kernel expansions from meshless collocation methods. Two construction strategies are offered, including learning kernels that behave like nonsingular fundamental solutions.

entry.title: SMOPD: Selective Token-Entropy Masking for Dirty-History Multi-Turn On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Chenyang Jiang, Changhan Huang

entry.summary: SMOPD stabilizes multi-turn on-policy self-distillation when a student has already emitted an erroneous intermediate reply, by masking the lowest-entropy 20 percent of token positions out of the distillation loss. It adds no parameters and no inference cost.

entry.title: RouteTS: Frequency-Time Routing for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Gaofeng Lin, Lei Duan

entry.summary: RouteTS routes frequency components of a time series to different computational domains, sending dominant periodic frequencies to a complex-valued linear predictor while leaving transient variation to time-domain processing. The premise is that the best domain is a property of the data rather than of the model.

entry.title: Is Grokking a Loss of Normal Hyperbolicity of the Interpolation Manifold?

author.name: Suvinava Basak

entry.summary: This paper asks whether the sharp generalization jump in grokking corresponds to a loss of normal hyperbolicity of the zero-loss interpolation manifold, that is a bifurcation-like flattening of a normal restoring direction, or merely smooth drift along a uniformly attracting manifold. It proposes an optimizer-level test to distinguish the two.

entry.title: PathFinder: Joint Decompositions of Linked Multimodal Datasets

author.name: Ying-Qiu Zheng, Alex Fung, Stephen M Smith, Rogier B Mars, Saad Jbabdi

entry.summary: PathFinder generalizes joint low-rank matrix decomposition so that datasets need only share dimensions pairwise, linked through a path, rather than all sharing a common mode. This lets researchers co-analyze heterogeneous multimodal datasets, with neuroimaging as the motivating application.

entry.title: Spectral Rank Certification for Foundation Model Adapters

author.name: Mohammed Ahnouch, Lotfi Elaachak

entry.summary: Develops a finite-sample statistical framework for inferring the effective rank of LoRA adapters, separating the nominal rank hyperparameter from calibrated spectral evidence using chi-square divergence bounds, Le Cam theory, and random-matrix BBP thresholds. It applies the toolkit to public foundation-model adapters.

entry.title: FAST-DeepONet: Factor-Augmented Branch Representations for High-Dimensional PDE Inputs in the Small-Sample Regime

author.name: Jiyong Kwon, Bongseok Kim, Guang Lin

entry.summary: FAST-DeepONet stabilizes operator learning when PDE inputs come from thousands of highly correlated sensors but few operator samples, by combining a fixed spectral branch path with a regularized projection of the orthogonal residual. On Navier-Stokes it keeps error roughly constant as the branch input grows from a hundred to several thousand coordinates, where plain DeepONet degrades sharply.

entry.title: Towards Reasonable Molecular Structure Elucidation from Infrared Spectroscopy with Chemical Feedback

author.name: Yusen Tan, Hongyu Zhan, Hai-tao Yu, Changxi Chi, Wenjie Du, Jun Xia

entry.summary: This paper attacks the tendency of IR-spectrum-to-structure models to output chemically inconsistent candidates by adding preference optimization signals that check whether a candidate's implied molecular formula matches the input and whether its theoretical spectrum matches the observation. The result is more chemically reasonable top-ranked structure elucidation.

entry.title: REFLEX: Reflexive Equilibrium Fixed-point Learning for Endogenous eXchanges

author.name: Vignesh Nagarajan, Shriraghav Ashok

entry.summary: REFLEX studies the feedback loop created when bond dealers retrain quoting models on the trades their own quotes attract, instantiating performative prediction stability conditions in a concrete market microstructure model. It asks not just whether a quoting model performs well but whether the market it induces remains stable as the model learns.

entry.title: Coverage-Maximizing Multinomial Subset Routing under Operational Constraints

author.name: Quan Zhou, Yiyan Huang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Multinomial Subset Routing, an online framework where a learner maintains a probability distribution over experts, samples several per round, and is rewarded only by the best performer in the resulting distinct subset, under long-term two-sided operational constraints. This max-style, non-additive reward structure is not covered by standard combinatorial bandits.

entry.title: UniTAC: Universal Task-Aware Compression via Weighted Distortion Measures

author.name: Homa Esfahanizadeh, Matin Mortaheb, Jinfeng Du, Harish Viswanathan

entry.summary: UniTAC trains a single learned image codec that can be retargeted at inference from fully task-agnostic to task-specialized operation, using a per-component importance vector derived from gradient attribution of any downstream model as transmitted side information. This avoids retraining a separate codec per downstream task in bandwidth-constrained robotic and vehicle systems.

entry.title: Learning to Unlearn: Machine Unlearning via Learning the Unlearning Behaviors

author.name: Hang Zhang, Kaifeng Zhang, Yixiao Ma, Weijie Xu, Ye Zhu, Kai Ming Ting

entry.summary: Rather than hand-designing an intricate unlearning function, this paper learns the unlearning behavior itself, motivated by the observation that complex unlearning operators become a computational bottleneck on massive training sets even for small models. The learned approach aims to approximate a retrained-from-scratch model more cheaply.

entry.title: A Vision Transformer for ECG-Based Detection of Left Ventricular Systolic Dysfunction Across Multiple Clinical Sites
